title: Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void
creator: Tim Lebbon
blurb: On Tython, Je'daii Ranger Lanoree Brock has always been the gifted one, strong with the Force while her brother Dalien was not. His training ended in what looked like tragedy years ago, and Lanoree has grieved him ever since. Now the Je'daii Council recalls her for an urgent, unsettling mission: track down and stop the leader of a fanatical cult bent on forcing open a forbidden hyperspace gateway, a scheme that risks tearing the entire star system apart. The twist that shakes her most isn't the threat of catastrophe, but discovering that the dangerous man she has to hunt down is the brother she thought long dead.
trivia: Set roughly 25,793 years before the Battle of Yavin, it's the earliest point yet reached in the Legends timeline, tying into the Dawn of the Jedi comic series.

title: Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith: The Collected Stories
creator: John Jackson Miller
notes: Collects the digital short-story series plus the previously unpublished finale, Pandemonium
blurb: Long before Darth Bane's Rule of Two, or even the Old Republic most fans know, a splinter group of Sith crash-lands on a remote, resource-poor world with no way home. This collection gathers the digital short-story series tracing how that stranded crew claws its way from castaways to a brutal, self-devouring Sith dynasty over the following decades, capped off with a new, previously unpublished finale.
trivia: Originally released as a series of free digital short stories before this collection added a previously unpublished finale, 'Pandemonium.'

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic: Revan
creator: Drew Karpyshyn
notes: Tie-in to the Old Republic MMO, sequel to the Knights of the Old Republic games
blurb: Years after vanishing without a word following his role in ending the Jedi Civil War, Revan is pulled back into action when nightmares of an ancient, unseen enemy start bleeding into his waking life. Convinced the threat is real and closing in on the galaxy, he sets out into unknown space with his old ally Canderous Ordo, willing to risk his own memories and identity to stop it, while his wife Bastila Shan races to track him down before it's too late.
trivia: Includes a preview chapter of Darth Plagueis, and the audiobook is narrated by Marc Thompson.

title: Star Wars: Red Harvest
creator: Joe Schreiber
blurb: A Jedi and a Sith find themselves stranded together after a crash-landing on a remote, ice-locked planet, forced into an uneasy truce just to survive the cold and each other. Joe Schreiber leans into horror-thriller territory here, trading galaxy-spanning stakes for a tighter, bloodier survival story.
trivia: One of a small handful of Star Wars novels to lean into horror, built around a Sith-made virus that raises the dead as lightsaber-wielding zombies.

title: Star Wars: Fatal Alliance
creator: Sean Williams
blurb: A Republic senator's peace mission becomes a target for hijacking, drawing in a mismatched group of bounty hunters, Jedi, and Sith who all have their own reasons for wanting the ship's cargo. Told through multiple POV characters, it widens out the Old Republic era beyond the core game protagonists.
trivia: Tied directly into the launch of the Old Republic MMO, weaving together several playable-class-style characters aboard one besieged ship.

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic: Deceived
creator: Paul S. Kemp
blurb: A Jedi Padawan is dispatched to investigate a Republic military disaster and uncovers a Sith plot reaching into the highest levels of government, forcing him toward choices that will cost him everything he's trained to believe in. Serves as backstory for one of the Old Republic game's most memorable villains.
trivia: Introduces Darth Malgus, who went on to become a major recurring character in the Old Republic MMO itself.

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic: Annihilation
creator: Drew Karpyshyn
blurb: Years after the war between the Republic and the Sith Empire, a former Jedi is pulled back into the fight when an old ally's death exposes a deeper conspiracy threatening the fragile peace. Continues plot threads from the Old Republic game's ongoing story updates.
trivia: Closes out the four-book Old Republic tie-in series that began with Fatal Alliance.

title: Star Wars: Knight Errant
creator: John Jackson Miller
blurb: Stranded alone in Sith space a thousand years before the films, a Jedi with no ship, no backup, and dwindling options has to survive using wits rather than force of arms, all while a ruthless Sith lord tightens his grip on the system around her.
trivia: Follows a single Jedi stranded deep in Sith-held space roughly 1,032 years before the Battle of Yavin, waging a one-woman campaign rather than joining a wider task force.

title: Star Wars: Darth Bane: Path of Destruction
creator: Drew Karpyshyn
blurb: The first novel to chart the making of a Sith Lord: a slave turned soldier turned outcast whose fury and ambition eventually curdle into the philosophy that eliminates all Sith but two. Origin story for Darth Bane and the Rule of Two that shapes everything that follows in Sith history.
trivia: Karpyshyn's first hardcover novel, written after his work as lead writer on the Knights of the Old Republic video game led to the opportunity.

title: Star Wars: Darth Bane: Rule of Two
creator: Drew Karpyshyn
blurb: Having destroyed his own Sith brotherhood to enforce a new, leaner doctrine, Darth Bane must train a secret apprentice capable of eventually replacing him — without that apprentice deciding to speed up the timeline. The book that cements the master-and-apprentice structure later Sith Lords like Sidious and Vader would follow.
trivia: Commissioned as a replacement after Del Rey's originally planned Darth Plagueis novel was shelved around the same time.

title: Star Wars: Droidography
creator: Marc Sumerak (writer), Joel Hustak, Arianna Sabella & Massimo Travaglini (art)
notes: Interactive kids' reference book with lift-the-flaps and textured pages; published by HarperFestival
blurb: An illustrated, interactive guide to the droids of the Star Wars galaxy, narrated in-character by Roger, a retired battle droid from LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures. It profiles everything from classics like C-3PO and R2-D2 to newer favorites like BB-8, mixing in lift-the-flap pages and tactile textures aimed at younger fans.
trivia: Narrated in-character by Roger, a battle droid who also appears in LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures.

title: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron
creator: Factor 5 (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL version, published in Europe by Nintendo; US release was December 1998
blurb: An arcade-style space combat game putting you in the cockpit of Luke Skywalker, newly placed in command of Rogue Squadron in the months after the Battle of Yavin. Across sixteen missions against the Empire, flying X-wings, Y-wings, snowspeeders and more, it was one of the first Nintendo 64 titles built around the console's Expansion Pak for higher-resolution visuals, and became the first entry in what grew into the Rogue Squadron trilogy.
rating: Metacritic user score 8.5/10; frequently ranked among the best N64 games ever made
trivia: Grew out of a single flight-combat level in 1996's Shadows of the Empire, which LucasArts and Factor 5 expanded into a full game.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Defy the Storm
creator: Justina Ireland & Tessa Gratton
notes: Book 7 of the YA line, Phase III, picks up right after The Eye of Darkness
rating: Goodreads ~4.1/5; Kirkus Reviews called it worth the wait
trivia: The fourth book Ireland and Gratton have co-written together, following a writing partnership that started after they became friends at a convention in 2013.
blurb: A year after the Nihil destroyed the space station Starlight Beacon, the Republic is still reeling, and the Nihil have walled off a chunk of space behind a barrier called the Stormwall. Jedi Knight Vernestra Rwoh, believing her Padawan died in the attack, has retreated to try to heal — until the fallout from the disaster pulls her and other familiar High Republic faces back into the fight against the Nihil's Occlusion Zone.

title: Star Wars: Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil
creator: Drew Karpyshyn
notes: Final book of the Darth Bane trilogy
trivia: Ends with Bane's apprentice Zannah poised to betray and replace him, cementing the Rule of Two that governs every Sith Lord who follows, right up to Darth Sidious and Darth Vader a thousand years later.
blurb: Decades after founding the Rule of Two, an aging Darth Bane searches for a way to cheat death and pass his knowledge on intact, while his apprentice Zannah quietly grows powerful enough to wonder whether her master's rule about there always being exactly two Sith really includes room for both of them much longer.

title: Star Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter
creator: Michael Reaves
notes: Some editions bundle the bonus ebook story "Darth Maul: Saboteur" by James Luceno
trivia: Set in Coruscant's Crimson Corridor just days before The Phantom Menace, giving Darth Maul his first extended solo spotlight in print.
blurb: Darth Sidious dispatches his fearsome apprentice to hunt down a Neimoidian defector who's about to sell secrets of the coming Naboo blockade. That trail leads Darth Maul into Coruscant's seedy underworld and into conflict with information broker Lorn Pavan and his droid partner I-5, setting up the opening moves that lead straight into The Phantom Menace.

title: Star Wars: Cloak of Deception
creator: James Luceno
trivia: Explains why the Trade Federation held a seat in the Galactic Senate at all, filling in political groundwork that The Phantom Menace assumes viewers already understand.
blurb: In the tense run-up to The Phantom Menace, Supreme Chancellor Valorum is fighting to hold together a corrupt Senate and a galaxy sliding toward a trade war, while a terrorist group called the Nebula Front threatens to assassinate him at a crucial trade summit. Qui-Gon Jinn and his Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi are assigned to the case, unaware they're also witnessing the opening moves of Darth Sidious's long game against the Republic.

title: Star Wars: Darth Plagueis
creator: James Luceno
trivia: Directly expands the "Tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise" story Palpatine tells Anakin in Revenge of the Sith, spelling out exactly how Plagueis could supposedly cheat death and how his apprentice ultimately betrayed him.
blurb: A Muun Sith Lord obsessed with using the dark side to cheat death takes on a promising young Naboo politician named Palpatine as his apprentice, grooming him across decades of political manipulation, banking-clan intrigue, and Sith philosophy. Their partnership builds patiently toward the betrayal every Star Wars fan already half-knows is coming from Palpatine's own words in Revenge of the Sith.

title: Star Wars: Rogue Planet
creator: Greg Bear
notes: The first adult prequel-era novel published after The Phantom Menace
trivia: Reached #9 on the New York Times bestseller list in 2000, despite becoming one of the more divisive Legends novels among fans in later years.
blurb: A young Anakin Skywalker and his new master Obi-Wan Kenobi travel to a mysterious living planet called Zonama Sekot, whose bio-organic technology grows living starships. As Anakin is drawn toward the planet's strange power, the pair uncover a plot that ties back to the Empire's future interest in the planet's unique shipbuilding secrets.

title: Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace
creator: Terry Brooks
notes: Based on the screenplay and story by George Lucas
trivia: Fantasy novelist Terry Brooks was hand-picked by George Lucas himself to write the novelization, and included an introduction describing what Star Wars meant to him as a storyteller.
blurb: The official novelization of the first prequel film, following Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn and his Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi as a trade dispute over Naboo draws them into discovering a young slave boy named Anakin Skywalker, believed to be the Chosen One prophesied to bring balance to the Force, while a mysterious Sith apprentice re-emerges after a thousand years in hiding.

title: Star Wars: Maul: Lockdown
creator: Joe Schreiber
notes: A direct follow-up to Darth Plagueis
trivia: Written by the same author as Red Harvest and Death Troopers, carrying over their signature gorier, horror-tinged tone into a prequel-era story for the first time.
blurb: Sent undercover into Cog Hive Seven, a brutal space prison where inmates are forced into gladiatorial combat for a gambling underworld, Darth Maul infiltrates the facility on a secret mission for his masters Darth Sidious and Darth Plagueis: track down a weapons dealer holding something that could hand the Sith the key to conquering the galaxy.

title: Star Wars: The Cestus Deception
creator: Steven Barnes
notes: A Clone Wars Novel
trivia: Introduces the "JK" bio-droids — techno-organic battle droids sensitive enough to the Force to predict a Jedi's next move, one of the more unusual weapons concepts in Legends.
blurb: Obi-Wan Kenobi and fellow Jedi Kit Fisto are sent to the industrial world of Ord Cestus, officially to negotiate, unofficially to sabotage a new line of Force-sensitive battle droids designed specifically to kill Jedi before the Separatists can get their hands on them.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Trial
creator: David Sherman & Dan Cragg
notes: A Clone Wars Novel
trivia: Written by two military-fiction authors best known for the Starfist series, bringing a grittier ground-combat feel to Anakin Skywalker's first command as a general.
blurb: Newly knighted and given his first command, Anakin Skywalker must lead a company of clone troopers against overwhelming odds on a besieged world, forcing him to prove himself as a battlefield commander while a Jedi test of a different kind quietly plays out around him.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando: Hard Contact
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Official tie-in to the Republic Commando video game; first of the series
trivia: Karen Traviss's clone commandos here are treated as fully realized individuals with their own names and personalities, a tone shift that became one of the most influential takes on clone troopers in Legends.
blurb: Omega Squad, a four-man team of elite clone commandos, is dropped onto the planet Qiilura to destroy a Separatist bioweapons lab. When their mission goes wrong and they're left without backup, squad leader Niner and his surviving brothers have to keep each other alive alongside a reluctant Jedi Padawan while cut off deep in enemy territory.

title: Star Wars: Shatterpoint
creator: Matthew Stover
notes: Includes a new prologue by George Lucas
trivia: Frequently cited by fans as one of the single best-written Legends novels, exploring Mace Windu's character and his morally murky homeworld far more deeply than the films ever did.
blurb: Mace Windu returns to his long-abandoned homeworld of Haruun Kal to track down a former Padawan who has gone dangerously off the rails leading a guerrilla war, forcing Mace to confront how thin the line really is between a Jedi's discipline and the brutal choices war demands of him.

title: Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones
creator: R.A. Salvatore
notes: Based upon the story by George Lucas and the screenplay by George Lucas and Jonathan Hales
trivia: Fantasy author R.A. Salvatore, best known for the Forgotten Realms Drizzt Do'Urden novels, was chosen to novelize a film built almost entirely around political intrigue and a forbidden romance.
blurb: The official novelization of the second prequel film, as Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi investigate an assassination attempt on Senator Padmé Amidala that unravels into the discovery of a secret clone army and the first shots of the Clone Wars, while Anakin's feelings for Padmé and his growing impatience with the Jedi Order both pull him toward the path he'll ultimately take.

title: Star Wars: The Approaching Storm
creator: Alan Dean Foster
notes: Marketed as a direct prologue to Attack of the Clones
trivia: Alan Dean Foster ghostwrote the original 1977 Star Wars novelization credited to George Lucas, making him one of the very first authors to ever write in the Star Wars universe, decades before this book.
blurb: As tensions rise between the Republic and a group of systems threatening to secede, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, and Yoda are sent to mediate a dispute that's really a Separatist plot in disguise, setting the stage directly for the political collapse depicted in Attack of the Clones.

title: Star Wars: Outbound Flight
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Expands on an expedition first referenced in Zahn's earlier Thrawn novels
trivia: Fleshes out an ambitious Jedi-led expedition to explore beyond the galaxy that Zahn had only ever mentioned in passing in his earlier Thrawn Trilogy, finally showing how it met its fate.
blurb: Jedi Master Jorus C'baoth leads an ambitious expedition of six converted Dreadnaught cruisers, Outbound Flight, on a mission to explore beyond the galaxy's edge — unaware that a rising Chiss military officer named Thrawn is about to determine whether that mission survives contact with his people at all.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando: True Colours
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 3 of the Republic Commando series; includes bonus short story "Odds"
trivia: Digs into questions the games never touched — whether clones can defect, what rights they're owed, and what happens to soldiers grown to age too fast once the war ends.
blurb: As the Clone Wars grind on, Sergeant Kal Skirata intensifies his search for a way to reverse the accelerated aging built into his adopted clone soldiers, racing against Palpatine's own agents who are hunting the same Kaminoan scientist for very different reasons.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando: Triple Zero
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 2 of the Republic Commando series
trivia: Widely considered by fans to be the strongest entry in the Republic Commando series, deepening the moral questions around cloned soldiers that Hard Contact introduced.
blurb: Omega Squad and rival unit Delta Squad are sent to Coruscant to root out a Separatist terror cell, reuniting Omega with the Jedi Padawan Etain Tur-Mukan and clone trainer Kal Skirata as the war's human cost starts weighing more heavily on everyone involved.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Gambit: Siege
creator: Karen Miller
notes: Book 2 of the Clone Wars Gambit duology
trivia: Closes out a duology that leans heavily on Anakin and Obi-Wan's banter-driven dynamic, building directly on plot threads from Miller's own Wild Space.
blurb: Picking up where Stealth left off, Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi are drawn deeper into a Separatist plot that threatens to expose Republic secrets, forcing them into a siege situation where trust and improvisation matter as much as lightsabers.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Gambit: Stealth
creator: Karen Miller
notes: Book 1 of the Clone Wars Gambit duology
trivia: A direct sequel to Miller's own Wild Space, continuing plot threads that novel had left open rather than standing fully alone.
blurb: Sent undercover on a covert mission that tests both his patience and his growing unease with the war, Obi-Wan Kenobi partners again with Anakin Skywalker to root out a threat that could hand the Separatists a critical advantage if it isn't stopped quietly.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: No Prisoners
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Tie-in to the animated Clone Wars TV series
trivia: One of the last pieces of Star Wars fiction Karen Traviss wrote before her public departure from the franchise over creative disagreements regarding clone continuity.
blurb: Anakin Skywalker, Ahsoka Tano, and a squad of clone troopers must retake a Separatist prison ship holding vital Republic intelligence, forcing Ahsoka to confront just how brutal a war fought with expendable soldiers really is.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Wild Space
creator: Karen Miller
notes: Tie-in to the animated Clone Wars TV series
trivia: Sets up the plot thread that the Clone Wars Gambit duology later continues directly.
blurb: When a Jedi convoy vanishes without a trace in a remote, uncharted region of space, Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi are sent to investigate, uncovering a Separatist scheme that could threaten the Republic's war effort far from any battlefield anyone's watching.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Based on the animated theatrical film from Lucasfilm Animation
trivia: Novelizes the theatrical film that served as a feature-length pilot for the animated Clone Wars series, introducing Ahsoka Tano to the wider Star Wars story for the first time.
blurb: The official novelization of the 2008 animated film, introducing Anakin Skywalker's new Padawan Ahsoka Tano as the pair are sent to rescue Jabba the Hutt's kidnapped son, a mission the Jedi hope will win the Hutts' favor for the Republic's war effort against the Separatists.

title: Star Wars: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader
creator: James Luceno
notes: Third book of the loose Dark Lord trilogy, following Labyrinth of Evil and the Episode III novelization
trivia: Reviewers commonly note it pairs well with John Jackson Miller's Kenobi, since its final chapter leads almost directly into where that novel begins.
blurb: In the immediate aftermath of Order 66 and the fall of the Jedi, the newly christened Darth Vader is sent by his master on a series of missions meant to harden him into his new role, while scattered Jedi survivors of the purge try to regroup and understand what's just happened to their Order.

title: Star Wars: Kenobi
creator: John Jackson Miller
trivia: Deliberately borrows structure and tone from Western films, casting Tatooine's moisture farmers and settlers like a frontier town Obi-Wan reluctantly gets drawn into protecting.
blurb: Newly arrived on Tatooine to watch over the infant Luke Skywalker from a distance, Obi-Wan Kenobi tries to keep to himself as a hermit — until a range war between moisture farmers and Tusken Raiders pulls him back into the role of protector he's supposed to be leaving behind.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando: Order 66
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 4 of the Republic Commando series
trivia: One of the highest-rated books in the entire Republic Commando/Imperial Commando series on Goodreads, closing out the Clone Wars-era arc for Omega and Delta Squad.
blurb: As Order 66 sweeps the galaxy and clone troopers are forced to turn on the Jedi they've fought alongside for years, the commandos of Omega and Delta Squad face an impossible choice between the chip in their heads and the loyalties they've actually built.

title: Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith
creator: Matthew Stover
notes: Based on the story and screenplay by George Lucas
trivia: Widely regarded by fans as the best film novelization in all of Star Wars, frequently topping "best Star Wars books" lists ahead of most original fiction.
blurb: The official novelization of the final prequel film, following Anakin Skywalker's descent into Darth Vader as Palpatine's manipulations, the Jedi Council's mistrust, and Anakin's own fear of loss combine to destroy the Jedi Order and give birth to the Galactic Empire.

title: Star Wars: Labyrinth of Evil
creator: James Luceno
notes: First book of the loose Dark Lord trilogy, marketed as a direct lead-in to Revenge of the Sith
trivia: Ends mere hours before Revenge of the Sith begins, deliberately timed to be read immediately before the film's opening scene.
blurb: Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker race against time to stop a Separatist plot to assassinate Chancellor Palpatine, uncovering a trail that leads disturbingly close to the shadowy Sith Lord secretly pulling the strings of the entire war.

title: Star Wars: Yoda: Dark Rendezvous
creator: Sean Stewart
notes: A Clone Wars Novel
trivia: One of the few Legends novels to put Yoda front and center as the viewpoint character rather than a supporting figure.
blurb: When Count Dooku sends word that he wants to discuss a private matter, Yoda accepts the invitation himself, suspecting a trap but hoping there's still a chance to reach his former apprentice's grand-apprentice before the war claims anyone else close to him.

title: Star Wars: MedStar II: Jedi Healer
creator: Michael Reaves & Steve Perry
notes: A Clone Wars Novel, second half of the MedStar duology
trivia: Continues the field-hospital perspective on the Clone Wars that Battle Surgeons introduced, keeping the war grounded in medics and wounded rather than generals and lightsabers.
blurb: The overworked medical staff of the mobile field hospital MedStar Two keep treating a stream of wounded clones and Jedi even as the fighting on Drongar grinds on, while personal entanglements among the surgeons complicate lives already stretched thin by war.

title: Star Wars: MedStar I: Battle Surgeons
creator: Michael Reaves & Steve Perry
notes: A Clone Wars Novel, first half of the MedStar duology
trivia: Focuses on the unglamorous side of the Clone Wars — field medicine — rather than Jedi heroics, following surgeons instead of soldiers.
blurb: On the fog-choked jungle world of Drongar, a mismatched team of Republic and Jedi field surgeons fights to keep wounded clones alive faster than the war can produce new casualties, all while a valuable local resource makes the planet a target worth fighting over in its own right.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Twilight
creator: Michael Reaves
notes: Coruscant Nights I
trivia: Was actually finished and edited back in 2007 but held back a year so the whole planned trilogy could release together, alongside Reaves' own Death Star novel.
blurb: One of the few Jedi to survive Order 66, Jax Pavan hides in plain sight as a private investigator in Coruscant's underworld, until the death of his old Master pulls him back into a mission he can't walk away from, with Darth Vader himself closing in.

title: Star Wars: Imperial Commando: 501st
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Direct continuation of the Republic Commando series under its new title
trivia: Was intended as the first of further Imperial Commando sequels that never materialized after Karen Traviss's public split from the Star Wars franchise.
blurb: Newly rebranded as Imperial stormtroopers after Order 66, the clone commandos of the old Republic forces have to reconcile who they were fighting for with who they're now serving, as some within their ranks start quietly working against the Empire they've been folded into.

title: Star Wars: Street of Shadows
creator: Michael Reaves
notes: Coruscant Nights II
trivia: Leans into a noir murder-mystery structure more heavily than Jedi Twilight, chasing a killer with only a loose connection to the series' larger Vader-hunting-Jax plot.
blurb: Still adjusting to life on the run with his droid companion I-5 and reporter Den Dhur, Jax Pavan gets pulled into investigating the murder of a celebrated artist, a case that turns out to be more tangled — and more personal — than it first appears.

title: Star Wars: Patterns of Force
creator: Michael Reaves
notes: Coruscant Nights III
trivia: The last Coruscant Nights book Michael Reaves wrote solo before his co-authored finale, The Last Jedi, closed out the series.
blurb: As Jax Pavan edges closer to unlocking secrets about his late father's past, the net Darth Vader has been quietly tightening around him finally starts to close, forcing a confrontation Jax has been dreading since Order 66.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
creator: Michael Reaves & Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff
notes: Coruscant Nights IV, co-written after Reaves brought in Bohnhoff to finish the series
trivia: Not to be confused with the 2017 sequel-trilogy film of the same name — this book predates that title by four years.
blurb: Closing out the Coruscant Nights series, Jax Pavan and his allies finally start building the connections and resistance networks on Coruscant that will one day feed into the wider Rebel Alliance, even as the Jedi Order they came from continues to fade further into memory.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes
creator: LucasArts Singapore
notes: The DS version follows a different, prequel storyline to the other platform versions, developed separately by LucasArts Singapore rather than Krome Studios
trivia: Uniquely among the multi-platform release, the DS version tells its own separate story that serves as a prequel to the version released on other consoles, rather than sharing the same plot.
blurb: A tie-in to the animated Clone Wars TV series, set between the show's first and second seasons. Players fight through droid armies as Jedi and clone troopers, tracking the bounty hunter Cad Bane and a Skakoan scientist building a new superweapon for the Separatists — though the DS version tells its own distinct story rather than mirroring the console editions.

title: Monopoly: Star Wars The Mandalorian Edition
creator: Hasbro Gaming
notes: Item F4257, inspired by Season 2 of The Mandalorian
rating: No consolidated public rating found — has a BoardGameGeek page but no aggregate score at last check; retailer reviews anecdotally 4.5–4.7/5
trivia: Lets players take on the roles of The Mandalorian, Bo-Katan Kryze, Ahsoka Tano, or Boba Fett, with Grogu's token granting a bonus power to whoever holds it, and losing him to an Imperial enemy token ending the game instantly for everyone.
blurb: A Star Wars reskin of classic Monopoly themed around The Mandalorian's second season, replacing properties with in-universe hideouts and Monopoly money with Imperial credits. Landing on Grogu's space lets a player claim his token and combine his power with their own character's special ability, while Stormtrooper, Dark Trooper, and Moff Gideon enemy tokens can trigger battles — and losing Grogu to one ends the game for everyone.

title: Star Wars: The Han Solo Trilogy: The Paradise Snare
creator: A.C. Crispin
trivia: Opens the Han Solo Trilogy, a prequel series written specifically to answer where Han's cynicism and skill actually came from, years before A.C. Crispin was asked to write it.
blurb: Before he's the galaxy's best-known smuggler, a young Han Solo is a naive cadet whose loyalty to a girl named Bria Tharen leads him into the clutches of the Ylesian slavers — and the first steps of the hard education that will make him who he becomes.

title: Star Wars: Classic: The Lando Calrissian Adventures
creator: L. Neil Smith
trivia: Originally published as three separate short novels in 1983; this omnibus edition bundles all three under one cover as 'classic value' three-for-one pricing.
blurb: Long before Cloud City, a much younger, much less certain Lando Calrissian cons his way across the galaxy with his sardonic droid partner Vuffi Raa, chasing legendary artifacts and staying one skip ahead of the people he's wronged.

title: Star Wars: The Han Solo Trilogy: The Hutt Gambit
creator: A.C. Crispin
trivia: The middle volume of the Han Solo Trilogy, it's the book that finally explains how Han came to own the Falcon in the first place — via a sabacc game with Lando, referenced constantly in later stories.
blurb: Having washed out of the Imperial Navy, Han falls in with Lando Calrissian and the galaxy's smuggling underworld, forging the uneasy Hutt-backed alliances that will eventually put him in the captain's chair of the Millennium Falcon.

title: Star Wars: The Han Solo Adventures
creator: Brian Daley
trivia: Brian Daley's original trilogy (1979–1980) predates almost all other Star Wars expanded fiction, making this one of the very first attempts to build out Han's backstory before the films had even finished their initial run.
blurb: Some years before A New Hope, Han and Chewbacca are already running from bounty hunters, corrupt bureaucrats, and their own bad luck, dragged into one galaxy-spanning scheme after another with nothing but wit and a fast ship to save them.

title: Star Wars: Death Troopers
creator: Joe Schreiber
trivia: A deliberate genre mashup pitched as 'Star Wars meets zombie horror,' it became one of the more divisive Legends novels for pushing the franchise's tone into outright body horror.
blurb: Two young criminals are swept up with a squad of stormtroopers aboard a seemingly abandoned Imperial prison ship — only to discover the vessel isn't empty, and whatever killed its crew is still very much awake.

title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed
creator: Sean Williams
trivia: Written concurrently with the video game of the same name and released to tie into it, the novel fills in additional character beats and internal monologue the game's cutscenes didn't have room for.
blurb: Darth Vader's secret enforcer, known only as Starkiller, is sent to hunt down the last remnants of the Jedi Order — until a mission gone wrong forces him to question the master he's devoted his entire life to serving.

title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II
creator: Sean Williams
trivia: Continues directly from the first Force Unleashed video game tie-in, mirroring the sequel game's central mystery about cloning and identity.
blurb: Haunted by fragmented memories and unsure if he's the real Starkiller or just another clone, the game's protagonist sets out to find Juno Eclipse and the truth about what the Empire actually did to him.

title: Star Wars: Shadow Games
creator: Michael Reaves & Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff
trivia: Centers on Dash Rendar, the smuggler introduced in the Shadows of the Empire multimedia project, rather than Han Solo or Lando as the cover art might suggest — written by the same Michael Reaves behind the Coruscant Nights trilogy, alongside co-author Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff.
blurb: Stranded on Tatooine with a broken hyperdrive, small-time smuggler Dash Rendar takes a bodyguard job protecting a famous holostar from an obsessive fan — only to find the real threat runs far deeper than a stalker, and pulls him into a conspiracy he never signed up for.

title: Star Wars: The Han Solo Trilogy: Rebel Dawn
creator: A.C. Crispin
trivia: Closes out the Han Solo Trilogy and is written to dovetail directly into the opening scenes of A New Hope, tying up every dangling thread A.C. Crispin set up across the first two books.
blurb: As the fledgling Rebellion gathers strength, Han's growing conscience collides with his smuggler instincts, culminating in the sabacc game that costs him the Falcon to Lando and the choice that finally sets him on the path to Tatooine.

title: Star Wars: Death Star
creator: Michael Reaves & Steve Perry
trivia: Notable for humanizing several Imperial personnel, including showing some crew members growing uneasy with the station's purpose well before its destruction at Yavin.
blurb: Told from the perspective of several Imperial officers and technicians serving aboard the first Death Star, the novel traces the battle station's construction and first mission through the eyes of the people who built and crewed the ultimate weapon.

title: Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope
creator: George Lucas
trivia: Credited to George Lucas but largely ghostwritten by Alan Dean Foster, it was published in late 1976, months before the film itself premiered, meaning many readers experienced this story before ever seeing it on screen.
blurb: The novelization of the film that started it all: a farm boy on a desert planet gets pulled into a rebellion, a rescue, and a fight against an empire — the story everything else in this collection eventually built itself around.

title: Star Wars: Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina
creator: ed. Kevin J. Anderson
trivia: Part of a broader trend of anthology short-story collections in the 1990s expanded universe, giving minor background characters from the films their own dedicated narratives for the first time.
blurb: Sixteen different authors each take on a patron of the galaxy's most notorious watering hole, filling in the backstories of the smugglers, bounty hunters, and background aliens glimpsed for only a few seconds in the cantina scene.

title: Star Wars: Scoundrels
creator: Timothy Zahn
trivia: Structured explicitly as a heist story in the vein of Ocean's Eleven, with each chapter introducing a new specialist recruited for their one specific skill.
blurb: Fresh off Yavin, Han Solo assembles a crew of specialists for one last heist against Black Sun's stronghold — a job that's part con, part vendetta, and entirely likely to get everyone involved killed.

title: Star Wars: Choices of One
creator: Timothy Zahn
trivia: Notable as one of the earliest appearances of Grand Admiral Thrawn's career, showing him well before he rises to the rank most fans know him by.
blurb: Shortly after the destruction of the first Death Star, Mara Jade and a fledgling Rebel fleet cross paths with a mysterious tactician whose cool, calculating brilliance will later make him one of the galaxy's most feared strategists.

title: Star Wars: Allegiance
creator: Timothy Zahn
trivia: One of the few Legends novels to seriously explore stormtroopers as individuals with doubts, rather than anonymous Imperial muscle.
blurb: Between A New Hope and The Empire Strikes Back, a handful of stormtroopers begin questioning the orders they're given, while Mara Jade is pulled into a mission that will test where her loyalties truly lie.

title: Star Wars: Honor Among Thieves
creator: James S.A. Corey
trivia: Part of the Empire and Rebellion trilogy, a set of three standalone novels each focusing on a different core trio member, written by three different acclaimed genre authors.
blurb: Han Solo is paired with an undercover Rebel operative on a mission into the criminal underworld, where the job quickly becomes less about following orders and more about surviving each other's very different methods.

title: Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine
creator: Voronica Whitney-Robinson & Haden Blackman
trivia: Tied directly to the MMO Star Wars Galaxies, its plot and setting were designed to connect to in-game content and events available to players at the time of release.
blurb: Imperial forces excavate the ruins of an old Jedi enclave on Dantooine in search of ancient secrets, while a small band of resistance fighters races to stop them from getting what they're looking for.

title: Star Wars: Splinter of the Mind's Eye
creator: Alan Dean Foster
trivia: Published in 1978, it's the very first Star Wars expanded universe novel ever released, written before The Empire Strikes Back had even revealed Luke and Leia were siblings — a fact that required some notable retroactive workarounds.
blurb: Stranded on the swampy planet Mimban after their ship goes down, Luke and Leia stumble onto the legendary Kaiburr crystal — and a confrontation with Darth Vader that pushes Luke's fledgling command of the Force further than he's ever gone.

title: Star Wars: Razor's Edge
creator: Martha Wells
trivia: Also part of the Empire and Rebellion trilogy, this is the volume centered on Leia, balancing her diplomatic instincts against the harder edges she's forced to develop as the war drags on.
blurb: Sent to negotiate with a band of pirates the Rebellion desperately needs as allies, Leia finds herself trapped between Imperial pursuit and her own crew's doubts about whether she's the right person for a job this dangerous.

title: The Art of Star Wars: Andor — The Complete Series
creator: Phil Szostak
notes: Foreword by Tony Gilroy, afterword by Dan Gilroy
rating: Too new for an established rating yet (released March 2026)
trivia: Written by Phil Szostak, the same author behind The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and the sequel-trilogy art books, covering the full concept art and design process across both seasons of Andor.
blurb: A comprehensive behind-the-scenes look at both seasons of Andor, gathering concept art, ship and vehicle designs, character studies, storyboards, and interviews with showrunner Tony Gilroy and the Lucasfilm art department that shaped the show's grounded, lived-in vision of the early Rebellion.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Light of the Jedi
creator: Charles Soule
notes: Phase I adult novel; launch title of the High Republic initiative
blurb: Two centuries before the Skywalker saga, the Republic is at its idealistic height and the Jedi are its shining guardians. When a freighter disaster in hyperspace sends debris hurtling toward an inhabited star system at relativistic speed, hundreds of Jedi mount an impossible rescue — and uncover the Nihil, marauders whose paths through hyperspace shouldn't exist. Chancellor Soh's dream of a connected galaxy collides with a storm that's only beginning.
trivia: Launch novel of Project Luminous, the multi-author High Republic publishing initiative announced in 2020 — its opening 'Great Disaster' unfolds in near real-time across dozens of viewpoints.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: A Test of Courage
creator: Justina Ireland
notes: Phase I middle-grade novel
blurb: Newly knighted at sixteen, Vernestra Rwoh is escorting a Padawan, an inventor's son and an ambassador's daughter aboard a luxury cruiser when sabotage tears the ship apart. Marooned on a toxic jungle moon, the young survivors must work together to stay alive — while grief and fear test how much of a Jedi Vernestra really is.
trivia: The first middle-grade entry of the initiative; Vernestra Rwoh, introduced here as a 16-year-old prodigy, went on to appear across the whole publishing line and in live action in The Acolyte.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Into the Dark
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Phase I YA novel
blurb: Padawan Reath Silas would rather be in the Archives than on the frontier, but he's shipped out anyway — just as the Great Disaster closes the hyperlanes. Stranded at an abandoned space station with a crew of misfit spacers, Reath and several Jedi discover something ancient and hungry sealed inside it, and long-buried Sith secrets stir.
trivia: Introduces fan-favourite Geode, a Vintian navigator who is, to all appearances, simply a rock — and Wayseeker Jedi Orla Jareni, who expanded what being a Jedi can mean.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: The Rising Storm
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Phase I adult novel
blurb: Chancellor Soh's Republic Fair on Valo is meant to showcase everything the Republic stands for. Marchion Ro intends to make it a lesson in how fragile that dream is. As the Nihil descend, Stellan Gios, Bell Zettifar and Elzar Mann each face the storm in their own way — and not everyone comes out whole.
trivia: Scott plotted the Republic Fair chapters like a disaster movie and has said he wrote the Marchion Ro scenes to horror soundtracks.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Race to Crashpoint Tower
creator: Daniel José Older
notes: Phase I middle-grade novel
blurb: While the Republic Fair burns, Padawan Ram Jomaram — happiest elbow-deep in an engine — discovers the Nihil have knocked out Valo's communications from a hidden mountain outpost. With a squad of droids and a borrowed starfighter, the galaxy's most reluctant hero races to get a warning out.
trivia: Runs in parallel with The Rising Storm — the two books depict the same attack on Valo from different vantage points.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Out of the Shadows
creator: Justina Ireland
notes: Phase I YA novel
blurb: Haulage pilot Sylvestri Yarrow just wants to keep her late mother's ship flying, but a Nihil ambush drags her into a feud between two powerful hyperspace-prospecting dynasties. With Jedi Vernestra Rwoh and Imri Cantaros in tow, she follows the money — and finds a hidden anomaly in deep space that changes everything.
trivia: Sylvestri Yarrow's storyline threads the YA books into the adult novels' Nihil conspiracy via the Graf and San Tekka hyperspace-prospecting families.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Tempest Runner
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Full-cast audio drama script book
blurb: Lourna Dee — Nihil Tempest Runner, presumed dead by the Jedi — is captured under a false name and sentenced to a Republic prison ship. Told through the script of the audio drama, this is her story: survival, manipulation and mutiny below decks, and the long trail of wreckage that made her.
trivia: A full-cast audio drama script published as a book — sound cues and stage directions printed as written, a first for the High Republic line.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Mission to Disaster
creator: Justina Ireland
notes: Phase I middle-grade novel
blurb: When the Nihil raid Port Haileap and kidnap young inventor Avon Starros, Padawan Imri Cantaros and Jedi Vernestra Rwoh mount a rescue. Avon, meanwhile, refuses to wait — studying her captors' Path engines from the inside, she looks for a way to break the Nihil's greatest advantage.
trivia: Avon Starros's arc here sets up her family's legacy — the Starros name recurs across Star Wars publishing eras.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: The Fallen Star
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Phase I adult novel
blurb: Starlight Beacon, the Republic's great lighthouse on the frontier, has weathered every storm the Nihil could raise. So Marchion Ro sends something worse: the Nameless, creatures that unmake a Jedi's connection to the Force. As the station falls, Stellan, Elzar and Bell must decide who they are when the light goes out.
trivia: The fall of Starlight Beacon was planned as Phase I's midpoint gut-punch from the initiative's earliest outlines; Gray asked to write the 'space-station disaster' book.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Midnight Horizon
creator: Daniel José Older
notes: Phase I YA novel
blurb: Far from the frontier, Jedi Cohmac Vitus and Reath Silas chase a Nihil signal to gleaming Corellia, teaming up with Padawan Ram Jomaram and streetwise bodyguard Crash. As they dig in, word arrives of catastrophe at Starlight — and the mission becomes about holding on to hope.
trivia: Set concurrently with The Fallen Star, on Corellia — featuring Crash's teenage bodyguard agency and a tour of Coronet City's underworld.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Path of Deceit
creator: Tessa Gratton & Justina Ireland
notes: Phase II YA novel
blurb: A hundred and fifty years before the Nihil, on the pastoral world of Dalna, the Path of the Open Hand preaches that the Force must be free — and no one, especially not the Jedi, should use it. When young believer Marda Ro meets Jedi investigating a stolen chalice, faith, love and fanaticism begin their long collision course.
trivia: Phase II's opening novel jumps 150 years before Phase I; the Path of the Open Hand introduced here is the seed of the Nihil's Nameless weapons.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Cataclysm
creator: Lydia Kang
notes: Phase II adult novel
blurb: The cold war between Eiram and E'ronoh is about to reignite, and the Path of the Open Hand is fanning the flames toward catastrophe on Dalna. Jedi Gella Nattai and disgraced heir Axel Greylark return to untangle the conspiracy — as the Path's 'Great Leveler' is unleashed and the Jedi learn what fear of the Force can do.
trivia: Kang's medical background shows in the Battle of Dalna's triage scenes; the book resolves Convergence's cliffhangers and echoes into Phase III.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Path of Vengeance
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Phase II YA novel
blurb: After Dalna burns, cousins Marda and Yana Ro pull the shattered Path of the Open Hand in opposite directions — Marda toward zealotry with the Leveler at her side, Yana toward escape. Their choices forge a creed, a weapon and a name that will haunt the Jedi for generations.
trivia: Marda Ro's transformation here directly explains the Ro family legacy — Marchion Ro is her inheritor, name and weapon alike.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Quest for Planet X
creator: Tessa Gratton
notes: Phase II middle-grade novel
blurb: Treasure hunter Dass Leffbruk and Force-sensitive stowaway Sky Graf strike out for the legendary Planet X, chasing a prize hidden in uncharted space. Between rival prospectors, a hostile wilderness and family secrets, the hunt becomes a test of what — and who — is worth the risk.
trivia: The Graf family's hunt for the fabled 'Planet X' ties the middle-grade line into the hyperspace-prospecting plot of Phase II's adult novels.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Quest for the Hidden City
creator: George Mann
notes: Phase II middle-grade novel
blurb: On drought-stricken Aubadas, Dass Leffbruk and his father hunt for water routes while young Jedi and local Katikoot allies uncover a hidden city beneath the surface — and with it, a discovery that could save or doom the region. A frontier adventure about courage in small packages.
trivia: Introduces the Leffbruk kids whose Phase II adventures continue in Quest for Planet X; set amid the Eiram–E'ronoh forever war.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Tales of Light and Life
creator: Various (anthology)
notes: Anthology bridging Phases I–III
blurb: An anthology of connective tissue: stories carrying beloved High Republic characters across the gap between the fall of Starlight Beacon and the Nihil's occupied zone. Padawans grow up, survivors regroup, and the seeds of Phase III's endgame are quietly planted.
trivia: The anthology bridges Phases II and III, with each story handed to the author most associated with its character.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Escape from Valo
creator: Daniel José Older & Alyssa Wong
notes: Phase III middle-grade novel
blurb: Trapped behind the Nihil's Stormwall, the children of Valo have grown up under occupation. A scrappy crew of young resisters plots to smuggle hope — and people — out from under the Eye of the Nihil, in a caper that's equal parts jailbreak and growing up.
trivia: Set inside the Occlusion Zone — the Nihil's walled-off pocket of the galaxy — showing the occupation from a kid's-eye view.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: The Eye of Darkness
creator: George Mann
notes: Phase III adult novel
blurb: A year after Starlight fell, the Nihil have walled off a swath of the galaxy behind the Stormwall, and the Nameless stalk any Jedi inside it. Elzar Mann and Bell Zettifar fight to breach the barrier from without; Avar Kriss fights to keep hope alive within. The endgame of the Nihil war begins here.
trivia: Phase III's launch novel; the Stormwall — a hyperspace barrier imprisoning whole sectors — became the era's defining image.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Temptation of the Force
creator: Tessa Gratton
notes: Phase III adult novel
blurb: The Stormwall is weakening, and for the first time since the occupation began, Avar Kriss and Elzar Mann stand together again. As the Jedi plan their counterstrike, the two must reckon with what they are to each other — and what Marchion Ro is willing to unleash to keep his prison intact.
trivia: The long-awaited Elzar–Avar reunion novel — the line's most explicit romance alongside the war's turning point.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Beware the Nameless
creator: Zoraida Córdova
notes: Phase III middle-grade novel
blurb: With the war against the Nihil reaching its peak, a band of younglings and Padawans must escort precious cargo through occupied space: knowledge that could blunt the Nameless. Terrifying for its age group in the best way — a story about being brave when the monsters are real.
trivia: Córdova's middle-grade finale sends the line's kids up against the Nameless directly — creatures the adult novels barely let Jedi survive.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Tears of the Nameless
creator: George Mann
notes: Phase III YA novel
blurb: Deep in the Occlusion Zone, a group of Jedi and their allies are hunted compartment by compartment by the Nameless. Part survival horror, part requiem, it strips the High Republic's heroes down to the question none of them can answer: what is a Jedi without the Force?
trivia: Pitched internally as 'Jedi horror' — Mann has called it the darkest book in the line, and reviewers dubbed it the era's Empire Strikes Back moment.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Into the Light
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Phase III YA novel
blurb: As the alliance against the Nihil closes in, Reath Silas carries the knowledge that could end the Nameless threat — if he can live long enough to deliver it. Claudia Gray closes the YA line the way she opened it: with scholarship, heart, and a Padawan who chose the light on purpose.
trivia: Gray bookends the YA line she opened with Into the Dark — Reath Silas's five-book arc from reluctant Padawan to Knight concludes here.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: A Valiant Vow
creator: Justina Ireland
notes: Phase III middle-grade novel
blurb: In the war's final days, young Jedi scattered across the galaxy converge for one last mission — a vow made in the line's first books comes due. The initiative's middle-grade line signs off with found family, small heroes and a promise kept.
trivia: The final middle-grade novel of the entire High Republic initiative, published in 2025 as the line wound toward its conclusion.

title: Star Wars: Dooku: Jedi Lost
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Audio drama script book; Dooku's fall told via Ventress
blurb: Asajj Ventress is hired to rescue a senator's kidnapped sister and finds the trail leading into her new master's past. Told in script form, it traces Count Dooku's path from idealistic Jedi to Sith apprentice — the slow, reasonable-sounding steps by which a good man talks himself into the dark.
trivia: Originally an audio-only drama; the script book preserves every sound cue, making it a de facto screenplay of Dooku's fall.

title: Star Wars: Master & Apprentice
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan before TPM
blurb: Eight years into an apprenticeship that isn't working, Qui-Gon Jinn is offered a seat on the Jedi Council — and considers taking it, which would hand Obi-Wan to another master. A mission to the corrupt court of Pijal, tangled in prophecy and slavery, forces master and apprentice to decide what they owe the Order, the future and each other.
trivia: Gray's Qui-Gon/Obi-Wan study became the canonical foundation for their dynamic; its prophecy subplot feeds later High Republic-era lore.

title: Star Wars: The Living Force
creator: John Jackson Miller
notes: Full Jedi Council adventure one year before TPM
blurb: One year before The Phantom Menace, the Jedi Council marks the closing of an outpost by doing something unheard of: taking a mission together. On a world sliding toward pirate rule, twelve masters rediscover what service on the ground feels like — and how far the Republic has drifted from the people it claims to serve.
trivia: Miller puts the entire Jedi Council — all twelve members — on a single field mission, a scenario the films never allowed.

title: Star Wars: Queen's Peril
creator: E. K. Johnston
notes: Padmé prequel; handmaidens assembled
blurb: Before Amidala faced the Trade Federation, newly elected Queen Padmé Naberrie and Captain Panaka assembled the handmaidens: decoys, bodyguards, and the truest friends she would ever have. A palace-intrigue prequel to The Phantom Menace about the girls behind the throne learning to become one another.
trivia: The handmaiden-assembly prequel — Johnston gave each handmaiden a full identity and skill set, cementing the fandom's 'Padmé's girl gang' canon.

title: Star Wars: Queen's Shadow
creator: E. K. Johnston
notes: Padmé transitions from queen to senator
blurb: Her two terms as queen over, Padmé Amidala expects a quiet life — until her successor asks her to represent Naboo in the Galactic Senate. With her handmaidens redeployed as a senator's staff, Padmé navigates a chamber where words are weapons and learns which battles can actually be won there.
trivia: Johnston wrote it as 'The West Wing on Naboo' — the book that explains how Padmé went from queen to the senator of Attack of the Clones.

title: Star Wars: Queen's Hope
creator: E. K. Johnston
notes: Padmé during the early Clone Wars
blurb: The Clone Wars have begun, and Padmé Amidala is newly, secretly married to a Jedi who has already shipped out. As she takes on a covert mission of her own and her handmaidens' paths diverge, the senator learns what hope costs when her own life has become a secret.
trivia: Set in the first days after the secret wedding on Naboo — a marriage that officially doesn't exist, during wartime.

title: Star Wars: Mace Windu: The Glass Abyss
creator: Steven Barnes
notes: Mace Windu solo novel after TPM
blurb: After The Phantom Menace, Mace Windu answers a dying Jedi's request and travels to the glass-scarred world of Metagos. Hunting a threat that dampens the Force itself, the Order's greatest living swordsman must rely on discipline, deduction and fists when his surest weapon fails him.
trivia: Barnes — a Hugo/Nebula-nominated author and martial artist — leans hard into Mace's Vaapad fighting style and a world where the Force itself is muffled.

title: Star Wars: Brotherhood
creator: Mike Chen
notes: Anakin & Obi-Wan early Clone Wars
blurb: In the first days of the Clone Wars, a terrorist bombing on neutral Cato Neimoidia threatens to tip the Trade Federation fully to the Separatists. Obi-Wan, newly a Council member, is sent to investigate alone — but Anakin, newly knighted and secretly married, was never good at staying away.
trivia: Chen's novel canonizes the 'Brotherhood' era between Episodes II and III — widely praised as the best prose treatment of the Obi-Wan/Anakin friendship.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn Ascendancy: Chaos Rising
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Ascendancy trilogy I; Chiss Space
blurb: Before the Empire, before the title Grand Admiral, the Chiss Ascendancy guards its borders in the lightless Chaos beyond the galaxy. When an unseen enemy strikes at Csilla through proxies, the Expansionary Defense Fleet turns to its most brilliant and least politic officer — and Thrawn's first great campaign begins.
trivia: The trilogy opens in the Chaos beyond the galaxy's edge — the Chiss Ascendancy from the inside, with Thrawn still just officer Mitth'raw'nuruodo.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn Ascendancy: Greater Good
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Ascendancy trilogy II
blurb: The Ascendancy stands victorious but shaken, and its true enemy has learned that the Chiss cannot be beaten in open battle — so Jixtus will not offer one. As hidden hands sow feud between the Nine Ruling Families, Thrawn's genius for war must fight a conflict with no fleets, no fronts and no name.
trivia: Features Zahn's favourite trick: the real attack is economic and invisible until the final chapters.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn Ascendancy: Lesser Evil
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Ascendancy trilogy III
blurb: Jixtus finally brings his war into the open, and the Nine Families' unity cracks exactly as designed. To save the Ascendancy, Thrawn must do what no Chiss officer may: act alone, beyond orders, whatever the cost to himself. The trilogy closes the loop on why a Chiss legend was found alone on a backwater world by the Empire.
trivia: The finale explains the exile that opens 2017's Thrawn — reframing his entire Imperial career as something other than banishment.

title: Star Wars: Sanctuary — A Bad Batch Novel
creator: Lamar Giles
notes: Bad Batch tie-in novel
blurb: On the run after the fall of the Republic, Clone Force 99 takes refuge on a world that offers something they've never had: a home. But sanctuary has its own politics, the Empire is never far, and Omega's safety pulls the squad between staying hidden and doing what soldiers of conscience do.
trivia: Giles's Star Wars debut and the first adult novel centred on the Bad Batch, released in 2025.

title: Star Wars: Dark Disciple
creator: Christie Golden
notes: Based on unproduced Clone Wars episodes; Ventress & Vos
blurb: Built from unproduced Clone Wars episodes: the Jedi Council, desperate to end the war, sanctions the assassination of Count Dooku — and pairs maverick Jedi Quinlan Vos with the one being who's come closest to killing him, Asajj Ventress. A story about lines the light side was never meant to cross.
trivia: Adapted from eight unproduced Clone Wars scripts; Golden kept whole scenes of Katie Lucas's Nightsisters dialogue intact.

title: Star Wars: Ahsoka
creator: E. K. Johnston
notes: Ahsoka post-Order 66
blurb: One year after Order 66, the Padawan who walked away lives under a false name, fixing machines and staying small. When the Empire comes to the farming moon of Raada, Ahsoka Tano must choose between hiding and helping — and in choosing, becomes the first spark of something that will be called a rebellion.
trivia: Johnston's debut Star Wars novel bridges Ahsoka's Clone Wars ending to her Fulcrum role in Rebels — including the white lightsabers' origin.

title: Star Wars: Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade
creator: Delilah S. Dawson
notes: Jedi-turned-Inquisitor Iskat Akaris
blurb: Iskat Akaris survived Order 66 by doing what the Jedi never let her do: everything she was told not to. Recruited into the Inquisitorius, she trades robes for armor and questions for certainty. A rare villain-protagonist Star Wars novel — the fall, told from inside, by someone who thinks she's finally free.
trivia: Dawson built Iskat Akaris from a background Jedi glimpsed in Attack of the Clones; the whole novel is told from the future Inquisitor's point of view.

title: Star Wars: Most Wanted
creator: Rae Carson
notes: Han & Qi'ra on Corellia before Solo
blurb: Before the Falcon, before the capes, Han and Qi'ra are two scrumrats in the White Worms' cellars competing for the same promotion. When a deal goes wrong, they end up on the run through Coronet City's underworld with a secret everyone wants — and learn to trust each other exactly once.
trivia: The Solo tie-in prequel: Han and Qi'ra's White Worm days on Corellia, published the month the film released.

title: Star Wars: Lords of the Sith
creator: Paul S. Kemp
notes: Vader & Palpatine on Ryloth
blurb: When Cham Syndulla's freedom fighters ambush the Emperor's flagship over Ryloth, Vader and Palpatine crash-land with rebels closing in. A predator-and-prey novel where the hunted are the two most dangerous men in the galaxy — and the Twi'lek resistance learns what hope costs.
trivia: Famous for stranding Vader and Palpatine together in the wilderness, and for canonizing Cham Syndulla's early Free Ryloth movement.

title: Star Wars: Tarkin
creator: James Luceno
notes: Tarkin's rise; second canon adult novel
blurb: The Empire's newest moff hunts the raiders who stole his ship — and the chase becomes a portrait. From the savage proving grounds of Eriadu to the Emperor's inner circle, Tarkin maps the making of the man who will hold Death Star command: not a monster by accident, but by philosophy.
trivia: Luceno's character study established Tarkin's Eriadu backstory and the carrion-plateau rituals later echoed in other canon works.

title: Star Wars: Jedi: Battle Scars
creator: Sam Maggs
notes: Jedi: Survivor game tie-in; Cal Kestis
blurb: Between the events of two video games, the crew of the Stinger Mantis — Cal Kestis, Merrin, Cere and Greez — pull a defecting stormtrooper out of Imperial space. Her price: help stealing something the Empire can't afford to lose. A heist story about what the crew owes each other after five years on the run.
trivia: Bridges the Jedi: Fallen Order and Jedi: Survivor video games; Merrin the Nightsister gets co-lead billing and a canon romance.

title: Star Wars: Solo — Expanded Edition
creator: Mur Lafferty
notes: Film novelization with added scenes
blurb: The novelization of Solo with room to breathe: Han's escape from Corellia, the Kessel Run, and the card game that won a ship — expanded with scenes the film never showed, from Qi'ra's side deals to what happened on Savareen after the credits.
trivia: The Expanded Edition adds scenes cut from the film, including Qi'ra's meeting with Enfys Nest and more Dryden Vos backstory.

title: Star Wars: Leia, Princess of Alderaan
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Leia's path to the Rebellion
blurb: At sixteen, Princess Leia Organa undertakes the three challenges of Alderaanian succession — body, mind and heart — while slowly realizing her parents are hiding something enormous: the beginnings of the Rebellion. A coming-of-age story about learning your family are traitors, and deciding to be proud of it.
trivia: Gray's YA Leia introduced Amilyn Holdo as Leia's childhood friend — Laura Dern's The Last Jedi character got her backstory here first.

title: Star Wars: A New Dawn
creator: John Jackson Miller
notes: First canon novel; Kanan & Hera meet
blurb: On the mining world of Gorse, a burned-out ex-Jedi hiding as a freighter pilot crosses paths with a Twi'lek pilot flying quiet reconnaissance against the Empire. The first canon novel of the Disney era: how Kanan Jarrus stopped hiding and Hera Syndulla found her first crewmate.
trivia: The first novel of the rebooted canon (2014), and the origin of Kanan and Hera's partnership before Star Wars Rebels.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Thrawn's rise through the Empire
blurb: Rescued from exile on a wild frontier world, the Chiss officer Mitth'raw'nuruodo is presented to Emperor Palpatine — and begins a meteoric, resented climb through the Imperial Navy. Told largely through aide Eli Vanto's eyes, it's the study of a tactical genius navigating an Empire built on politics he refuses to play.
trivia: Zahn's triumphant return to his most famous creation after the canon reboot — Eli Vanto's outsider POV deliberately mirrors Watson to Thrawn's Holmes.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn: Alliances
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Dual-timeline with Anakin/Vader
blurb: The Emperor senses a disturbance on Batuu and sends an unlikely pair: Grand Admiral Thrawn and Darth Vader. Years earlier, the same world saw Thrawn working alongside Anakin Skywalker. Two missions, one planet, and a Grand Admiral who never says how much he's figured out.
trivia: The dual-timeline structure pairs Thrawn with both Anakin Skywalker and Darth Vader — letting Vader wonder how much Thrawn has deduced about who he was.

title: Star Wars: Thrawn: Treason
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Thrawn trilogy III
blurb: With his TIE Defender programme fighting for funding against Krennic's secret project, Thrawn is handed a test: stop the creatures eating the Empire's cargo shipments. What looks like pest control unravels into Grysk infiltration — and forces Thrawn to weigh his oath to the Empire against his loyalty to the Chiss.
trivia: Set during the weeks before A New Hope; Thrawn's TIE Defender programme loses its funding battle to the Death Star, dovetailing with Rebels' final season.

title: Star Wars: Rebel Rising
creator: Beth Revis
notes: Jyn Erso between Lah'mu and Rogue One
blurb: Saved from a field on Lah'mu by Saw Gerrera, eight-year-old Jyn Erso grows up in safehouses and firefights, learning that in Saw's war there are no civilians. The story of every hard year between losing her mother and the cell on Wobani — and how Jyn learned to stop hoping.
trivia: The bridge between Jyn's childhood on Lah'mu and the prisoner the Rebellion frees in Rogue One — Saw Gerrera's foster parenting, canonized.

title: Star Wars: Catalyst — A Rogue One Novel
creator: James Luceno
notes: Galen Erso and Krennic prequel to Rogue One
blurb: Brilliant, unworldly Galen Erso believes his kyber crystal research will give the galaxy free energy. His old friend Orson Krennic knows exactly what it will give the Empire. A slow-burn tragedy of friendship, manipulation and the moment a scientist realizes what he's actually been building.
trivia: Luceno's prequel to Rogue One traces the Erso–Krennic relationship and how kyber research became a weapon programme.

title: Star Wars: Rogue One (novelization)
creator: Alexander Freed
notes: Film novelization
blurb: The novelization of Rogue One: a hope-starved thief, a faithless Imperial defector, a blind guardian and a broken assassin steal the plans that will save the galaxy none of them will see. Freed's prose leans into the war story the film implied — and makes the ending land even harder.
trivia: Freed's novelization is noted for its interstitial 'Imperial documents' and for giving every doomed member of the team an inner life the film couldn't.

title: Star Wars: From a Certain Point of View
series: From a Certain Point of View
creator: Various (anthology)
notes: 40 stories for ANH's 40th anniversary
blurb: A New Hope retold forty times by forty authors, never once from a hero's point of view. The cantina band plays its set, the dianoga meditates in the trash compactor, and Obi-Wan's ghost gets mail. A celebration of the galaxy's extras for the film's 40th anniversary.
trivia: Forty authors, forty stories, zero appearances by Luke's face — every tale retells A New Hope from a bystander's eyes, from Aunt Beru to the trash-compactor dianoga.

title: Star Wars: From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back
series: From a Certain Point of View
creator: Various (anthology)
notes: 40 stories for ESB's 40th
blurb: The Empire Strikes Back from the margins: the wampa's very bad day, an exogorth's long patience, and the untold panics of Cloud City's evacuation. Forty more stories proving the galaxy's most interesting lives happen just off-camera.
trivia: The wampa, the space slug and Willrow Hood's ice-cream maker all get their due; forty stories for ESB's 40th.

title: Star Wars: From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi
series: From a Certain Point of View
creator: Various (anthology)
notes: 40 stories for ROTJ's 40th
blurb: Return of the Jedi through forty other pairs of eyes: Jabba's court after the rancor, Ewoks meeting their gods, and the Imperials who watched the second Death Star bloom and die. The anthology series' send-off to the original trilogy.
trivia: Completes the original-trilogy anthology set; includes Olivie Blake and Mike Chen among its forty contributors for ROTJ's 40th.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront: Twilight Company
creator: Alexander Freed
notes: Battlefront game tie-in; grunt's-eye war novel
blurb: Twilight Company holds the line where the Rebellion's speeches never reach: trench by trench, world by world. When an Imperial governor defects mid-campaign, Sergeant Namir has to decide whether hope is a weapon or a liability. Star Wars as a boots-in-the-mud war novel.
trivia: The tie-in that outgrew its video game — Freed's grunt's-eye Rebellion novel is routinely recommended with no Battlefront caveats attached.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront II: Inferno Squad
creator: Christie Golden
notes: Battlefront II tie-in; Iden Versio
blurb: Formed in the ashes of the Death Star, Inferno Squad is the Empire's answer to its own failure: an elite unit that fixes leaks. Iden Versio's team infiltrates the remnants of Saw Gerrera's partisans — and being very good at their job means learning exactly what the Empire does with the truth.
trivia: The origin of Iden Versio and Inferno Squad, created to seed the Battlefront II campaign; opens minutes after the first Death Star dies.

title: Star Wars: Lost Stars
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Two friends on opposite sides of the war
blurb: Thane Kyrell and Ciena Ree grow up together on Jerrhome, enter the Imperial academy together, and end up on opposite sides of the Galactic Civil War. Told across the entire original trilogy and beyond, it's Star Wars' great doomed romance — and the best view of the war from both cockpits at once.
trivia: Gray's star-crossed epic spans A New Hope through Jakku; the Japanese webcomic adaptation made its central couple minor legends.

title: Star Wars: Heir to the Jedi
creator: Kevin Hearne
notes: First-person Luke novel
blurb: Fresh off destroying the Death Star, Luke Skywalker is a hero with no idea how to be a Jedi. A mission to extract a cryptographer — alongside pilot Nakari Kelen — becomes his first solo steps toward the Force, told in Luke's own uncertain, earnest voice.
trivia: Canon's only first-person Luke novel, set between A New Hope and ESB; infamous for the fate of Nakari Kelen.

title: Star Wars: Aftermath
creator: Chuck Wendig
notes: Aftermath trilogy I; post-Endor
blurb: The second Death Star is gone, but the Empire isn't. On Akiva, rebel pilot Norra Wexley, her slicer son Temmin, bounty hunter Jas Emari and defector Sinjir Rath Velus stumble into a secret summit of Imperial survivors — and become the ad-hoc team that starts pulling the dying Empire's threads.
trivia: The first post-ROTJ canon novel — its present-tense prose and interlude chapters were divisive, but its Jakku setup pays off across the trilogy.

title: Star Wars: Aftermath: Life Debt
creator: Chuck Wendig
notes: Aftermath trilogy II; liberation of Kashyyyk
blurb: Norra Wexley's team now hunts war criminals for the New Republic — until Han Solo goes missing trying to free Kashyyyk. Life Debt is the payoff of Chewbacca's title debt and Grand Admiral Rae Sloane's slow discovery of who is really steering the Imperial remnant.
trivia: Delivers the liberation of Kashyyyk and Han and Chewie's post-ROTJ story the films skipped over.

title: Star Wars: Aftermath: Empire's End
creator: Chuck Wendig
notes: Aftermath trilogy III; Battle of Jakku
blurb: Everything converges on Jakku: the Imperial remnant makes its apocalyptic last stand, Norra Wexley hunts Gallius Rax through the wreckage, and the Emperor's posthumous Contingency is revealed. The trilogy's finale explains both the graveyard of ships in The Force Awakens and the road to the First Order.
trivia: Stages the Battle of Jakku — the wreckage-strewn setting of The Force Awakens' opening — and reveals Palpatine's Contingency plan.

title: Star Wars: Alphabet Squadron
creator: Alexander Freed
notes: Alphabet Squadron trilogy I
blurb: After Endor, defector Yrica Quell joins a New Republic working group hunting Shadow Wing — the elite TIE unit she used to fly with. Given a squadron of five mismatched fighters and pilots as damaged as herself, she has to forge them into a weapon while lying to every one of them about what she did in the war.
trivia: Freed's trilogy follows five mismatched pilots — one of each classic starfighter, hence the name — hunting the TIE wing Yrica Quell deserted.

title: Star Wars: Shadow Fall
creator: Alexander Freed
notes: Alphabet Squadron trilogy II
blurb: Alphabet Squadron sets a trap for Shadow Wing over the industrial hell of Troithe — but Soran Keize has returned to lead his people, and the hunters become the hunted. The trilogy's dark middle act, where Quell's lie finally comes due.
trivia: The middle chapter pits Alphabet Squadron against Shadow Wing's counter-campaign; Freed has called it his 'horror movie' entry in the trilogy.

title: Star Wars: Victory's Price
creator: Alexander Freed
notes: Alphabet Squadron trilogy III
blurb: With the Empire collapsing toward Jakku, Yrica Quell flies with Shadow Wing again — as infiltrator, penitent or traitor, even she isn't sure. Freed's finale asks what justice looks like for people who followed orders, and answers it dogfight by dogfight.
trivia: The trilogy closes at the Battle of Jakku from the cockpit level — and lands one of new canon's most debated redemption arcs.

title: Star Wars: Last Shot
creator: Daniel José Older
notes: Han & Lando caper across timelines
blurb: A device called the Phylanx Redux Transmitter could turn every droid in the galaxy into a weapon, and the only two people who ever crossed its maker are Han Solo and Lando Calrissian. A caper told across three eras of their friendship — new fatherhood, old debts and one very angry Pau'an inventor.
trivia: A Han-and-Lando caper hopping between three timeframes, tying Solo's ending to the post-ROTJ era — with Older's signature comic timing.

title: Star Wars: Shadow of the Sith
creator: Adam Christopher
notes: Luke & Lando hunt Exegol clues
blurb: Seventeen years before The Force Awakens, Luke Skywalker and Lando Calrissian chase a whisper: a Sith assassin hunting a little girl named Rey. Shadow of the Sith connects Return of the Jedi's heroes to The Rise of Skywalker's mysteries — Exegol, Ochi, and the family that fled to Jakku.
trivia: The connective tissue of the sequel era: Luke and Lando's hunt for Exegol, Ochi of Bestoon, and Rey's parents — filling The Rise of Skywalker's biggest gaps.

title: Star Wars: Bloodline
creator: Claudia Gray
notes: Leia in the New Republic Senate
blurb: Six years before The Force Awakens, Senator Leia Organa fights a New Republic Senate too comfortable to see the rot. An investigation into a criminal cartel leads to something worse — and when her own secret becomes a weapon against her, the galaxy's greatest hero decides to build something new: the Resistance.
trivia: Published as 'Journey to The Force Awakens' — the Senate's centrist/populist split and the outing of Leia's parentage explain the First Order's rise.

title: Star Wars: Phasma
creator: Delilah S. Dawson
notes: Captain Phasma origin
blurb: A Resistance spy in a First Order cell buys her life with a story: the truth of Captain Phasma, from the dying world of Parnassos to the chrome armor. A nested-narrative survival epic about the galaxy's most ruthless self-made survivor.
trivia: Dawson's villain study is told as an interrogation — a captured Resistance spy trading the story of Phasma's brutal homeworld for time.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens (novelization)
creator: Alan Dean Foster
notes: Film novelization
blurb: The novelization of The Force Awakens, with connective tissue the film skipped: Poe's escape from Jakku, Unkar Plutt at Maz's castle, and extra Snoke. Foster bookends his own career — he ghost-wrote the original 1976 novelization — by introducing Rey, Finn and Kylo Ren in prose.
trivia: Foster also wrote the very first Star Wars novelization in 1976 — returning 39 years later to novelize the sequel era's opening film.

title: Star Wars: Canto Bight
creator: Various (anthology)
notes: Four novellas set in the casino city
blurb: Four novellas set in the casino city of Canto Bight, where the galaxy's war money comes to play. A wine merchant's worst week, a masseuse caught between identical alien divas, a gambler's last system — the glittering, grubby underside of The Last Jedi's most divisive setting.
trivia: Four novellas about the casino city from The Last Jedi — including Mira Grant's masseuse-to-the-Grammus-twins farce and JJM's unlucky sommelier.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi — Expanded Edition (2017 novelization)
creator: Jason Fry
notes: Film novelization with added scenes; distinct from the 2013 Legends novel of the same name
blurb: Fry's Expanded Edition novelization of The Last Jedi adds what the film couldn't hold: Han Solo's funeral, Paige Tico's last flight, and an opening dream of the life Luke never lived. The bleakest and most interior of the sequel novelizations, written with Rian Johnson's direct input.
trivia: Opens with a dream sequence of Luke married on Tatooine having never left; adds Han's funeral and Rose's sister Paige's final minutes. Not to be confused with the 2013 Legends novel of the same name.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Black Spire
creator: Delilah S. Dawson
notes: Batuu tie-in to the theme park land
blurb: Resistance spy Vi Moradi crash-lands on Batuu with a broken ship, a stolen First Order captain and orders to build a secret base from nothing. Black Spire is the story behind the Disney parks' Galaxy's Edge — recruitment, sabotage and found family on the galaxy's last honest outpost.
trivia: The Galaxy's Edge theme-park tie-in: General Organa sends Vi Moradi to build the Resistance outpost guests walk through at Disney parks.

title: Star Wars: Resistance Reborn
