creator: Rebecca Roanhorse
notes: Bridge between TLJ and TROS
blurb: After Crait, the Resistance fits inside the Millennium Falcon. Leia, Poe, Finn and Rey scatter across the galaxy calling in every favor the cause has left, while the First Order silences potential allies one by one. The story of how a fleet of nothing became the armada of Exegol.
trivia: The connective novel between The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker — the Resistance rebuilt from a single freighter's worth of survivors.

title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker — Expanded Edition
creator: Rae Carson
notes: Film novelization with added scenes
blurb: The Rise of Skywalker with its connective tissue restored: the Sith Eternal's rituals, Rey's training interlude, and quiet scenes between Rose and Leia the film cut for time. Carson's expanded novelization is the sequel trilogy's official last word.
trivia: Carson's Expanded Edition confirmed details the film only implied — including that Rey and Ben's final moment was, canonically, a kiss of gratitude... and Babu Frik's full backstory.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: Convergence
creator: Zoraida Córdova
notes: Phase II adult novel
blurb: A century and a half before the Nihil, the twin worlds of Eiram and E'ronoh are locked in a forever war their children are expected to end with a political marriage. Jedi Knight Gella Nattai and gambling chancellor's son Axel Greylark escort the betrothed — as saboteurs work to make sure peace never lands.
trivia: Phase II's adult-line opener: Córdova's Jedi-and-rogue pairing of Gella Nattai and Axel Greylark carries the era's central odd-couple energy.

title: Star Wars: The New Droid Army
creator: Amaze Entertainment (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge.
blurb: An action-adventure sequel to Jedi Power Battles, sending Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi to a droid factory world to stop a new line of battle droids before the Separatists can mass-produce them.
trivia: One of several original-story handheld tie-ins LucasArts commissioned in the prequel era rather than direct film adaptations.

title: Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force
creator: Full Fat (dev) / THQ (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge.
blurb: A side-scrolling action game retelling the original trilogy through Luke Skywalker's eyes, from Tatooine moisture farm to the second Death Star, compressed into handheld-sized levels.
trivia: Released as part of a wave of GBA tie-ins timed to the original trilogy's DVD release that same year.

title: Star Wars: Flight of the Falcon
creator: Full Fat (dev) / THQ (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge.
blurb: A Millennium Falcon flight-combat game across original trilogy locations, tasking players with piloting Han Solo's ship through asteroid fields, Death Star trenches and Imperial blockades.
trivia: One of the lowest-rated Star Wars games ever released, criticized on release for sluggish controls and repetitive level design.

title: Star Wars Episode I: Racer
creator: Torus Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge; handheld port of the N64/PC podracing game.
blurb: A scaled-down handheld port of the podracing game built around The Phantom Menace's Boonta Eve Classic, letting players race Anakin Skywalker's podracer and rivals across Tatooine's course.
trivia: The N64/PC original was, for years, the best-selling Star Wars game ever made; this GBC version condensed it for handheld hardware.

title: Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones
creator: THQ (dev/pub)
notes: PAL cartridge.
blurb: A top-down action game following the film's plot across Coruscant, Geonosis and Kamino, casting players as Obi-Wan, Anakin and Padmé across different missions.
trivia: Rushed to release alongside the film's 2002 debut, a common fate for movie tie-in games of the era.

title: Star Wars
creator: Beam Software (dev) / JVC (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge; based on the original 1977 film.
blurb: A side-scrolling action game adapting A New Hope's plot beat for beat — Tatooine, the Death Star trench run and all — for the original monochrome Game Boy.
trivia: Part of a trilogy of Game Boy adaptations Beam Software made for all three original films; this is the earliest and best-received of the three.

title: Star Wars Episode I: Obi-Wan's Adventures
creator: Torus Games (dev) / THQ (pub)
notes: PAL cartridge.
blurb: A side-scrolling action game retelling The Phantom Menace from Obi-Wan Kenobi's point of view, fighting through Naboo and facing Darth Maul in a simplified handheld lightsaber duel.
trivia: One of two competing Phantom Menace-era Obi-Wan games Torus Games made for Game Boy Color, alongside a same-year Star Wars Episode I: Racer port.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: TT Games (dev) / Warner Bros. Interactive (pub)
notes: Special Edition disc.
blurb: The LEGO treatment of The Force Awakens, plus original 'Level Ahead' bonus missions filling story gaps between Return of the Jedi and the sequel trilogy's opening.
trivia: The first LEGO Star Wars game built for the sequel trilogy era, released the same year as The Force Awakens' home video debut.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga
creator: TT Games (dev) / Warner Bros. Games (pub)
blurb: A ground-up rebuild covering all nine Skywalker saga films in one game, with hub-world free roam across every major planet and a scale far beyond any prior LEGO Star Wars release.
trivia: Originally announced in 2019, its release was delayed nearly three years — long enough to become a running fan joke before it finally launched in 2022.

title: Disney Infinity 3.0 Edition
creator: Avalanche Software (dev) / Disney Interactive (pub)
notes: Star Wars-branded starter pack; toys-to-life game requiring physical figures on a portal.
blurb: A toys-to-life crossover platform bringing Star Wars characters into the Disney Infinity sandbox for the first time, with playsets built around The Force Awakens, the prequel trilogy and Twilight of the Republic (Clone Wars era).
trivia: The last entry in the Disney Infinity series before Disney discontinued the toys-to-life line in 2016.

title: Star Wars Outlaws
creator: Massive Entertainment (dev) / Ubisoft (pub)
blurb: The first open-world Star Wars game, casting players as scoundrel Kay Vess navigating the criminal underworld's rival syndicates between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi.
trivia: The first Star Wars video game to receive an official canon designation from Lucasfilm's Story Group at launch.

title: Star Wars: Squadrons
creator: Motive Studios (dev) / EA (pub)
blurb: A first-person starfighter dogfighting game with full VR support, alternating between New Republic and Imperial remnant squadrons in the years following Return of the Jedi.
trivia: Built with a much smaller budget and team than EA's prior Battlefront titles, deliberately scoped as a focused genre piece rather than a blockbuster.

title: Star Wars Battlefront II
creator: DICE (dev) / EA (pub)
notes: 2017 EA/DICE title, distinct from the 2005 LucasArts game of the same name.
blurb: A large-scale multiplayer shooter spanning the entire saga timeline, launching alongside a single-player campaign following Imperial special forces commander Iden Versio after the first Death Star's destruction.
trivia: Infamous at launch for a loot-box progression system that triggered regulatory scrutiny in multiple countries; EA removed microtransactions within days and substantially reworked progression afterward.
inUniverseDate: Campaign: ~4 ABY; multiplayer spans entire saga

title: Star Wars Battlefront
creator: DICE (dev) / EA (pub)
notes: 2015 EA/DICE title, distinct from the 2004 LucasArts game of the same name; includes Battle of Jakku early access code.
blurb: A multiplayer-focused reboot of the Battlefront series built on DICE's Frostbite engine, recreating original trilogy battlefields with widely praised visual and sound design.
trivia: Criticized on release for lacking a single-player campaign and shipping with a thin roster of maps, both addressed to some degree in post-launch free content updates.

title: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
creator: Respawn Entertainment (dev) / EA (pub)
blurb: The sequel to Jedi: Fallen Order, picking up five years later as Cal Kestis and the Stinger Mantis crew go into hiding from an Empire tightening its grip on the galaxy.
trivia: Expanded Fallen Order's Metroidvania structure with a hub-world cantina and multiple distinct lightsaber-and-blaster combat stances.

title: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
creator: Respawn Entertainment (dev) / EA (pub)
blurb: A Soulslike/Metroidvania hybrid following Padawan Cal Kestis in hiding after Order 66, reconnecting with the Force while pursued by the Empire's Inquisitors.
trivia: EA's first major single-player, story-driven Star Wars game after years of live-service and multiplayer-focused titles under its publishing deal.

title: The Sims 4 + Star Wars: Journey to Batuu Bundle
creator: Maxis (dev) / EA (pub)
notes: Bundle pairing the 2014 base game with the 2020 Star Wars-themed game pack.
blurb: A bundle pairing the Sims 4 base life-simulation game with its Star Wars-themed Journey to Batuu game pack, letting Sims visit a version of the Galaxy's Edge theme park land and join the Resistance, First Order or Scoundrels.
rating: The Sims 4 base ~70/100 (Xbox One); Batuu game pack not separately Metacritic-scored
trivia: Journey to Batuu was one of the more divisive Sims 4 game packs, criticized for lacking core build/buy-mode content typical of the series' expansions.
inUniverseDate: N/A (contemporary life sim; no fixed Star Wars timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A direct sequel following Starkiller, Darth Vader's secret apprentice, as he escapes cloning facilities and searches for the woman he loved in the first game.
trivia: Shorter and more linear than its predecessor; producers acknowledged time pressure from a compressed development schedule.

title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: Introduces Starkiller, Darth Vader's secret apprentice, hunting down the last Jedi survivors of Order 66 with a physics-driven Force-powers system built on the Havok and Digital Molecular Matter engines.
trivia: Marketed heavily on its destructible environments and ragdoll physics; also notable as the first major appearance of Vader's secret apprentice, later folded into Legends continuity as a foundational story.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes
creator: Krome Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Console version; distinct storyline from the Nintendo DS release already in the archive.
blurb: A co-op action-platformer tie-in to the animated Clone Wars series, tracking bounty hunter Cad Bane and a Separatist superweapon plot across Republic and Separatist worlds.
trivia: Released the same year as the DS version already in this collection, but developed separately with a different plot — the DS edition serves as a prequel to this console storyline.

title: Kinect Star Wars
creator: Terminal Reality (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Motion-controlled; requires Kinect sensor.
blurb: A Kinect motion-control game bundling several minigame modes — including full-body lightsaber duels and a much-mocked 'Galactic Dance-Off' mode featuring dancing Star Wars characters.
trivia: The dance-off mode featuring a boogieing Han, Leia and Boba Fett went viral for its tonal weirdness and is now one of the most-memed moments in Star Wars gaming history.

title: Angry Birds Star Wars
creator: Rovio Entertainment (dev) / Activision (pub)
notes: Requires Kinect for motion controls on this Xbox 360 release.
blurb: A physics-puzzle mashup casting the Angry Birds cast as Star Wars characters — Red as Luke, the pigs as Imperial stormtroopers — slinging birds through original trilogy-themed obstacle courses.
rating: Metacritic score based on only ~5 critic reviews (mixed; console port of the 99-cent mobile game criticized for its $50 price)
trivia: Originally a mobile game; this console release added exclusive levels and Kinect motion controls but was criticized for charging full retail price for content available far cheaper on phones.
inUniverseDate: N/A (parody retelling, not a real timeline placement)

title: SoulCalibur IV
creator: Project Soul (dev) / Namco Bandai (pub)
notes: Xbox 360 exclusive bonus content: Darth Vader and Yoda as playable guest characters (PS3 got Vader and The Apprentice instead).
blurb: A 3D weapons-based fighting game, notable in Star Wars collecting circles for its console-exclusive crossover: Yoda and Darth Vader appear as fully playable guest fighters on the Xbox 360 version.
trivia: The first time Star Wars characters appeared as guest fighters in a non-Star Wars franchise game — Sony's PS3 version swapped Yoda for a different exclusive character, making platform choice matter to collectors.
inUniverseDate: N/A (crossover fighting game, no Star Wars setting)

title: LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars
creator: TT Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: Adapts the animated Clone Wars series rather than the films, with a galaxy-map mission structure and squad-based gameplay letting players command groups of clone troopers.
trivia: The first mainline LEGO Star Wars game built around the animated series instead of the movies.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga
creator: Traveller's Tales (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Classics reissue printing.
blurb: Combines the original LEGO Star Wars and LEGO Star Wars II into one package covering all six films of the original and prequel trilogies, with visual and gameplay upgrades over both originals.
trivia: For years the best-selling LEGO video game and a template the entire LEGO games genre — Batman, Marvel, Harry Potter and beyond — was built from.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A space-combat sequel to Star Wars: Starfighter, following Jedi Knight Nym and Bounty hunter Aayla Secura (here an independent operative, pre-Clone Wars TV canon) across missions bridging Episodes I and II.
trivia: One of the last LucasArts games built specifically for the original Xbox's launch-era hardware push toward more detailed space combat visuals.

title: Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith
creator: The Collective (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A hack-and-slash action game adapting the film, letting players fight as both Anakin and Obi-Wan across Coruscant, Utapau and the film's climactic Mustafar duel.
trivia: Notable for including the closest thing to a full Order 66 mission the games got for years — playing as multiple Jedi cut down across the galaxy in a single sequence.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
creator: BioWare (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A story-driven RPG set roughly 4,000 years before the films, following an amnesiac Republic soldier whose past holds a galaxy-altering secret, amid war with the Sith.
trivia: Widely considered one of the greatest RPGs and Star Wars games ever made; its mid-game revelation is still cited as one of gaming's best-executed twists.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
creator: Obsidian Entertainment (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A darker, more philosophical sequel following a disgraced Jedi exile piecing together what happened to the Jedi Order and the Sith Lords hunting the last Force-sensitives in the galaxy.
trivia: Rushed out in under 18 months to hit a holiday deadline, leaving substantial content — including much of the intended ending — cut; a long-running fan restoration project later recovered much of it from disc data.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A squad-based first-person shooter following Delta Squad, an elite clone commando unit, across missions during the early Clone Wars, with AI squadmates players issue tactical orders to.
trivia: Its four clone commando protagonists — Boss, Scorch, Sev and Fixer — went on to become significant figures across Legends comics and novels well beyond this one game.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront
creator: Pandemic Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: 2004 LucasArts/Pandemic title, distinct from the 2015 EA/DICE game of the same name.
blurb: A large-scale multiplayer shooter letting players fight as Rebel, Imperial, Republic or Separatist troopers across iconic original and prequel trilogy battlefields.
trivia: Widely credited as the game that first proved a mass-scale, ground-combat Star Wars shooter could work, directly inspiring the entire Battlefront series that followed.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront II
creator: Pandemic Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: 2005 LucasArts/Pandemic title, distinct from the 2017 EA/DICE game of the same name.
blurb: Adds a story-driven campaign following the 501st Legion from the Clone Wars through Order 66 and into the Galactic Civil War, alongside expanded space combat and hero characters in multiplayer.
trivia: Its campaign is one of the few games to dramatize Order 66 from the clone troopers' own point of view rather than the Jedi's.

title: Star Wars: Obi-Wan
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A third-person lightsaber-combat game following Obi-Wan Kenobi across an original story bridging The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones, hunting a rogue Padawan turned Sith apprentice.
trivia: An Xbox launch window title; its story was later folded loosely into the broader Legends timeline despite mixed reviews at release.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game
creator: Traveller's Tales (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The original LEGO Star Wars game, adapting the prequel trilogy with cooperative two-player action, silent slapstick-comedy cutscenes and a formula that launched the entire LEGO games genre.
trivia: Built by Traveller's Tales specifically to appeal to both kids and adult Star Wars fans simultaneously — a dual-audience approach that became the studio's signature.

title: LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy
creator: Traveller's Tales (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: Adapts the original trilogy with gameplay refinements over the first LEGO Star Wars game, including vehicle sections and expanded free-play exploration.
trivia: Widely regarded as an improvement on the first game in nearly every way, and the version most frequently cited as the series' creative high point before The Complete Saga combined both.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast
creator: Raven Software (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A first-person shooter/lightsaber-combat hybrid following Kyle Katarn, who abandoned the Jedi path after Dark Forces II, forced back into training to stop a Dark Jedi cult.
trivia: Built on a modified Quake III engine; its lightsaber combat system is still cited by fans as one of the best ever made for a Star Wars game.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy
creator: Raven Software (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A direct follow-up to Jedi Outcast, this time letting players build a custom Jedi student at Luke Skywalker's academy, choosing lightsaber styles and Force powers across a non-linear mission structure.
trivia: Its character creator and non-linear mission select were unusual for the era and remain the reason the PC version has an active modding community decades later.

title: Star Wars: Starfighter
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A space-combat game set during the Naboo blockade of The Phantom Menace, following three pilots — Rhys Dallows, Nym and Vana Sage — across Naboo's atmosphere and orbit.
trivia: A PS2 launch window title praised for translating the podracer-and-starfighter fantasy of the prequel era into accessible arcade combat.

title: Star Wars: Racer Revenge
creator: Vicarious Visions (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A more combat-focused podracing sequel to Episode I: Racer, adding weapons and destructible pods to the high-speed racing formula, with Anakin's rival Sebulba returning as a major antagonist.
trivia: Unlike the original Racer, built exclusively around an original non-film storyline rather than adapting Phantom Menace's Boonta Eve race directly.

title: Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: A Mario Kart-style kart racer starring chibi-styled prequel-era characters — Anakin, Jar Jar, Darth Maul and more — racing with power-ups across Star Wars locations.
trivia: Frequently cited on 'worst Star Wars games' lists despite its middling-but-not-terrible Metacritic score, largely due to sluggish handling compared to genre leader Mario Kart.

title: Star Wars: Empire at War
creator: Petroglyph Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A real-time strategy game spanning galactic and tactical scales, letting players command the Rebellion or Empire across a galaxy-map campaign set between Episodes III and IV.
trivia: Made by Petroglyph, a studio founded by former Westwood Studios (Command & Conquer) developers, bringing significant RTS pedigree to the Star Wars license.

title: Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption
creator: Petroglyph Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Expansion pack for Empire at War.
blurb: An expansion adding a third playable faction — Tyber Zann's criminal Zann Consortium — plus corruption and espionage mechanics layered onto the base game's RTS conquest.
trivia: Introduced Tyber Zann, who went on to headline his own Legends novel, The Old Republic-era comics tie-ins, and remains a fan-favorite original LucasArts character.

title: Star Wars: Force Commander
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: LucasArts' first 3D real-time strategy game, set between Episodes III and IV and following an Imperial officer who begins questioning his loyalty to the Empire.
rating: Metacritic score not clearly available (user score 8.2/10 on Metacritic)
trivia: Widely considered a technically ambitious but rough production; its lukewarm critical reception was part of why LucasArts turned to Ensemble Studios' engine for the more successful Galactic Battlegrounds the following year.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing Collector Series
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Two-game compilation: X-Wing and TIE Fighter (Collector's CD-ROM editions).
blurb: A compilation pairing remastered CD-ROM editions of X-Wing and TIE Fighter, the two space-combat sims that founded the Star Wars flight-sim genre from the Rebel and Imperial perspectives respectively.
rating: No consolidated Metacritic score (2-in-1 compilation of two previously released games)
trivia: TIE Fighter in particular is still frequently cited as one of the best space combat sims ever made, notable for casting players as an Imperial pilot in a sympathetic light.

title: Star Wars: Republic Commando
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: The PC edition of the squad-based Clone Wars shooter following Delta Squad's elite commandos, with the same tactical order system and mission structure as the Xbox release.
trivia: PC players got mod support the Xbox version lacked, extending the game's community well beyond its console lifespan.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront
creator: Pandemic Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: 2004 LucasArts/Pandemic title, distinct from the 2015 EA/DICE game of the same name.
blurb: The PC edition of the original mass-battle Battlefront, with mod support that fueled a long-running community of custom maps and total conversions.
trivia: Its PC mod scene kept the 2004 game playable and evolving years after LucasArts moved on to the sequel.

title: Star Wars: Battlefront II
creator: Pandemic Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: 2005 LucasArts/Pandemic title, distinct from the 2017 EA/DICE game of the same name.
blurb: The PC edition of the Clone Wars-to-Galactic-Civil-War campaign game, with an especially active modding community that produced total conversions still played today.
trivia: Community-made patches and mods (like the fan-made 'Conversion Pack') kept this version actively updated for over a decade after its original release.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II & Mysteries of the Sith
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
notes: Two-game compilation: Dark Forces II (1997) and its Mysteries of the Sith expansion (1998).
blurb: A compilation pairing Dark Forces II — the game that introduced Kyle Katarn's lightsaber and the light side/dark side choice system to Star Wars gaming — with its Mysteries of the Sith expansion starring Mara Jade.
rating: No consolidated compilation score (Dark Forces II individually scored in the mid-80s on release)
trivia: Dark Forces II was one of the first games to let a Star Wars protagonist meaningfully choose the dark side, with an entirely different back half of the campaign depending on the player's choices.
inUniverseDate: Dark Forces II: ~0 ABY; Mysteries of the Sith: ~1 ABY

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast
creator: Raven Software (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The PC edition of Kyle Katarn's return to the Jedi path, built on id Software's Quake III engine and widely modded for its saber-combat system.
trivia: Its PC multiplayer lightsaber dueling scene remained active for years and directly inspired dueling mechanics in later fan mods and even other studios' games.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy
creator: Raven Software (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The PC edition of the custom-Jedi academy game, with the same character creator and non-linear missions as console versions plus a long-lived modding community.
trivia: Still receives fan patches and mods today, over two decades after release, thanks to its open engine and character customization system.

title: Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds
creator: Ensemble Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A real-time strategy game built on the Age of Empires II engine, letting players build bases and armies as six playable Star Wars civilizations across a prequel-and-original-trilogy timeline.
trivia: Developed by Ensemble Studios — the Age of Empires creators — reusing and reskinning that engine's systems for a Star Wars setting.

title: Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns
creator: Ensemble Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Expansion pack for Galactic Battlegrounds.
blurb: An expansion adding two new playable civilizations — Wookiees and the Naboo — plus new campaigns tied to Attack of the Clones, released alongside the film.
rating: No consolidated Metacritic score found (expansion pack)
trivia: Added the game's first Clone Wars-specific content, timed to release the same year as Attack of the Clones itself.

title: Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds Saga
creator: Ensemble Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: All-in-one compilation of the base game and Clone Campaigns expansion.
blurb: An all-in-one repackaging bundling the base Galactic Battlegrounds game with its Clone Campaigns expansion on a single disc.
rating: No separate Metacritic score (bundle of base game + Clone Campaigns expansion)
trivia: A common way LucasArts re-released its RTS titles once expansion sales slowed, bundling base game and add-on together for budget pricing.

title: Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided
creator: Sony Online Entertainment (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: MMO base game; requires (or required, prior to server shutdown) a subscription.
blurb: The base game of Star Wars Galaxies, LucasArts and Sony Online Entertainment's massively multiplayer online RPG letting players live an entirely player-driven life across the galaxy — bounty hunter, smuggler, entertainer or Jedi.
trivia: Its deeply open-ended profession and player-city systems were ahead of their time for 2003, though a controversial 2005 'New Game Enhancements' overhaul alienated much of its original playerbase.

title: Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience
creator: Sony Online Entertainment (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Bundle: base game plus Jump to Lightspeed and both Rage of the Wookiees/Trials of Obi-Wan expansions.
blurb: A complete bundle collecting the Star Wars Galaxies base game with all of its expansions, including Jump to Lightspeed's space combat, in one budget package.
rating: No separate Metacritic score (bundle of base game + all three expansions)
trivia: Already in this archive as a companion piece is The Ruins of Dantooine, a separate standalone expansion — Galaxies had an unusually sprawling family of add-ons even by MMO standards.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
creator: BioWare (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The PC edition of BioWare's landmark RPG, identical in story and structure to the Xbox original — an amnesiac Republic soldier's journey toward a galaxy-altering secret amid the Jedi Civil War.
trivia: Its PC release included mod tools that spawned a robust modding community still active decades later, including full companion romance overhauls and restored content.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
creator: Obsidian Entertainment (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The PC edition of Obsidian's darker KOTOR sequel, following a disgraced Jedi Exile investigating the near-extinction of the Jedi Order.
trivia: The PC version's accessible files enabled 'The Sith Lords Restored Content Mod,' a long-running fan project that recovered much of the game's original, unfinished ending from data left on the disc.

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic
creator: BioWare Austin (dev) / EA (pub)
notes: Base/launch edition.
blurb: A massively multiplayer online RPG set roughly 3,600 years before the films, with eight fully voiced class storylines split between the Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire.
trivia: At the time the most expensive video game ever made, with a reported development budget exceeding $200 million; it later transitioned to a free-to-play model in 2012.

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic – Collector's Edition
creator: BioWare Austin (dev) / EA (pub)
notes: Steelbook Collector's Edition packaging with in-game and physical bonus items; game content identical to the standard release.
blurb: The premium launch packaging for The Old Republic, bundling the base game with a steelbook case, art book, soundtrack and exclusive in-game items like a HK-51 assassin droid companion.
trivia: The HK-51 companion droid bundled with this edition became available to all players through an in-game quest chain roughly a year after launch.

title: Star Wars: Dark Forces
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: Mercenary Kyle Katarn infiltrates the Empire's Dark Trooper project in this ground-breaking first-person shooter, released two years before Doom's rivals could touch it. Built on LucasArts' own Jedi engine, it let players jump, duck, and look up and down years before that was standard. The game that introduced Kyle Katarn to the galaxy and kicked off the entire Jedi Knight series.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score found for the original 1995 PC release (pre-dates Metacritic); Metacritic user score 7.5/10 (PC)
trivia: Dark Forces originated the Dark Trooper concept later referenced throughout Legends media, and its engine's jump/look mechanics predated similar features in id Software's own titles.
inUniverseDate: 2-0 BBY (Kyle Katarn's theft of the Death Star plans through the Dark Trooper mission, concurrent with the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
blurb: Kyle Katarn returns in a fully 3D sequel that lets players choose the light or dark side of the Force, complete with a branching campaign and lightsaber duels. Combining first-person shooting with Jedi powers, it sends Katarn after a data disc left by his father and into a confrontation with the Dark Jedi Jerec at the Valley of the Jedi. A landmark title for its light side/dark side choice system.
trivia: Dark Forces II was one of the first mainstream games to let players' moral choices measurably shift the story, tracking a 'dark side points' system that altered Kyle's ending and abilities.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
notes: Big box, companion missions expansion to Dark Forces II
blurb: This standalone expansion to Dark Forces II shifts focus to Kyle Katarn's new apprentice, Mara Jade, as she searches for her missing master. Fourteen new levels add a grappling hook, new Force powers, and deeper lightsaber combat to the Jedi Knight formula. A pivotal early appearance for Mara Jade as a playable protagonist.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score found; MobyGames lists limited critic coverage for the standalone expansion
trivia: Mysteries of the Sith marked one of Mara Jade's first appearances as a controllable video game protagonist, years before her prominence expanded further in Legends novels.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box, VGA 256 color
blurb: The game that launched LucasArts' celebrated space combat sim lineage, putting players in the cockpit of an X-wing, Y-wing, or A-wing as Rebel pilot Keyan Farlander. Three campaign tours of increasingly difficult missions build toward the climactic trench run on the first Death Star. A best-seller that defined the space-sim genre for a generation of PC gamers.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score found for the 1993 original release (pre-dates Metacritic/GameRankings coverage)
trivia: X-Wing was developed by the small team that would later formally incorporate as Totally Games, which went on to make every subsequent LucasArts space-combat sim through X-Wing Alliance.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY (months of Rebel operations leading up to the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars: X-Wing - Imperial Pursuit
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box, Tour of Duty expansion for X-Wing
blurb: The first Tour of Duty expansion disk for X-Wing, sending Rebel pilots on new missions to hunt down the fleeing remnants of Imperial forces after Yavin. Adds fresh mission tours and tougher AI opponents to the base game's engine. A disk-only expansion that required the original X-Wing to play.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score found for the original release; retrospective MobyGames critic average approximately 87%
trivia: Imperial Pursuit was released the same year as the base game, reflecting how quickly LucasArts iterated on the fledgling X-Wing engine in 1993.
inUniverseDate: 0 ABY (shortly after the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars: TIE Fighter
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: A daring perspective flip: instead of flying for the Rebellion, players pilot for the Galactic Empire, defending order against terrorist Rebel scum. Widely regarded as the high point of the genre, its tight flight model and morally shaded Imperial storyline set a benchmark few space sims have matched since. Frequently cited on best-games-of-all-time lists.
trivia: TIE Fighter's manual and mission briefings gave players a sympathetic, in-universe Imperial viewpoint years before Legends media regularly explored that angle.
inUniverseDate: 0-1 ABY (shortly after the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars: TIE Fighter - Defender of the Empire
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box, campaign disk expansion for TIE Fighter
blurb: The campaign disk expansion to TIE Fighter, continuing the unnamed Imperial pilot's rise through the ranks with new secret-order missions and the debut of the fearsome TIE Defender starfighter. Requires the base TIE Fighter game to run. A fan favorite for introducing one of the most iconic Imperial fighter designs in Legends canon.
trivia: The TIE Defender introduced in this expansion became one of the most requested playable ships in later LucasArts space sims, appearing again in X-Wing Alliance and X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: LucasArts pushes its space-combat engine online, letting players fly against each other as Rebel or Imperial pilots over a modem or early internet connection. The original release shipped without a dedicated single-player campaign, focusing instead on skirmish and multiplayer dogfights, a choice that drew criticism until the Balance of Power add-on arrived. A technical showcase for multiplayer space combat in the late '90s.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score confirmed for the base 1997 release; Metacritic user score 8.2/10 (PC)
trivia: The lack of a single-player campaign in the original release was controversial enough that LucasArts responded the following year with the story-driven Balance of Power Campaigns expansion.
inUniverseDate: N/A - primarily a multiplayer skirmish game with only a loose framing story, not fixed to a specific in-universe date

title: Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter - Balance of Power Campaigns
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box expansion
blurb: The expansion that finally gave X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter the single-player campaigns fans wanted, with separate storylines for Rebel and Imperial pilots. Adds new capital ships, missions, and a proper narrative structure absent from the base release. A response to fan and critic feedback that rounded out the standalone game.
trivia: Balance of Power required the original X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter disc to install, and its two mirrored campaigns let players experience the same conflict from opposing sides.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
blurb: The final and most ambitious entry in the original X-Wing series, following Ace Azzameen and his family of independent freighter pilots as they're drawn into the Rebellion. Players fly everything from starfighters to the Millennium Falcon itself across a story that runs from the aftermath of Hoth to the Battle of Endor. Widely considered the series' most polished and narratively complete installment.
rating: No confirmed Metacritic critic score found; Metacritic user score 7.8/10 (PC)
trivia: X-Wing Alliance let players briefly pilot the Millennium Falcon during its campaign, a first for the series, and included a mission recreating the Battle of Endor from the Rebel fleet's perspective.
inUniverseDate: 3-4 ABY (shortly after the Battle of Hoth through the Battle of Endor)

title: Monopoly Star Wars: CD-ROM Edition
creator: Artech Digital Entertainment (dev) / Hasbro Interactive (pub)
notes: Big box, Hasbro Interactive
blurb: The classic board game reskinned with Star Wars characters, ships, and locations replacing the usual Monopoly properties, complete with full-motion video and 3D animated sequences. Won a 1998 Software Publishers Association award for its use of visual arts in multimedia, though critics found the animations occasionally slowed play down. A curio for collectors more than a narrative game.
rating: Mixed reviews on release; no reliable modern aggregate score found
trivia: Monopoly Star Wars won the 1998 Software Publishers Association Award for Best Use of Visual Arts in Multimedia despite mixed critical reception of the gameplay itself.
inUniverseDate: N/A - a board game reskin with no story or timeline placement

title: Star Wars: Behind the Magic
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
notes: Big box, insider's guide CD-ROM
blurb: A two-disc interactive encyclopedia of the original trilogy, packed with thousands of photos, production art, ship schematics, and a searchable glossary of over 700 terms. Its standout feature is a set of deleted scenes from A New Hope, including the long-lost 'Biggs Scene' on Tatooine. A must-have reference disc for behind-the-scenes trivia rather than a game with a story.
rating: PC Gaming World 92/100; All Game Guide 4.5/5
trivia: Behind the Magic's inclusion of deleted Anchorhead footage featuring Luke's friend Biggs Darklighter made it one of the only official home releases of that cut scene for years.
inUniverseDate: N/A - a documentary/reference disc about the making of the films, not an in-universe story

title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
notes: Big box
blurb: One of the earliest CD-ROM 'interactive movie' rail shooters, casting players as Rookie One, a Tatooine farmhand who joins the Rebellion. Full-motion video sequences and digitized Star Wars footage were a showpiece for CD-ROM drives in 1993. A commercial hit that helped sell an entire generation on CD-ROM gaming.
rating: No reliable aggregate critic score found for the original 1993 PC release (pre-dates Metacritic/GameRankings coverage)
trivia: Rebel Assault was one of the best-selling CD-ROM games of its era and was frequently used as a technology demo to showcase early CD-ROM drives.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY (concurrent with the events of A New Hope)

title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault II - The Hidden Empire
creator: LucasArts (dev/pub)
notes: Big box
blurb: Rookie One returns for a bigger, more cinematic sequel, filmed with live actors on bluescreen sets rather than relying solely on digitized movie footage. The rail-shooter formula gets more varied mission types, from snowspeeder runs to lightsaber-adjacent close encounters. A visual step up that leaned harder into full-motion video storytelling.
trivia: Rebel Assault II used live-action, bluescreen-filmed footage of actual actors rather than reusing film clips, an ambitious (and expensive) production choice for a 1995 CD-ROM game.

title: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron 3D
creator: Factor 5 (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box
blurb: Luke Skywalker leads the newly formed Rogue Squadron on strike missions across the galaxy in this arcade-style flight-combat game, developed by the German studio behind the Turrican series. Simultaneously released on Nintendo 64, the PC version added enhanced visuals and control options. A launch showcase for both console 3D hardware and PC 3D accelerator cards of the era.
rating: No confirmed Metacritic critic score found for the PC release
trivia: Rogue Squadron 3D was developed by Factor 5, the same studio behind the Turrican series, and its N64 cartridge famously included extra onboard RAM to handle the game's ambitious visuals.
inUniverseDate: 0-1 ABY (beginning roughly six months after the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier
creator: Lucas Learning (dev/pub)
notes: Big box
blurb: A SimCity-style ecosystem simulation set on the Naboo moon of Ohma-D'un, tasking players with introducing plant and animal life to build a stable environment for Gungan colonization. An unusual, educational entry from LucasArts' short-lived Lucas Learning label tied to The Phantom Menace. Blends edutainment biology lessons with light strategy gameplay.
trivia: The Gungan Frontier was developed and published by Lucas Learning rather than LucasArts proper, part of a short-lived educational-games label aimed at younger players during the Phantom Menace era.
inUniverseDate: Pre-32 BBY (an ecosystem-building simulation set on Naboo prior to and during the events of The Phantom Menace)

title: Star Wars: Supremacy
creator: Coolhand Interactive (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Big box (aka Star Wars: Rebellion in North America)
blurb: An ambitious 4X grand-strategy game letting players command the full Rebel Alliance or Galactic Empire across as many as 200 star systems, juggling diplomacy, espionage, research, and fleet deployment. Released as Star Wars: Rebellion in North America and Star Wars: Supremacy in the UK and Ireland. Coolhand Interactive's only released game before the studio dissolved.
rating: GameRankings 50%; received mixed-to-poor reviews on release
trivia: Star Wars: Rebellion/Supremacy was the sole game ever released by developer Coolhand Interactive, which disbanded not long after the game shipped.
inUniverseDate: 0 ABY start (opens immediately after the Battle of Yavin; the open-ended strategy campaign can run for several years beyond)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Knight Gold Pack
creator: LucasArts (pub); bundles titles developed by LucasArts and Raven Software
notes: Bundle: Jedi Knight, Mysteries of the Sith, Jedi Knight II Jedi Outcast, Jedi Academy. Exact edition name/release year for this specific 4-game big-box bundle could not be independently confirmed online; multiple similarly named LucasArts 'Gold Pack'/'Collection' bundles exist with varying contents (some pairing only Jedi Outcast + Jedi Academy). Year given is an estimate based on Jedi Academy's September 2003 release.
blurb: A compilation box gathering the full Jedi Knight saga in one package: Dark Forces II, its Mysteries of the Sith expansion, and the Raven Software-developed sequels Jedi Outcast and Jedi Academy. A value bundle for newcomers wanting to play Kyle Katarn's entire arc from mercenary to Jedi Master in order.
rating: N/A - compilation bundle; no aggregate score exists for the pack itself (see individual titles for their own ratings)
trivia: The bundle spans two different developers: the original Dark Forces II and Mysteries of the Sith were made in-house at LucasArts, while Jedi Outcast and Jedi Academy were developed by Raven Software on id Software's Quake III engine.
inUniverseDate: N/A - compilation spanning multiple games set across 5-28 ABY; see individual titles

title: Star Wars: Jar Jar's Journey - Adventure Book
creator: Lucas Learning (dev/pub)
notes: LucasLearning kids CD-ROM storybook
blurb: An interactive storybook for young children, retelling an abridged version of The Phantom Menace across fourteen narrated, click-to-animate pages. Each page is voiced by one of the film's characters, with Jar Jar Binks guiding the journey from the Naboo swamps to Tatooine. The last PC title Lucas Learning developed before the label's closure.
trivia: Jar Jar's Journey was the final game Lucas Learning developed for PC before the educational label was shut down.
inUniverseDate: N/A - a children's storybook retelling, not treated as an independent in-universe placement

title: Star Wars: TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM
creator: Totally Games (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Jewel case collector's edition; confirmed as a distinct item from the big-box TIE Fighter (IMG_9745) - this CD-ROM compiles the original TIE Fighter campaigns plus the Defender of the Empire add-on, and adds a third, previously unreleased campaign called Enemies of the Empire, for over 100 total missions.
blurb: A jewel-case compilation combining the original TIE Fighter campaigns with the Defender of the Empire add-on, plus an exclusive third campaign, Enemies of the Empire, never sold separately. Effectively the definitive 1995 edition of TIE Fighter, with all missions on a single CD-ROM instead of multiple floppy-based installs. A must-have for series completists since it contains content unavailable in the original big box.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found specific to the Collector's CD-ROM compilation
trivia: This CD-ROM's Enemies of the Empire campaign was exclusive to this release and not included in either the original floppy/CD big box or the Defender of the Empire expansion disk.
inUniverseDate: 0-1 ABY (same period as TIE Fighter, extended by the Enemies of the Empire campaign)

title: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire
creator: LucasArts (dev) / Nintendo (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release December 2, 1996; PAL release March 1, 1997.
blurb: Mercenary Dash Rendar takes the fight to Prince Xizor's criminal empire between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. A launch-window N64 showcase, it mixes Battle of Hoth-style snowspeeder combat, Mos Eisley speeder chases, and third-person blaster action across a story told through an accompanying novel, comic, and soundtrack.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (Metacritic tracks the PC version only, not the N64 release)
trivia: Shadows of the Empire was conceived as a cross-media experiment: the game, a novel by Steve Perry, a Dark Horse comic, and a John Williams-inspired soundtrack were all released in tandem to fill the gap between Empire and Jedi.
inUniverseDate: ~3.5 BBY (between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi)

title: Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo
creator: Factor 5 / LucasArts (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release December 14, 2000.
blurb: Rookie pilot Rric Olie flies starfighters, gunboats, and gian speeders to drive the Trade Federation off Naboo. A spiritual successor to Rogue Squadron, it expands the formula with land, sea, and space missions built around the events of The Phantom Menace.
trivia: Developed by Factor 5, the same studio behind the Rogue Squadron series, Battle for Naboo reused and refined that engine's vehicle-combat technology for N64.
inUniverseDate: 32 BBY (Invasion of Naboo, concurrent with The Phantom Menace)

title: Star Wars Episode I: Racer
creator: LucasArts (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release May 18, 1999; European release June 4, 1999.
blurb: Strap into a podracer and hurtle through Tatooine's canyons at breakneck speed as Anakin Skywalker, Sebulba, or one of a dozen other racers from the Boonta Eve Classic. Widely regarded as a technical showpiece for the N64 and one of its best-selling third-party titles.
trivia: Episode I: Racer became one of the best-selling N64 games of all time, and its podracing physics engine was later reused for the PC and Dreamcast ports.
inUniverseDate: 32 BBY (Boonta Eve Classic, concurrent with The Phantom Menace)

title: Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi
creator: Sculptured Software / LucasArts (dev) / JVC Musical Industries (pub)
notes: PAL, JVC. North American release June 22, 1994; PAL release March 30, 1995.
blurb: The brutal Super Star Wars trilogy concludes on Jabba's sail barge, the forest moon of Endor, and the second Death Star. Players switch between Luke, Han, Leia, and Chewbacca through punishing run-and-gun platforming stages lifted straight from the film's biggest set pieces.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (predates Metacritic; contemporary magazine scores were generally positive)
trivia: This closing chapter finally lets players control Leia as a fully playable fighter, and adds Mode 7-scaled speeder bike chase stages through the forests of Endor.

title: Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
creator: Sculptured Software / LucasArts (dev) / JVC Musical Industries (pub)
notes: PAL, JVC. North American release November 12, 1993.
blurb: Luke, Han, and Chewbacca battle through Hoth's snowfields, Dagobah's swamps, and Cloud City's corridors in the notoriously tough middle chapter of the Super Star Wars trilogy. Lightsaber duels against Vader cap off a run-and-gun adventure built on unforgiving 16-bit difficulty.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (predates Metacritic; well-reviewed at the time, praised for graphics but criticized for extreme difficulty)
trivia: The infamous asteroid field level is frequently cited by retro-gaming outlets as one of the hardest stages in any licensed SNES game, thanks to instant-death hazards and unforgiving hit detection.

title: Super Star Wars
creator: Sculptured Software / LucasArts (dev) / JVC Musical Industries (pub)
notes: PAL, JVC. North American release November 1992.
blurb: Luke Skywalker's journey from moisture farmer to Death Star trench-run hero, retold as a grueling side-scrolling shooter-platformer. The game that launched the Super Star Wars trilogy is remembered as much for its punishing difficulty as for its faithful recreation of A New Hope's biggest moments.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (Metacritic has a listing but no aggregated critic score for the SNES release)
trivia: Super Star Wars deviates from the film by inventing entirely new levels not shown on screen, including an extended trek across the Jundland Wastes and a battle inside the Sandcrawler.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight Collection
creator: Raven Software (original dev) / Aspyr (port dev) / THQ Nordic (pub)
notes: Jedi Outcast + Jedi Academy, THQ Nordic. Released November 16, 2021.
blurb: Two classic Kyle Katarn-era lightsaber adventures in one cartridge: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast and Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy, ported to handheld by Aspyr for THQ Nordic. Both retain their acclaimed saber combat and Force-power systems from the original PC releases.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (no critic Metascore recorded for the Switch collection at time of research)
trivia: This bundle marked the first time either game had an official handheld release, arriving nearly two decades after their original PC debuts.
inUniverseDate: Two-game bundle: Jedi Outcast and Jedi Academy are both set in the years following the Battle of Endor, roughly 8-14 ABY per Legends chronology (exact placement varies by source)

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Lightsaber Duels
creator: Krome Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. Released November 11, 2008.
blurb: Swing the Wii Remote like a lightsaber in one-on-one duels between Jedi and Sith across the Clone Wars era, tied to the 2008 animated series relaunch. Fourteen characters, including Anakin, Ahsoka, and General Grievous, face off in motion-controlled combat.
trivia: Lightsaber Duels was one of the first Star Wars games built specifically around Wii motion controls, translating physical saber swings and blocks directly into gameplay.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast
creator: Raven Software (dev) / Vicarious Visions (GC port) / Activision (EU pub)
notes: PAL. European GameCube release November 22, 2002.
blurb: Mercenary Kyle Katarn reluctantly rediscovers his Jedi past to stop the Imperial remnant group the Disciples of Ragnos. Built on a modified Quake III engine, its acclaimed lightsaber combat and Force powers set the standard for Star Wars melee games.
trivia: Jedi Outcast's PC version was so highly regarded for its saber combat that its console ports, including this GameCube version by Vicarious Visions, were published by Activision in Europe rather than LucasArts.
inUniverseDate: ~8-9 ABY per Legends chronology (exact year varies by source)

title: Star Wars: Bounty Hunter
creator: LucasArts (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release December 5, 2002; PAL release February 7, 2003.
blurb: Play as Jango Fett hunting the shapeshifting assassin Zam Wesell across the galaxy, in a third-person action game that fills in the backstory of how Jango became the clone template for the Republic's army. Set immediately before Attack of the Clones.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (contemporary reviews were mixed, citing camera and control issues alongside praise for the Jango Fett fantasy)
trivia: Bounty Hunter was built using an evolved version of the game engine LucasArts first developed for Star Wars: Obi-Wan on the original Xbox.
inUniverseDate: 22 BBY (shortly before Attack of the Clones)

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
creator: Pandemic Studios (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL, based on 2003 microseries. North American/GameCube release October 28, 2002 (predates the Genndy Tartakovsky microseries it shares a name and aesthetic with).
blurb: Command squads of clone troopers and pilot AT-TEs, gunships, and starfighters across large-scale vehicular battlefields of the Clone Wars. Pandemic Studios' debut Star Wars title emphasizes tank and dogfight combat over on-foot action.
trivia: Despite its title and imagery, this game predates Genndy Tartakovsky's animated Clone Wars microseries by several months, and the two were developed independently.

title: Star Wars Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike
creator: Factor 5 (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release October 21, 2003; PAL release November 7, 2003.
blurb: Rogue Squadron's trilogy closer adds on-foot ground combat missions alongside its signature starfighter dogfights, letting players storm the Death Star corridors and fight through Hoth on the ground as well as in the cockpit. A two-disc GameCube release rounds out the package with bonus content.
trivia: Rebel Strike's bonus disc includes a playable recreation of Atari's 1983 Star Wars vector arcade game, letting players relive the original trench run in its classic form.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY-3 ABY (missions span A New Hope through The Empire Strikes Back)

title: Star Wars Rogue Leader: Rogue Squadron II
creator: Factor 5 (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release November 18, 2001, alongside the GameCube launch.
blurb: Fly with Rogue Squadron through the Death Star trench run, the Battle of Hoth, and other legendary Original Trilogy dogfights, rendered with graphics that stunned critics at the GameCube's launch. Widely considered one of the finest licensed games ever made.
trivia: Rogue Leader launched alongside the GameCube itself and its visuals were so far ahead of contemporaries that it was frequently used by Nintendo to demonstrate the console's power.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY-3 ABY (missions span A New Hope through The Empire Strikes Back)

title: Star Wars
creator: Beam Software (dev) / JVC (pub)
notes: JVC/LucasFilm Games; note in source photo references an earlier arcade tie-in, though this is an original side-scrolling action-platformer adaptation of A New Hope. North American release November 1991; PAL release March 1992.
blurb: Luke Skywalker's escape from Tatooine and journey to the Death Star, adapted into a demanding side-scrolling action game. Developed by Australian studio Beam Software, it was one of Lucasfilm Games' earliest console collaborations.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (predates review-aggregation era; contemporary magazine reviews were mixed-to-positive)
trivia: This was one of the first Star Wars games developed by Lucasfilm Games itself (rather than a third party working under license), created in partnership with Melbourne-based Beam Software.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Power Battles
creator: HotGen Studios (dev) / THQ (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release December 4, 2001; PAL release March 1, 2002.
blurb: A scaled-down handheld take on the 3D console brawler, sending Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and other Jedi through Theed Palace to repel the droid invasion of Naboo. Compresses the original's arcade-style lightsaber combat into a top-down 2D format.
trivia: Reviewers at the time noted the GBA port struggled to translate the original's 3D arena combat into two dimensions, resulting in a notably different and less well-received experience than the console versions.

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
creator: Parker Brothers (dev, programmed by Rex Bradford) / Parker Brothers (pub)
notes: Cartridge only, no box shown.
blurb: Pilot a snowspeeder over the ice fields of Hoth, using your tow cable to trip up AT-AT walkers before the Empire crushes the Rebel base. The first licensed Star Wars video game ever released, and a huge commercial hit for Parker Brothers.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (1982 title predates review aggregation; it was a major commercial success)
trivia: Empire Strikes Back and Frogger were Parker Brothers' two best-selling titles of 1982, together moving roughly 3 million cartridges.
inUniverseDate: 3 BBY (Battle of Hoth, The Empire Strikes Back)

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi - Death Star Battle
creator: Parker Brothers (dev, programmed by Rex Bradford) / Parker Brothers (pub)
notes: Cartridge only, no box shown.
blurb: Fly the Millennium Falcon through TIE fighter swarms and a Death Star energy shield before diving in to blast the reactor core and escape the resulting explosion. The first video game based on Return of the Jedi.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (1983 title predates review aggregation)
trivia: The game was also released for the Atari 5200 and Atari 8-bit computers, and was later bundled into a ZX Spectrum+ software pack by Sinclair Research in 1985.
inUniverseDate: 4 ABY (Battle of Endor, Return of the Jedi)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Arena
creator: Atari (dev, programmed by Rex Bradford) / Parker Brothers (pub)
notes: Cartridge only, no box shown.
blurb: Two Jedi face off with lightsabers, deflecting a Force-thrown 'seeker' ball at one another using paddle controllers. The first video game to feature lightsaber combat, requiring a second paddle controller for two-player duels.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (1983 title predates review aggregation)
trivia: Jedi Arena is the first game in the Star Wars franchise to feature lightsabers, predating any game showing on-screen lightsaber duels between named film characters.
inUniverseDate: N/A - abstract training-arena concept with no placement in the Legends timeline

title: Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron
creator: Rebellion Developments (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release November 3, 2009; PAL release November 6, 2009.
blurb: Fight across the entire Clone Wars-to-Galactic-Civil-War timeline as members of the 501st Legion, moving seamlessly from ground combat to vehicle warfare to full starfighter dogfights within a single mission. The last handheld Battlefront release before the series went dormant.
trivia: Elite Squadron introduced multi-layered space-to-ground battles for the first time in the Battlefront series, letting players land a starfighter directly onto a capital ship to continue the fight on foot.
inUniverseDate: ~19 BBY-4 ABY (campaign spans the Clone Wars through the Battle of Endor)

title: Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron
creator: Rebellion Developments (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. North American release October 9, 2007.
blurb: The first PSP-exclusive entry in the Battlefront series follows a Rebel special-ops unit from its formation before the Battle of Yavin through to the Battle of Endor. Supports up to 16-player online multiplayer, a first for the handheld series.
trivia: Renegade Squadron was the first Battlefront game built exclusively for a handheld platform rather than ported down from a home console release.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY-4 ABY (campaign spans Battle of Yavin through Battle of Endor)

title: Star Wars: Lethal Alliance
creator: Ubisoft Montreal (dev) / Ubisoft (pub)
notes: PAL, Ubisoft. Released December 2006.
blurb: Rebel agent Rianna Saren and her droid companion Zeeo infiltrate Imperial facilities on a stealth-and-action mission set between Revenge of the Sith and A New Hope. A rare Star Wars entry developed entirely by Ubisoft rather than LucasArts.
trivia: Lethal Alliance was developed in parallel by two different Ubisoft studios, Montreal for the PSP version and Casablanca for the Nintendo DS version, resulting in two distinct games sharing the same story.
inUniverseDate: ~19 BBY (between Revenge of the Sith and A New Hope)

title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault
creator: LucasArts (dev) / JVC Musical Industries (pub)
notes: PAL (Sega Mega-CD is the PAL/European branding of the Sega CD add-on; original US Sega CD release was 1993, with the European Mega-CD version following in 1994).
blurb: Blast TIE fighters and dodge asteroid fields as a rookie Rebel pilot in this rail-shooter interactive movie built around full-motion video sequences. LucasArts' first CD-ROM-only release used pre-rendered cinematics unlike anything else on cartridge-based consoles at the time.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (1994 title predates review aggregation)
trivia: Rebel Assault was LucasArts' first CD-ROM-exclusive game, and its FMV-driven presentation was considered a major technical showcase for the format when it launched on PC in 1993.
inUniverseDate: ~0 BBY (shortly before the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault II - The Hidden Empire
creator: LucasArts (dev) / Factor 5 (PlayStation port) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. PlayStation release November 26, 1996 (original DOS/multiplatform release was 1995).
blurb: A new Rebel recruit is drawn into a plot involving an Imperial superweapon in this FMV-heavy rail-shooter sequel, filmed with live actors composited into rendered environments. The PlayStation port brought the CD-based spectacle to Sony's console.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (Metacritic has no critic score aggregated for this title)
trivia: Unlike its predecessor, Rebel Assault II was shot with live actors on blue-screen soundstages rather than using in-engine character models, giving it a distinctly cinematic look for a mid-90s console game.
inUniverseDate: ~0 BBY (shortly before the Battle of Yavin)

title: Star Wars: Masters of Teras Kasi
creator: LucasArts (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: English/Finnish. North American release November 25, 1997; PAL release March 1998.
blurb: Luke, Vader, Boba Fett, and other Star Wars icons settle their differences in a 3D fighting game built around the martial art Teräs Käsi. Notorious among fans as one of the more poorly received licensed Star Wars titles of the era.
rating: GameSpot 4.4/10 (Poor); no reliable Metacritic aggregate found
trivia: Masters of Teras Kasi popularized the term 'Teräs Käsi' for Star Wars fans, a hand-to-hand fighting style that had only been mentioned in passing in Expanded Universe fiction before this game built an entire roster around it.
inUniverseDate: ~3 ABY (between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, per the game's own framing story)

title: Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace
creator: Big Ape Productions (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL, Value Series. North American release September 14, 1999; PAL release September 24, 1999.
blurb: Guide Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and other heroes through a beat-'em-up retelling of The Phantom Menace, from the invasion of Naboo to the duel with Darth Maul. This PlayStation version was later reissued as a budget Value Series release.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (contemporary reviews were mixed, praising the story fidelity but criticizing the camera and combat)
trivia: Because the game was developed alongside the film's production, some character voice lines and story beats reflect earlier drafts of the Phantom Menace script rather than the finished movie.

title: Star Wars: Demolition
creator: Luxoflux (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. Released November 12, 2000.
blurb: Star Wars characters climb into armed vehicles and battle it out arena-style, built on the same engine as Luxoflux's Vigilante 8 series. Boba Fett, Darth Maul, and other fan favorites trade blaster fire and missiles across a variety of themed arenas.
trivia: Demolition repurposed the vehicular-combat engine from Luxoflux's Vigilante 8 series, simply reskinning its arena-battle gameplay with a Star Wars license and cast.
inUniverseDate: N/A - non-canon vehicular arena combat without a fixed story placement

title: Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles
creator: LucasArts (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: Released October 4, 2000.
blurb: Four playable Jedi, including Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Mace Windu, and Adi Gallia, hack through waves of battle droids to retake Theed Palace during the invasion of Naboo. The Dreamcast version is widely considered the definitive release thanks to sharper visuals than its PlayStation counterpart.
trivia: Critics at the time singled out the Dreamcast version as the best-looking release of Jedi Power Battles, citing noticeably improved textures and frame rate over the original PlayStation version.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Jedi Alliance
creator: LucasArts Singapore (dev) / LucasArts (pub)
notes: PAL. Released November 11, 2008.
blurb: Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano lead a squad of Jedi and clone troopers on a rescue mission through touch-screen lightsaber combos and stylus-driven puzzles. Released alongside the Wii's Lightsaber Duels to tie into the 2008 animated Clone Wars relaunch.
trivia: Jedi Alliance uses the DS touch screen for context-sensitive lightsaber combo attacks, a control scheme distinct from its Wii motion-control sibling released the same month.

title: Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith
creator: Ubisoft Montreal (dev) / LucasArts / Ubisoft (pub)
notes: PAL. Released to coincide with the film's May 2005 debut; some sources credit Double Helix Games rather than Ubisoft Montreal for the DS version specifically.
blurb: Relive Anakin Skywalker's fall to the dark side across the Battle of Coruscant, Utapau, and the final duel on Mustafar in this handheld adaptation of the final prequel film. Released day-and-date with the movie and its console counterparts.
trivia: LucasArts released Revenge of the Sith simultaneously across an unusually wide spread of platforms, with different studios handling different versions to hit the film's May 2005 theatrical release date.

title: Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: THX digitally mastered
blurb: The Galactic Republic is in turmoil as the Trade Federation blockades the peaceful planet of Naboo. Jedi Knights Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are dispatched to negotiate, but soon find themselves protecting young Queen Padme Amidala and a gifted slave boy named Anakin Skywalker, in whom the Force runs unusually strong. As political intrigue masks the rise of a hidden Sith Lord, the seeds of the Republic's downfall are sown.
trivia: The Phantom Menace's 2000 VHS release carried Lucasfilm's THX certification for audio/video mastering quality, part of a home-video push to replicate the film's theatrical sound design on tape.

title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: THX digitally mastered, special edition
blurb: Ten years after the invasion of Naboo, the Galactic Republic teeters on the brink of civil war as thousands of solar systems threaten to secede. Anakin Skywalker, now a headstrong Jedi apprentice, is assigned to protect Senator Padme Amidala while Obi-Wan Kenobi uncovers a mysterious clone army and a growing Separatist movement. Forbidden love and dark secrets set the stage for galaxy-wide war.
trivia: Attack of the Clones reached VHS and DVD on the same release day in November 2002, one of the last times a major theatrical Star Wars title was issued on tape at all.

title: Star Wars Trilogy - Limited Edition Box Set
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: Darth Vader helmet cover, THX digitally mastered box set
blurb: This collector's box gathers the original Star Wars trilogy - A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi - following Luke Skywalker's journey from Tatooine farm boy to Jedi Knight as the Rebel Alliance topples the Galactic Empire.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 8.3-8.7/10 (Eps. IV-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: This THX-remastered VHS box set appears to predate the 1997 theatrical Special Edition VHS releases, preserving the pre-CGI 1977-83 cuts with newly remastered audio; the exact release year of this particular THX pressing could not be pinned down with certainty and may fall anywhere in the mid-1990s.

title: Star Wars Trilogy - Special Edition (Widescreen)
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: Silver Darth Vader cover, widescreen
blurb: This 1997 Special Edition VHS box collects the theatrically re-released original trilogy - A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi - complete with the new digitally enhanced effects, scenes, and the widescreen letterboxed presentation.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 8.3-8.7/10 (Eps. IV-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: The silver-cased box housed the widescreen (letterboxed) transfer of the 1997 Special Edition VHS release, sold alongside a gold-cased pan-and-scan counterpart for buyers with then-standard 4:3 televisions.

title: Star Wars Trilogy - Special Edition
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: Gold/bronze Darth Vader cover variant - confirm if pan & scan vs widescreen counterpart to IMG_9763
blurb: This 1997 Special Edition VHS box collects the theatrically re-released original trilogy - A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi - complete with the new digitally enhanced effects and scenes, presented in a full-screen pan-and-scan transfer.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 8.3-8.7/10 (Eps. IV-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: The gold/bronze-cased box held the full-screen, pan-and-scan transfer of the 1997 Special Edition VHS release - confirmed as the fullscreen counterpart to the silver widescreen box (IMG_9763), matching Lucasfilm's known 1997 dual-SKU VHS release strategy.

title: Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: 2-disc set
blurb: The Galactic Republic is in turmoil as the Trade Federation blockades the peaceful planet of Naboo. Jedi Knights Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are dispatched to negotiate, but soon find themselves protecting young Queen Padme Amidala and a gifted slave boy named Anakin Skywalker, in whom the Force runs unusually strong. As political intrigue masks the rise of a hidden Sith Lord, the seeds of the Republic's downfall are sown.
trivia: The Phantom Menace's October 2001 DVD was the first Star Wars saga film released on the format, arriving over two years after the film's May 1999 theatrical debut.

title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: 2-disc set
blurb: Ten years after the invasion of Naboo, the Galactic Republic teeters on the brink of civil war as thousands of solar systems threaten to secede. Anakin Skywalker, now a headstrong Jedi apprentice, is assigned to protect Senator Padme Amidala while Obi-Wan Kenobi uncovers a mysterious clone army and a growing Separatist movement. Forbidden love and dark secrets set the stage for galaxy-wide war.
trivia: The bonus disc's documentary 'From Puppets to Pixels' chronicled the heavy shift to digital character animation that defined Attack of the Clones' production.

title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: 2-disc set
blurb: As the Clone Wars rage across the galaxy, Anakin Skywalker is torn between his loyalty to the Jedi Order and a secret marriage to Padme Amidala. Manipulated by the Sith Lord Darth Sidious and haunted by visions of losing those he loves, Anakin makes a fateful choice that will turn him into Darth Vader. The Republic falls, the Jedi are hunted to near-extinction, and the Empire rises.
trivia: Revenge of the Sith was the first and only Star Wars saga film rated PG-13, a fact its DVD's darker-toned bonus documentaries about Anakin's fall lean into.

title: Star Wars Trilogy
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: Gold embossed box, 4-disc set, first time on DVD
blurb: This collector's box gathers the original Star Wars trilogy - A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi - following Luke Skywalker's journey from Tatooine farm boy to Jedi Knight as the Rebel Alliance topples the Galactic Empire.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 8.3-8.7/10 (Eps. IV-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: Released September 21, 2004, this gold-embossed box marked the original trilogy's first-ever appearance on DVD, though the films included were the 2004 digitally revised versions rather than the unaltered 1977-83 theatrical cuts.

title: Star Wars: Prequel Trilogy
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: Six disc set
blurb: This set collects the complete prequel trilogy - The Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones, and Revenge of the Sith - tracing Anakin Skywalker's path from gifted slave child to fallen Jedi, and the collapse of the Old Republic into the tyranny of the Galactic Empire.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 6.5-7.6/10 (Eps. I-III); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: This September 2008 box was the first time all three prequel films were packaged together on DVD as a dedicated trilogy set, each retaining its own 2-disc bonus-feature configuration.

title: Star Wars Trilogy
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: Six disc set, includes both remastered and original theatrical cuts
blurb: This collector's box gathers the original Star Wars trilogy - A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi - following Luke Skywalker's journey from Tatooine farm boy to Jedi Knight as the Rebel Alliance topples the Galactic Empire.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 8.3-8.7/10 (Eps. IV-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: Released as a Limited Edition in September 2006, this was the only official DVD set to include the unaltered 1977-83 theatrical cuts (as non-anamorphic bonus discs) alongside the 2004 remastered versions; it has never been reissued since.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: J.J. Abrams (dir.)
blurb: Thirty years after the fall of the Empire, a new threat called the First Order has risen from its ashes. Scavenger Rey, defected stormtrooper Finn, and ace pilot Poe Dameron join forces with Han Solo and Chewbacca to find the missing Luke Skywalker and stop the First Order's superweapon, Starkiller Base, before it destroys the New Republic.
trivia: The Force Awakens' home release included deleted scenes but, notably, no feature-length audio commentary from director J.J. Abrams, unlike several earlier saga entries.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
creator: Rian Johnson (dir.)
blurb: Rey seeks out the reclusive Luke Skywalker on a remote island, hoping he will train her and join the fight against the First Order. Meanwhile, the battered Resistance fleet, led by General Leia Organa, is pursued across the galaxy by Kylo Ren and the First Order's relentless armada, forcing hard choices about legacy, failure, and hope.
trivia: The Last Jedi's bonus features included 'The Director and the Jedi,' a feature-length documentary chronicling Rian Johnson's production journey on the film.

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
creator: Gareth Edwards (dir.)
blurb: In the years before A New Hope, rebel fighter Jyn Erso is recruited by the Alliance to help steal the plans to the Empire's Death Star. Joined by a ragtag team of soldiers, spies, and a reprogrammed Imperial droid, Jyn must complete her father's secret legacy in a desperate, self-sacrificing mission that makes the Rebellion's ultimate victory possible.
trivia: Rogue One was the first live-action Star Wars film to skip an on-disc audio commentary track, a pattern later carried through the rest of the anthology and sequel-era releases.

title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
creator: Ron Howard (dir.)
blurb: Before he was a legendary smuggler and Rebel hero, Han Solo was a young man trying to survive the criminal underworld of the Outer Rim. Alongside the Wookiee Chewbacca and gambler Lando Calrissian, Han pulls off a daring heist that will set him on the path to the man he becomes, aboard a ship called the Millennium Falcon.
trivia: Solo underperformed at the box office relative to other Star Wars films, and its home release arrived roughly three months after its May 2018 theatrical debut, one of the franchise's fastest theatrical-to-disc turnarounds.

title: Family Guy Presents: Laugh It Up, Fuzzball - The Star Wars Trilogy
creator: Seth MacFarlane (creator); Dominic Polcino, Peter Shin (dirs.)
blurb: Peter Griffin and the Family Guy cast retell the entire original Star Wars trilogy in this animated parody compilation, combining the specials 'Blue Harvest,' 'Something, Something, Something, Dark Side,' and 'It's a Trap!' Peter stars as Han Solo (and Darth Vader), Stewie as Luke Skywalker (and the Emperor), and Chris as Chewbacca, spoofing the saga's biggest moments with Family Guy's signature cutaway humor.
rating: IMDb ~8.2/10 (based on the three component episodes; not separately listed on IMDb as a standalone compilation)
