trivia: George Lucas personally granted Seth MacFarlane rare permission for Family Guy to parody Star Wars this extensively, and the three specials collected here originally aired individually between 2007 and 2010 before being packaged as this trilogy DVD.
inUniverseDate: 0 BBY - 4 ABY (parody of the original trilogy's timeline)

title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
creator: J.J. Abrams (dir.)
blurb: The remnants of the Resistance make a final stand against the First Order as a resurrected threat from the past, the ancient Sith Lord Emperor Palpatine, reveals a plan to destroy the galaxy. Rey, Finn, and Poe race to uncover the truth about Rey's origins and confront Kylo Ren in a battle that will decide the fate of the Skywalker legacy.
trivia: The Rise of Skywalker's home release included the making-of documentary 'Aftermath,' reflecting on the film's famously compressed and heavily revised post-production schedule.

title: Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
notes: 4K UHD + Blu-ray + Bonus Disc
blurb: The Galactic Republic is in turmoil as the Trade Federation blockades the peaceful planet of Naboo. Jedi Knights Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are dispatched to negotiate, but soon find themselves protecting young Queen Padme Amidala and a gifted slave boy named Anakin Skywalker, in whom the Force runs unusually strong. As political intrigue masks the rise of a hidden Sith Lord, the seeds of the Republic's downfall are sown.
trivia: This 2020 4K UHD release used a new transfer supervised by Lucasfilm as part of the complete Skywalker Saga 4K box set, giving Episode I its UHD debut alongside the other eight saga films simultaneously.

title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
blurb: Ten years after the invasion of Naboo, the Galactic Republic teeters on the brink of civil war as thousands of solar systems threaten to secede. Anakin Skywalker, now a headstrong Jedi apprentice, is assigned to protect Senator Padme Amidala while Obi-Wan Kenobi uncovers a mysterious clone army and a growing Separatist movement. Forbidden love and dark secrets set the stage for galaxy-wide war.
trivia: Attack of the Clones was the first major Hollywood film shot almost entirely on digital cinema cameras (Sony HDW-F900), and its 4K UHD transfer showcases that original digital-native photography.

title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
blurb: As the Clone Wars rage across the galaxy, Anakin Skywalker is torn between his loyalty to the Jedi Order and a secret marriage to Padme Amidala. Manipulated by the Sith Lord Darth Sidious and haunted by visions of losing those he loves, Anakin makes a fateful choice that will turn him into Darth Vader. The Republic falls, the Jedi are hunted to near-extinction, and the Empire rises.
trivia: Revenge of the Sith's 4K UHD release draws on Industrial Light & Magic's original digital intermediate, since the film was mastered digitally from the start rather than scanned from film.

title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
creator: Ron Howard (dir.)
blurb: Before he was a legendary smuggler and Rebel hero, Han Solo was a young man trying to survive the criminal underworld of the Outer Rim. Alongside the Wookiee Chewbacca and gambler Lando Calrissian, Han pulls off a daring heist that will set him on the path to the man he becomes, aboard a ship called the Millennium Falcon.
trivia: Ron Howard took over directing Solo midway through production after original directors Phil Lord and Christopher Miller were let go; the 4K disc's extras touch on the film's unusually turbulent production history.

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
creator: Gareth Edwards (dir.)
blurb: In the years before A New Hope, rebel fighter Jyn Erso is recruited by the Alliance to help steal the plans to the Empire's Death Star. Joined by a ragtag team of soldiers, spies, and a reprogrammed Imperial droid, Jyn must complete her father's secret legacy in a desperate, self-sacrificing mission that makes the Rebellion's ultimate victory possible.
trivia: Rogue One reached 4K UHD in April 2020, later than most of the other post-2015 films, following an extended high dynamic range grading pass on its notably dark, VFX-heavy cinematography.

title: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope
creator: George Lucas (dir.)
blurb: Luke Skywalker, a young farm boy on the desert planet Tatooine, is thrust into a galactic struggle when he acquires two droids carrying stolen plans to the Empire's ultimate weapon, the Death Star. Joined by Han Solo, Princess Leia, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Chewbacca, Luke must learn the ways of the Force to strike a blow against the evil Galactic Empire.
trivia: The 2020 4K UHD release of A New Hope used the same 4K scan and restoration prepared for the Skywalker Saga box set, addressing some of the color-grading criticism leveled at earlier Blu-ray releases.

title: Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back
creator: Irvin Kershner (dir.)
blurb: The Rebel Alliance suffers a crushing defeat as the Empire drives them from their hidden base on Hoth. While Han Solo and Princess Leia flee from Darth Vader's forces, Luke Skywalker travels to the swamp world of Dagobah to train with the Jedi Master Yoda. A shocking revelation on Cloud City will forever change Luke's understanding of his family and his destiny.
trivia: Widely regarded by fans and critics as the high point of the saga, The Empire Strikes Back's 4K transfer restores fine film grain detail that had been digitally smoothed over in earlier DVD-era remasters.

title: Star Wars: Episode VI - Return of the Jedi
creator: Richard Marquand (dir.)
blurb: Luke Skywalker leads a daring mission to rescue Han Solo from Jabba the Hutt before rejoining the Rebel Alliance for a final assault on the Empire's second Death Star. As the Rebel fleet battles overhead and Han and Leia fight to disable the station's shield on Endor, Luke confronts Darth Vader and the Emperor in a climactic struggle for his own soul.
trivia: Return of the Jedi's 4K UHD carries over the 2004 digitally inserted 'Jedi Rocks' musical number, replacing the original 1983 Max Rebo Band performance seen only in the unaltered theatrical cut.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: J.J. Abrams (dir.)
notes: With new collectible sleeves
blurb: Thirty years after the fall of the Empire, a new threat called the First Order has risen from its ashes. Scavenger Rey, defected stormtrooper Finn, and ace pilot Poe Dameron join forces with Han Solo and Chewbacca to find the missing Luke Skywalker and stop the First Order's superweapon, Starkiller Base, before it destroys the New Republic.
trivia: This copy was repackaged with new poster-art collectible sleeves as part of a wider re-release of the sequel trilogy's 4K UHD packaging; the exact reissue wave and date could not be independently confirmed.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
creator: Rian Johnson (dir.)
blurb: Rey seeks out the reclusive Luke Skywalker on a remote island, hoping he will train her and join the fight against the First Order. Meanwhile, the battered Resistance fleet, led by General Leia Organa, is pursued across the galaxy by Kylo Ren and the First Order's relentless armada, forcing hard choices about legacy, failure, and hope.
trivia: The Last Jedi was shot on a mix of 35mm film and Arri Alexa digital cameras, and its 4K UHD transfer was struck from the completed 4K digital intermediate rather than a native camera-negative scan.

title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
creator: J.J. Abrams (dir.)
blurb: The remnants of the Resistance make a final stand against the First Order as a resurrected threat from the past, the ancient Sith Lord Emperor Palpatine, reveals a plan to destroy the galaxy. Rey, Finn, and Poe race to uncover the truth about Rey's origins and confront Kylo Ren in a battle that will decide the fate of the Skywalker legacy.
trivia: The Rise of Skywalker's 4K disc includes a substantial set of deleted scenes with on-camera introductions from director J.J. Abrams, reflecting the film's famously compressed and heavily revised production schedule.

title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
creator: Ron Howard (dir.)
blurb: Before he was a legendary smuggler and Rebel hero, Han Solo was a young man trying to survive the criminal underworld of the Outer Rim. Alongside the Wookiee Chewbacca and gambler Lando Calrissian, Han pulls off a daring heist that will set him on the path to the man he becomes, aboard a ship called the Millennium Falcon.
trivia: The standard Blu-ray edition of Solo carries a smaller selection of deleted scenes than the later 4K UHD release, which added several additional cut sequences.

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
creator: Gareth Edwards (dir.)
blurb: In the years before A New Hope, rebel fighter Jyn Erso is recruited by the Alliance to help steal the plans to the Empire's Death Star. Joined by a ragtag team of soldiers, spies, and a reprogrammed Imperial droid, Jyn must complete her father's secret legacy in a desperate, self-sacrificing mission that makes the Rebellion's ultimate victory possible.
trivia: Rogue One's Blu-ray bonus features focus heavily on the film's extensive connections and callbacks to the original 1977 trilogy, including matching sets, ships, and costumes recreated for continuity.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: J.J. Abrams (dir.)
notes: Limited edition, Choose the Lightside sleeve
blurb: Thirty years after the fall of the Empire, a new threat called the First Order has risen from its ashes. Scavenger Rey, defected stormtrooper Finn, and ace pilot Poe Dameron join forces with Han Solo and Chewbacca to find the missing Luke Skywalker and stop the First Order's superweapon, Starkiller Base, before it destroys the New Republic.
trivia: The Force Awakens received numerous retailer-exclusive packaging variants at launch; this lightside-themed slipcover is one of several limited-edition sleeves issued alongside a corresponding dark-side-themed design, though the precise retailer/edition name could not be independently verified.

title: Star Wars: The Complete Saga
creator: George Lucas, Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand (dirs.)
notes: 9-disc box set, episodes I-VI
blurb: This box set collects all six films of the original Star Wars saga, Episodes I through VI, following the Skywalker family across two generations - from Anakin's rise and fall as Darth Vader to his son Luke's redemption of him and defeat of the Empire.
rating: IMDb ratings for included films range 6.5-8.7/10 (Eps. I-VI); no single box-set rating exists
trivia: Released September 16, 2011, The Complete Saga was the first Blu-ray release of the prequel trilogy and packaged six film discs with three additional discs of supplemental documentaries and deleted scenes.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
creator: Rian Johnson (dir.)
notes: Target-exclusive The Resistance Rises steelbook/slipcover, possible dup of IMG_9844, confirm distinct edition
blurb: Rey seeks out the reclusive Luke Skywalker on a remote island, hoping he will train her and join the fight against the First Order. Meanwhile, the battered Resistance fleet, led by General Leia Organa, is pursued across the galaxy by Kylo Ren and the First Order's relentless armada, forcing hard choices about legacy, failure, and hope.
trivia: This Target-exclusive steelbook was part of a wave of retailer-specific packaging (Target, Best Buy, Walmart) that accompanied The Last Jedi's 2018 home video launch, each carrying unique cover art; this Blu-ray-format item is a physically distinct disc/edition from the 4K UHD copy also in this collection (IMG_9844).

title: Ewoks: The Battle for Endor
creator: Jim & Ken Wheat (dir.)
notes: TV movie
blurb: Sequel to Caravan of Courage. Orphaned Cindel Towani teams with the Ewoks and grizzled hermit Noa Briqualon to fight off Terak's Marauders and the shapeshifting witch Charal, who are after a mysterious power source salvaged from the wrecked Towani starcruiser. Written and directed by Jim and Ken Wheat from a story by George Lucas.
trivia: Wilford Brimley (Noa) did not get along with directors Jim and Ken Wheat, so his scenes were instead directed by production designer Joe Johnston.

title: Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure
creator: John Korty (dir.)
notes: TV movie, CBS/FOX
blurb: The Towani family crash-lands on the forest moon of Endor; after the parents are captured by the giant Gorax, their children Cindel and Mace join Wicket and a band of Ewoks on a quest to rescue them. Directed by John Korty from a story by George Lucas, this was Lucasfilm's first Ewok TV movie, originally aired as "The Ewok Adventure" on ABC in 1984.
trivia: The film won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Special Visual Effects and was also nominated for Outstanding Children's Programming.
inUniverseDate: 3 ABY (officially placed here per Star Wars: Behind the Magic)

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
creator: Dave Filoni (dir.)
notes: 2008 animated theatrical film
blurb: Theatrical film that served as the pilot for the CGI Clone Wars series. Anakin Skywalker and his new Padawan, Ahsoka Tano, are tasked with rescuing Jabba the Hutt's kidnapped son to secure a vital hyperspace route through Hutt Space. Directed by Dave Filoni, it was Lucasfilm Animation's theatrical feature debut.
rating: IMDb 5.8/10 (theatrical film; Rotten Tomatoes 18% critics / 41% audience)
trivia: Although it remains Star Wars' lowest Rotten Tomatoes-rated theatrical release, the film successfully launched the CGI series that would go on to be one of the franchise's most acclaimed pieces of media.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 1, Volume 1
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: Subtitled "A Galaxy Divided," this first Season 1 DVD volume (released March 24, 2009) collects the episodes "Ambush," "Rising Malevolence," "Shadow of Malevolence," and "Destroy Malevolence," introducing Asajj Ventress and the hunt for General Grievous's flagship, the Malevolence.
trivia: A Walmart-exclusive edition of this disc added a bonus fifth episode, "Downfall of a Droid," ahead of its general home-video release.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 1, Volume 2
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: A further batch of Season 1 episodes released on DVD by Warner Home Video in 2009, continuing the CGI series' first-year run of stories set during the early Clone Wars campaigns. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 1's individual-volume DVD releases preceded the full four-disc "Complete Season One" box set, which Warner Home Video issued on November 3, 2009.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 1, Volume 3
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: A further batch of Season 1 episodes released on DVD by Warner Home Video in 2009, continuing the CGI series' first-year story arcs across the early Clone Wars. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 1 ran 22 episodes covering campaigns on Christophsis, Teth, Ryloth, and Geonosis, among other worlds, before the full-season box set collected everything onto four discs.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 1, Volume 4
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: The final individually-released Season 1 DVD volume, rounding out the CGI series' debut year on disc ahead of the complete-season box set. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 1 introduced core recurring characters like Asajj Ventress, Captain Rex, and Ahsoka Tano, all of whom became central to the franchise's future storytelling well beyond this series.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 2, Volume 1
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: First individually-released Season 2 DVD volume, collecting the opening four episodes of the show's second year (released December 6, 2010), which continued the war across new fronts including Rodia and the hunt for bounty hunter Cad Bane.
trivia: Season 2 is generally considered a turning point for the series, expanding the scope of the war and deepening its ensemble cast, which is reflected in its higher IMDb rating compared to Season 1.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 2, Volume 2
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: A further batch of Season 2 episodes released on DVD by Warner Home Video, continuing the second year's expanded storylines across the galaxy. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 2's individual-volume DVDs were released piecemeal through late 2010 and into 2011, alongside the complete four-disc "Season Two" box set that Warner Home Video issued on October 26, 2010.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 2, Volume 3
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: A further batch of Season 2 episodes released on DVD by Warner Home Video, continuing the second year's storylines. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 2 introduced fan-favorite bounty hunter Cad Bane and expanded the roles of Padme Amidala and the Jedi Council in the political side of the war.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 2, Volume 4
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
blurb: Final individually-released Season 2 DVD volume, rounding out the show's second year on disc. Exact episode lineup for this specific volume could not be independently confirmed.
trivia: Season 2 closed with a multi-episode arc on Mortis exploring the mystical Force-wielding "Father, Son, and Daughter," a storyline that had an outsized influence on later Star Wars canon.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Clone Commandos
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer)
notes: 4 episodes
blurb: A Walmart-exclusive Season 1 compilation (released September 15, 2009) collecting the clone-trooper-centric arc "Rookies," "Storm Over Ryloth," "Innocents of Ryloth," and "Liberty on Ryloth" — following rookie clones Fives, Echo, Cutup, and Droidbait, and the campaign to liberate Ryloth from Separatist occupation.
trivia: "Rookies" introduced clone troopers Echo and Fives, who went on to become recurring fan-favorite characters throughout the rest of the series and later Star Wars: The Bad Batch.

title: Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion
creator: Dave Filoni (exec. producer); Steward Lee (dir.)
blurb: Feature-length pilot for Star Wars Rebels, set five years before A New Hope on the Outer Rim world of Lothal. Street thief Ezra Bridger falls in with the crew of the starship Ghost — Kanan Jarrus, Hera Syndulla, Sabine Wren, Zeb Orrelios, and the droid Chopper — as they carry out small acts of rebellion against the Empire.
trivia: The show's character and vehicle designs were deliberately modeled on Ralph McQuarrie's original concept art for the classic trilogy, a stylistic direction championed by executive producer Dave Filoni.

title: Star Wars: Droids - The Animated Adventures
creator: Ben Burtt & Peter Sauder (developed by); Nelvana (animation studio)
notes: 2 films
blurb: Double-feature DVD (released November 23, 2004) compiling episodes of the 1985 Droids animated series into two edited TV movies, "The Pirates and the Prince" and "Treasure of the Hidden Planet." Follows R2-D2 and C-3PO through a string of adventures with various masters years before serving Luke Skywalker.
trivia: The show's own marketing described its adventures as taking place roughly 15 years before R2-D2 and C-3PO meet Luke Skywalker in A New Hope.

title: Star Wars: Ewoks - The Animated Adventures
creator: Paul Dini & Bob Carrau (developed by); Nelvana (animation studio)
notes: 2 films
blurb: Double-feature DVD (released November 23, 2004) compiling episodes of the 1985-86 Ewoks animated series into two edited TV movies, "The Haunted Village" and "Tales from the Endor Woods." Follows a young Wicket W. Warrick and the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village in the years before Return of the Jedi.
trivia: For its second season, Lucasfilm brought production in-house and gave the show a new title sequence using early CGI animation — an unusual choice for a mid-1980s Saturday-morning cartoon.
inUniverseDate: ~3 ABY (Legends placement, preceding the Battle of Endor)

title: Star Wars Ewoks Adventures: Caravan of Courage & Battle for Endor
creator: John Korty (dir., Caravan of Courage); Jim & Ken Wheat (dir., Battle for Endor)
notes: Double feature, DVD reissue of the two Ewok TV movies
blurb: 2004 double-sided DVD reissue pairing both 1980s Ewok TV movies, Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure and Ewoks: The Battle for Endor, presented in their original 1.33:1 broadcast aspect ratio with no bonus features.
trivia: The disc itself is double-sided, with one film mastered on each side rather than spread across two separate discs.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars - Volume Two
creator: Genndy Tartakovsky (dir.)
notes: 2003 Genndy Tartakovsky micro-series
blurb: DVD (released December 6, 2005) collecting "Season Three" (Chapters 21-25) of Genndy Tartakovsky's stylized 2D micro-series, depicting General Grievous's rise, the fall of Coruscant's shield, and Anakin Skywalker's descent toward the iconic Chapter 25 cliffhanger that leads directly into Revenge of the Sith.
rating: IMDb ~7.7/10 average (no single series rating on IMDb; individual chapters range roughly 7.4-8.1)
trivia: Chapter 25's climactic space battle and Anakin's capture by General Grievous set up the exact opening scene of Revenge of the Sith, making this the direct on-screen bridge between the two.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars - Volume One
creator: Genndy Tartakovsky (dir.)
notes: 2003 Genndy Tartakovsky micro-series
blurb: DVD (released March 22, 2005) collecting Seasons One and Two (Chapters 1-20) of Genndy Tartakovsky's Emmy-winning 2D micro-series, told in short vignettes covering the opening battles of the Clone Wars, Anakin Skywalker's rise toward Jedi Knighthood, and the introduction of Sith assassin Asajj Ventress.
trivia: Fresh off Samurai Jack, Genndy Tartakovsky pitched the micro-series' bold, minimalist 2D animation style specifically to set it apart visually from the CGI prequel films it bridges.

title: Phineas and Ferb: Star Wars
creator: Dan Povenmire & Jeff "Swampy" Marsh (creators)
blurb: Hour-long Disney XD crossover special reimagining the plot of A New Hope with the Phineas and Ferb cast: Candace becomes Princess Leia, Doofenshmirtz plays a Darth Vader analog, and Perry the Platypus is recast as a Kenobi-style mentor. The DVD also includes several bonus regular-series episodes.
trivia: Lucasfilm gave its blessing for the crossover, and Star Wars sound designer Ben Burtt contributed some of the special's sound effects; it is treated as a lighthearted parody outside the official Star Wars canon or Legends continuity.
inUniverseDate: N/A — comedic alternate-universe crossover loosely paralleling A New Hope (~0 BBY)

title: Robot Chicken: Star Wars
creator: Seth Green & Matthew Senreich (creators/dir.)
blurb: Stop-motion sketch-comedy special from Adult Swim's Robot Chicken (originally aired June 2007, DVD released July 22, 2008), parodying moments across the entire Star Wars saga through dozens of rapid-fire skits.
trivia: Several original-trilogy actors — including Mark Hamill, Billy Dee Williams, and Ahmed Best — voiced parody versions of their own characters for the special.
inUniverseDate: N/A — comedic parody anthology spanning the entire saga

title: Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II
creator: Seth Green & Matthew Senreich (creators/dir.)
notes: Limited edition
blurb: Second Robot Chicken Star Wars stop-motion special (originally aired 2008, DVD released July 21, 2009), again lampooning the saga with an emphasis on the prequel trilogy through dozens of quick-cut parody sketches.
trivia: This special earned Robot Chicken a 2009 Primetime Emmy nomination for Outstanding Animated Program (Programming Less Than One Hour).

title: Robot Chicken: Star Wars III
creator: Seth Green & Matthew Senreich (creators/dir.)
blurb: Third and final entry in the Robot Chicken Star Wars stop-motion trilogy (originally aired 2010, DVD released July 12, 2011), wrapping up the saga-wide parody format with sketches spanning the prequel and original trilogies plus the wider Expanded Universe.
trivia: Lucasfilm gave Seth Green's team unusually broad creative latitude, making the Robot Chicken specials some of the few officially licensed pieces of Star Wars media built around raunchy, adult-oriented humor.

title: Fanboys
creator: Kyle Newman (director)
blurb: A group of lifelong Star Wars fans road-trips across the country to break into Skywalker Ranch and watch an early screening of The Phantom Menace before one of them succumbs to cancer. The 2009 comedy stars Sam Huntington, Chris Marquette, Dan Fogler, and Jay Baruchel, with cameos from Kevin Smith, Carrie Fisher, and William Shatner.
trivia: The film sat on the shelf for years amid studio disputes over cutting a character's terminal cancer subplot; an organized fan campaign helped pressure the studio into restoring it before release.
inUniverseDate: N/A — real-world comedy film, not set within the Star Wars story

title: Elstree 1976
creator: Jon Spira (director)
notes: Documentary
blurb: A documentary profiling the little-known actors and extras — stormtroopers, background rebels, and other bit players — who worked on the original 1977 Star Wars at Elstree Studios. It explores how a few days or weeks of anonymous work on a low-budget sci-fi film reshaped their lives decades later.
trivia: The title refers to Elstree Studios in Hertfordshire, England, where the original Star Wars was shot in 1976; several interviewees only grasped how significant their tiny roles had become to fans decades after filming.
inUniverseDate: N/A — real-world documentary about the making of the original 1977 film, not part of the in-story timeline

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace / The Empire Strikes Out
creator: David Scott (The Padawan Menace); Guy Vasilovich (The Empire Strikes Out)
notes: 2 animated adventures
blurb: A double-feature DVD pairing two LEGO Star Wars animated specials: 'The Padawan Menace' (2011), where young Anakin Skywalker is left babysitting a group of unruly Jedi younglings, and 'The Empire Strikes Out' (2012), a comedic riff on The Empire Strikes Back in which Darth Vader battles a nasty head cold instead of the Rebellion.
rating: IMDb 7.0/10 for The Padawan Menace; The Empire Strikes Out is lightly rated with only a small number of IMDb votes
trivia: The Empire Strikes Out swaps the Rebellion's fight for survival with Vader sneezing his way through Imperial equipment, playing the entire Hoth battle for slapstick rather than stakes.
inUniverseDate: The Padawan Menace ~22 BBY (Clone Wars era); The Empire Strikes Out ~0 ABY (parallels The Empire Strikes Back)

title: LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales - Vol. 2
creator: Jake Blais and John McCormack (creators)
blurb: Volume 2 of the five-part LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales miniseries, continuing C-3PO and R2-D2's comedic, LEGO-ified retelling of the saga to a captive audience in Jabba's palace. This volume covers the miniseries' later chapters, including riffs on the Death Star trench run and galactic civil war.
rating: IMDb 7.4/10 (series overall; a few hundred votes)
trivia: Droid Tales frames the entire six-film saga as a story told by C-3PO and R2-D2, timed to launch around Force Friday merchandise ahead of The Force Awakens' theatrical release later in 2015.
inUniverseDate: Framing story ~4 ABY, shortly after Return of the Jedi, with flashback chapters spanning 32 BBY–4 ABY

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures - Complete Season One
creator: Bill Motz and Bob Roth (creators)
blurb: Season one of the LEGO Star Wars animated series following the Freemaker siblings — Rowan, Zander, and Kordi — as they salvage starships on the junk planet Ruusan and get swept into an Imperial-era hunt for ancient Kyber saber crystals. Set shortly after Return of the Jedi, it introduced an entirely original family of protagonists rather than adapting saga characters.
trivia: The Freemaker Adventures was the first LEGO Star Wars animated project built around wholly original lead characters instead of retelling stories starring existing saga heroes.
inUniverseDate: ~4-5 ABY, shortly after the Battle of Endor

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures - Complete Season Two
creator: Bill Motz and Bob Roth (creators)
blurb: Season two of LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures continues the family's adventures as Rowan grows into his Force sensitivity while the crew clashes with new Imperial and criminal threats. This was the series' final season, wrapping up the Freemaker siblings' story.
trivia: The Freemaker Adventures was not renewed past its second season, making this DVD set the closing chapter of the Freemaker siblings' story.
inUniverseDate: ~5 ABY, following directly from Season One

title: LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales - Vol. 1
creator: Jake Blais and John McCormack (creators)
blurb: Volume 1 of the LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales miniseries, opening the five-part story as C-3PO and R2-D2 spin comedic LEGO retellings of the saga's earlier chapters — including the Clone Wars and the fall of the Jedi — while trying to escape captivity in Jabba's palace.
rating: IMDb 7.4/10 (series overall; a few hundred votes)
trivia: The five-episode miniseries originally aired weekly on Disney XD in mid-2015 before being compiled onto these two DVD volumes.
inUniverseDate: Framing story ~4 ABY; flashback chapters largely covering 22 BBY–19 BBY (Clone Wars/Order 66 era)

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles
creator: Michael Hegner (director)
notes: The Phantom Clone / Menace of the Sith
blurb: Collects the first two chapters of the LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles trilogy: 'The Phantom Clone,' in which General Grievous lures Yoda away from the Jedi Temple so Count Dooku can steal Padawan lightsabers to create Sith clones, and 'Menace of the Sith,' continuing the young Padawans' battle against Dooku's clone army.
trivia: The Yoda Chronicles moved LEGO Star Wars away from standalone holiday specials toward a serialized trilogy format, a structure later reused for The New Yoda Chronicles and Droid Tales.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The New Yoda Chronicles - Vol. 1
creator: Martin Skov (director); Michael Price (writer)
blurb: Volume 1 of The New Yoda Chronicles, continuing directly from The Yoda Chronicles trilogy with short animated segments that aired on Disney XD through 2014 before being compiled onto DVD, following the young Padawans and Yoda as they contend with Dooku's clone forces.
trivia: The New Yoda Chronicles episodes originally aired in short bursts on Disney XD between May and November 2014 before being packaged onto these two DVD volumes.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The New Yoda Chronicles - Vol. 2
creator: Martin Skov (director); Michael Price (writer)
blurb: Volume 2 of The New Yoda Chronicles, wrapping up the story threads from the trilogy's earlier chapters as the young Padawans face escalating threats from Dooku and General Grievous late in the Clone Wars.
trivia: This second volume closed out the Yoda Chronicles storyline that began with the Walmart-exclusive DVD release of The Phantom Clone and Menace of the Sith in 2014.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace
creator: David Scott (director)
notes: Includes exclusive minifigure
blurb: A standalone Blu-ray/DVD combo release of the 2011 LEGO Star Wars animated special, in which Anakin Skywalker is left in charge of a group of unruly Jedi younglings at the Jedi Temple and must fend off an attack while babysitting.
trivia: This release included an exclusive LEGO Young Han Solo minifigure never sold in any physical brick set, making it a sought-after collectible on its own.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
creator: Dave Filoni (director)
notes: 2008 animated theatrical film, Captain Rex cover
blurb: The theatrical animated film that launched the Star Wars: The Clone Wars TV series, following Anakin Skywalker and his new Padawan Ahsoka Tano as they attempt to rescue Jabba the Hutt's kidnapped son to secure a hyperspace route through Hutt space. It served as a feature-length pilot for the long-running series.
trivia: The film holds the lowest Rotten Tomatoes score of any theatrically released Star Wars project, but it introduced Ahsoka Tano, who went on to become one of the franchise's most popular characters across multiple series.
inUniverseDate: ~22 BBY, early in the Clone Wars

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
creator: Dave Filoni (director)
notes: 2008 animated theatrical film, Anakin cover - possible duplicate/alt cover of IMG_9846, confirm
blurb: The theatrical animated film that launched the Star Wars: The Clone Wars TV series, following Anakin Skywalker and his new Padawan Ahsoka Tano as they attempt to rescue Jabba the Hutt's kidnapped son to secure a hyperspace route through Hutt space. This copy appears to share the same film as the Captain Rex cover entry, possibly an alternate cover printing — recommend confirming whether this is a true duplicate before finalizing the catalog.
trivia: Warner Home Video issued this film on Blu-ray with multiple alternate cover variants featuring different characters, which is likely the source of this apparent duplicate.
inUniverseDate: ~22 BBY, early in the Clone Wars

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Complete Season One
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: The complete first season of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, which introduced Ahsoka Tano and expanded the war between the Republic and the Separatists across dozens of new worlds, characters, and campaigns not seen in the films.
trivia: Season one was released on Blu-ray as a three-disc digibook set with extensive concept-art galleries, reflecting Lucasfilm's early push to treat the series as a prestige production rather than a simple kids' show.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Complete Season Two
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: Season two of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, notable for its multi-episode arc exploring Boba Fett's origin story and his quest for revenge against Mace Windu for his father Jango Fett's death.
trivia: The season's Boba Fett arc ('Death Trap,' 'R2 Come Home,' and 'Lethal Trackdown') gave the bounty hunter his first substantial characterization since the original trilogy.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Complete Season Three
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: Season three of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, which expanded the Nightsister and Mother Talzin storyline, introduced Savage Opress, and continued to deepen Ahsoka Tano's development as Anakin's Padawan.
trivia: This season's introduction of Savage Opress as Count Dooku's new apprentice set up the character's eventual role as Darth Maul's brother and enforcer in later seasons.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Complete Season Four
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: Season four of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, featuring the 'Deception' arc in which Obi-Wan Kenobi fakes his own death to go undercover as bounty hunter Rako Hardeen, plus arcs deepening the mystery of the Umbaran War and clone trooper Fives' storyline.
trivia: The 'Deception' arc's Rako Hardeen disguise storyline planted early seeds for the show's later exploration of the clones' Order 66 programming.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Complete Season Five
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: Season five of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, featuring the 'Brothers' and 'Revenge' arc that reintroduced Darth Maul (revealed to have survived Obi-Wan's duel in The Phantom Menace) alongside Savage Opress, and the Onderon rebellion arc introducing Saw Gerrera.
trivia: This season's surprise revelation that Darth Maul survived his apparent death in The Phantom Menace was one of the show's most significant retcons, reshaping the character's legacy for the rest of the franchise.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Lost Missions (Season Six)
creator: Dave Filoni (supervising director)
blurb: The unaired sixth-season episodes of Star Wars: The Clone Wars, released after the show's cancellation following Disney's acquisition of Lucasfilm. Includes the clone-trooper-focused arc exploring Order 66's origins and Yoda's mystical 'Destiny' arc journeying into the Force.
trivia: These 13 episodes were completed before the series' cancellation and released direct-to-Netflix in March 2014, then on Blu-ray/DVD that November, rather than airing on television.

title: Star Wars Rebels - Complete Season One
creator: Dave Filoni (executive producer/supervising director); Simon Kinberg and Greg Weisman (executive producers)
blurb: The first season of Star Wars Rebels, introducing the crew of the starship Ghost — Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, Hera Syndulla, Sabine Wren, Zeb Orrelios, and the droid Chopper — as they carry out small acts of rebellion against the Empire on Lothal, years before the events of A New Hope.
trivia: Season one closes with the reveal of Darth Vader taking a direct interest in the fledgling rebel cell, tying the show explicitly into the larger saga's villain.

title: Star Wars Rebels - Complete Season Two
creator: Dave Filoni (executive producer/supervising director)
blurb: Season two of Star Wars Rebels, which brings back Ahsoka Tano and reveals her fateful confrontation with her former master, now Darth Vader, while introducing Grand Inquisitor rivals and expanding the growing rebellion against the Empire.
trivia: Season two's finale, 'Twilight of the Apprentice,' features Ahsoka Tano's climactic lightsaber duel with Darth Vader, confirming on-screen that her old master survived as the Sith Lord.

title: Star Wars Rebels - Complete Season Three
creator: Dave Filoni (executive producer/supervising director)
blurb: Season three of Star Wars Rebels introduces Grand Admiral Thrawn, a brilliant Imperial tactician adapted into canon from the Star Wars Legends novels, as the rebels' most dangerous adversary yet, while Ezra Bridger grapples with the pull of the dark side.
trivia: Grand Admiral Thrawn's introduction marked one of the biggest Legends-to-canon revivals in Disney-era Star Wars, voiced by Lars Mikkelsen and later reused in live-action for Ahsoka (2023).

title: Star Wars Rebels - Complete Season Four
creator: Dave Filoni (executive producer/supervising director)
blurb: The fourth and final season of Star Wars Rebels, culminating in the liberation of Lothal from Imperial control and Ezra Bridger's disappearance alongside Grand Admiral Thrawn, with an epilogue set after Return of the Jedi.
trivia: The series finale's post-Return of the Jedi epilogue, showing Sabine Wren and Ahsoka Tano setting out to find Ezra, directly set up plot threads later picked up in the live-action Ahsoka series.
inUniverseDate: ~1 BBY-1 ABY, with an epilogue ~4-5 ABY

title: Star Wars: A New Hope - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack (Special Edition)
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: Special edition
blurb: This 1997 RCA Victor 2-CD remastered release expanded the original 1977 John Williams score with previously unreleased cues and a 32-page booklet, timed to the theatrical Special Edition re-release. Highlights include the 20th Century Fox Fanfare, Princess Leia's Theme, and the Cantina Band numbers. It remains the score widely credited with reviving the symphonic Hollywood film score tradition.
rating: AllMusic review (James Christopher Monger); AlbumOfTheYear user score 88/100 based on 333 ratings for the John Williams score
trivia: Williams recorded the score with the London Symphony Orchestra in just eight days in March 1977, and its commercial success helped popularize the symphonic film score at a time when pop-song soundtracks dominated.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: Michael Giacchino (composer)
blurb: Michael Giacchino stepped in during post-production, reportedly composing the score for the first Star Wars anthology film in under a month. The soundtrack weaves in John Williams' established leitmotifs (including a haunting statement of the Imperial March in "Krennic's Aspirations") alongside new material for Jyn Erso and the Rogue One squad. It was released by Walt Disney Records on December 16, 2016.
rating: AlbumOfTheYear user score 75/100 based on 48 ratings
trivia: Giacchino had roughly four and a half weeks to write and record the score after replacing original composer Alexandre Desplat, one of the shortest turnarounds of his career.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack (Special Edition)
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: 2-disc
blurb: The 1997 RCA Victor 2-disc remaster of Williams' 1980 score, expanded with additional cues and packaged with Special Edition trilogy poster art. It introduces two of the franchise's most iconic themes, the Imperial March and Yoda's Theme, and is frequently cited by fans and critics as the strongest of the original trilogy scores.
rating: AllMusic review (Tavia Hobart); AlbumOfTheYear user score 88/100 based on 216 ratings
trivia: The Imperial March, now one of the most recognizable pieces of film music ever written, did not appear anywhere in the first Star Wars film — it was created from scratch for Empire to give Vader a distinct musical identity.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack (Special Edition)
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: 2-disc
blurb: This RCA Victor 2-disc remastered Special Edition release (August 26, 1997) restores and expands Williams' 1983 score for the trilogy's original finale, including Luke and Leia's theme, the Emperor's theme, and the Ewok celebration finale. It notably omits the disco-tinged "Yub Nub" celebration song from the theatrical cut in favor of Williams' orchestral material.
rating: AllMusic review (Steven McDonald); AlbumOfTheYear user score 85/100 based on 122 ratings
trivia: The album's closing "Ewok Celebration and Finale" is the last original-trilogy cue Williams wrote before returning to the saga sixteen years later for The Phantom Menace.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Williams (composer)
blurb: Williams' return to the saga after a decade away, released by Walt Disney Records on December 18, 2015. It introduces new themes for Rey, Kylo Ren, and the Resistance while weaving in classic motifs, and earned Williams his 50th Academy Award nomination and a Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack.
rating: AllMusic review (Neil Z. Yeung); AlbumOfTheYear user score 71/100 based on 81 ratings
trivia: At 83 years old during production, Williams stated this would likely be his final Star Wars score before ultimately returning for four more entries in the saga.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes (Cantina Band CD Single)
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: Cantina Band single, A New Hope Special Edition
blurb: A promotional CD single released by RCA in November 1997, pairing "Cantina Band" and "Cantina Band #2" as performed in-story by the fictional Bith band Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes. Both tracks were pulled from the 1997 A New Hope Special Edition sessions recorded at Anvil Studios, Denham, England.
trivia: The alien jizz-band material was written by Williams to sound deliberately unlike traditional Hollywood scoring, giving the Mos Eisley cantina scene a lived-in, otherworldly bar-band feel.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Meco - Star Wars and Other Galactic Funk
creator: Meco (artist)
notes: 1977 disco album
blurb: Producer/arranger Domenico "Meco" Monardo's disco reimagining of John Williams' Star Wars themes, built around a sprawling 15-minute "Star Wars Theme/Cantina Band" medley. Released on Millennium Records in mid-1977, it became a surprise commercial phenomenon, hitting #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and going platinum.
rating: AllMusic 4/5 stars (score of 80); AlbumOfTheYear user score 80/100 based on 26 ratings
trivia: The single edit of the title medley hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in October 1977, making it one of the best-selling instrumental singles of the disco era and reportedly outselling the film's own official soundtrack album for a period.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Williams (composer)
blurb: Williams' first Star Wars score in sixteen years, released by Sony Classical on May 4, 1999. It introduces Anakin's Theme and the choral "Duel of the Fates," which became one of the most enduringly popular pieces in the entire saga and was later reused as recurring musical shorthand for the prequel-era conflict.
rating: AllMusic review (Steven McDonald); AlbumOfTheYear user score 81/100 based on 136 ratings
trivia: "Duel of the Fates" was inspired by a Welsh translation of a stanza from the Gaelic poem "The Battle of the Trees" and was recorded with a 120-voice choir singing invented pseudo-Sanskrit lyrics.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: Joel McNeely (composer)
notes: Joel McNeely score, Enhanced CD
blurb: Composed by Joel McNeely for the multimedia Shadows of the Empire project (novel, video game, comics) that filled the story gap between Empire and Jedi, this Varese Sarabande release was recorded with the 90-piece Royal Scottish National Orchestra and a 150-voice chorus in Glasgow. It marked a rare instance of a large-scale orchestral score for a non-film Star Wars story, deliberately written in the style of Williams' saga scores.
trivia: This was the first substantial Star Wars orchestral score not composed by John Williams, and McNeely intentionally echoed Williams' leitmotif technique to keep it stylistically consistent with the films.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi - The Max Rebo Band: Jedi Rocks (CD Single)
creator: Jerry Hey (composer)
notes: Special Edition
blurb: A promotional RCA Victor CD single from November 1997 featuring "Jedi Rocks," the CGI musical number performed in-story by Sy Snootles, Max Rebo, and Droopy McCool that replaced "Lapti Nek" in the 1997 Return of the Jedi Special Edition. The tune was composed by Jerry Hey rather than John Williams, giving it a distinct pop/funk flavor compared to the orchestral score.
trivia: "Jedi Rocks" was a deliberate replacement for the original 1983 "Lapti Nek" number, and its CGI-animated Max Rebo Band performance became one of the more divisive changes George Lucas made for the 1997 Special Editions.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Williams (composer)
blurb: Released by Sony Classical on April 23, 2002, this score introduces "Across the Stars," the sweeping Anakin/Padmé love theme, alongside darker material foreshadowing the Clone Wars and the rise of the Empire. It was recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra and London Voices.
rating: AlbumOfTheYear critic score 60/100 (1 review); user score 76/100 based on 108 ratings
trivia: "Across the Stars" is structurally modeled on Williams' own Empire-era love theme for Han and Leia, intentionally echoing it to foreshadow the tragic arc of Anakin and Padmé's relationship.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: Kevin Kiner (composer)
notes: Kevin Kiner
blurb: Kevin Kiner's score for the 2008 animated theatrical film that launched the Star Wars: The Clone Wars television series, released by Sony Classical/Walt Disney Records in August 2008. It incorporates John Williams' established themes while introducing new material for Anakin, Ahsoka, and the CGI-era Clone Wars conflict, performed by the Prague Philharmonic Orchestra under Nic Raine.
trivia: This was the first Star Wars screen composition not written by John Williams to be released theatrically, and Kiner would go on to score all six seasons of the subsequent animated series plus several spin-off shows.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Williams (composer)
blurb: Released by Sony Classical on May 3, 2005, this score closes out the prequel trilogy with "Battle of the Heroes" (the Anakin/Obi-Wan duel theme), Anakin's fall to the dark side, and a final reprise linking directly into the original trilogy's "A New Hope and End Credits." It is widely regarded by critics and fans as one of Williams' finest achievements in the saga.
rating: AllMusic review (Rob Theakston); AlbumOfTheYear user score 88/100 based on 208 ratings
trivia: The closing track deliberately reprises music from the 1977 original film to musically bridge the prequel and original trilogies, ending the six-film saga (as it existed in 2005) on the same fanfare it began with.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Solo: A Star Wars Story - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Powell (composer)
notes: John Powell
blurb: John Powell's score for the 2018 Han Solo origin film, released by Walt Disney Records on May 25, 2018. Powell incorporates John Williams' original themes (including a Williams-composed "The Adventures of Han" theme) while building his own material for young Han, Qi'ra, and Chewbacca. Powell won the International Film Music Critics Association's Score of the Year award for the work.
trivia: John Williams came out of retirement from active scoring duties just to compose the brief but memorable new Han Solo theme, "The Adventures of Han," which Powell then wove throughout the rest of the score.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Corellian Edition
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: Compilation featuring music from all six episodes
blurb: A promotional compilation disc pulling highlight cues from Williams' scores across all six Star Wars saga films (Episodes I-VI), originally distributed as a Target-exclusive bonus packaged with the Revenge of the Sith soundtrack around its 2005 release. It later circulated as a standalone collectible among soundtrack completists.
trivia: As a retailer-exclusive promotional giveaway rather than a standard commercial release, this disc was never assigned its own catalog sales run, making original sealed copies a minor collectible among Star Wars soundtrack completists.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
creator: John Williams (composer)
notes: Sealed
blurb: Released by Walt Disney Records on December 15, 2017, Williams' score for the second sequel-trilogy film expands on Rey's and Kylo Ren's themes from The Force Awakens and introduces new material for Rose Tico, Vice Admiral Holdo, and the Canto Bight sequence. It earned Williams Oscar and Grammy nominations.
trivia: This score gave John Williams his fifth-consecutive Academy Award nomination for a Star Wars film, extending a nomination streak for the saga that stretches back to the original 1977 film.
inUniverseDate: N/A (real-world music release, no in-story timeline placement)

title: Star Wars: Dark Forces - The Collector's Trilogy
creator: John Whitman (dramatization writer, based on novellas by William C. Dietz)
notes: Sealed audio drama CD box set: Soldier for the Empire, Rebel Agent, Jedi Knight
blurb: A 6-CD, six-hour full-cast audio drama trilogy dramatizing Kyle Katarn's journey from Imperial Academy graduate to Rebel operative to Jedi Knight. Adapted by John Whitman from William C. Dietz's Dark Forces novellas, directed by Peter Moore, and scored with music drawn from John Williams' original film cues. Comprises three self-contained dramas: Soldier for the Empire, Rebel Agent, and Jedi Knight.
rating: Goodreads: 3.60/5 (82 ratings, 12 reviews), for John Whitman's 'The Collector's Trilogy' edition
trivia: The dramatization also aired on NPR and reused a musical score sourced from John Williams' original trilogy recordings rather than a newly composed soundtrack.
inUniverseDate: Approx. 5 BBY-1 ABY (spans Kyle Katarn's Imperial service through the events dramatized in the Dark Forces and Jedi Knight video games)

title: Star Wars Trading Card Game: Attack of the Clones
creator: Wizards of the Coast (publisher)
notes: Sealed starter/two-player game box
blurb: The two-player starter box for the debut set of Wizards of the Coast's Star Wars Trading Card Game, released in April 2002 to coincide with Attack of the Clones. Contains preconstructed 30-card Light Side and Dark Side decks, rulebook, and play accessories designed to teach the game head-to-head, plus access to a 180-card base set (60 rare/60 uncommon/60 common).
rating: BoardGameGeek: Geek Rating approx. 5.9/10 (low vote count; a niche/out-of-print CCG entry)
trivia: Attack of the Clones was the first Star Wars TCG set published by Wizards of the Coast after it took over the license from Decipher Inc., whose earlier Star Wars Customizable Card Game had ceased production in 2001.
inUniverseDate: N/A - collectible trading card game, not narrative story content

title: Star Wars Trivial Pursuit DVD Game: Saga Edition
creator: Hasbro (publisher)
notes: DVD-based trivia board game
blurb: A Star Wars-themed edition of Trivial Pursuit for 2-4 players/teams, combining a traditional trivia board and 1,800 question cards with two bonus DVDs holding 700 additional video-based questions and film clips spanning all six Saga films through Revenge of the Sith. Released by Hasbro/Parker Brothers in 2005 to coincide with Episode III.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (BoardGameGeek listing exists but returned no surfaced aggregate score during research)
trivia: The set was timed to release alongside Revenge of the Sith in 2005 and was one of the first Trivial Pursuit editions built around DVD-based video questions rather than cards alone.
inUniverseDate: N/A - trivia board game, not narrative story content

title: The Complete Star Wars Trilogy: The Original Radio Dramas
creator: Brian Daley (writer; John Whitman contributed rewrites on Return of the Jedi)
notes: NPR radio dramatizations, complete boxed trilogy: 29 episodes on 15 compact discs (confirmed from box text).
blurb: Collects NPR's full-cast radio dramatizations of the original trilogy: Star Wars (1981), The Empire Strikes Back (1983), and Return of the Jedi (1996), scripted by Brian Daley and directed by John Madden. Expands on the films with additional character and story material suited to the audio format, using surviving cast members including Mark Hamill, Anthony Daniels, and Billy Dee Williams.
trivia: When the original A New Hope radio dramatization first aired on NPR in 1981, it generated the largest listener response in the network's history to that point - about 50,000 letters and calls in a single week, with a subsequent 40% jump in NPR listenership.
inUniverseDate: Approx. 0 BBY-4 ABY (dramatizes the events of A New Hope through Return of the Jedi)

title: Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion - Das Original-Hörspiel zur TV-Serie
creator: Gabriele Bingenheimer (adaptation); Kiddinx/Universal Music Germany (producer)
notes: German-language radio-play adaptation, not a music score. Deviation note: input research guidance suggested Legends/EU status for this batch's audio dramas by default, but Star Wars Rebels is 2014-era Disney canon, not Legends - canon field set accordingly based on verified research rather than the default assumption.
blurb: German-language full-cast Hörspiel (audio drama) adaptation of the Star Wars Rebels pilot TV movie 'Spark of Rebellion,' adapted by Gabriele Bingenheimer with narrator/cast led by Hanns Jörg Krumpholz. Released December 19, 2014 by Kiddinx/Universal Music as the first entry in a German audio-drama series that eventually adapted the show's first 35 episodes through 2017.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found (no BoardGameGeek/Goodreads-equivalent aggregate located for this German-market audio release; only individual retailer listings found)
trivia: This release continues Germany's long-running Star Wars Hörspiel tradition and was the opening entry in a multi-year series that adapted dozens of Star Wars Rebels episodes into German audio dramas between 2014 and 2017.
inUniverseDate: 5 BBY (the Star Wars Rebels pilot 'Spark of Rebellion' is set in 5 BBY, on the planet Lothal)

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
creator: Donald F. Glut
notes: Novelization of Episode V, released by Del Rey before the film's May 1980 theatrical debut.
blurb: The Rebellion, scattered after the destruction of the Death Star, regroups on the ice world of Hoth only to be routed by a massive Imperial assault. As Han Solo and Leia Organa flee into an asteroid field with Vader's fleet in pursuit, Luke Skywalker travels to a swamp planet to complete his Jedi training under the reclusive Master Yoda. A confrontation in the clouds of Bespin brings Luke face to face with Darth Vader and a truth that will shatter everything he believes about himself.
trivia: Because it hit shelves in April 1980, weeks ahead of the film's May premiere, many fans first learned that Vader was Luke's father from reading the book rather than seeing it on screen.

title: Star Wars: Tales of the Bounty Hunters
creator: ed. Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Anthology giving backstories to the bounty hunters Vader assembles aboard his Star Destroyer in The Empire Strikes Back.
blurb: Six bounty hunters stand assembled before Darth Vader, each summoned to track down the Millennium Falcon. This collection peels back their masks and mystery, following Boba Fett, Dengar, Bossk, IG-88, and Zuckuss and 4-LOM through jobs, rivalries, and grudges that stretch across the galaxy. Every story circles back to the same fateful moment on the Executor's bridge, revealing why each hunter answered the call.
trivia: Each of the anthology's five stories was written by a different author (including Dave Wolverton and Kathy Tyers) and centers on one of the bounty hunters glimpsed only briefly aboard Vader's Star Destroyer in The Empire Strikes Back.

title: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire
creator: Steve Perry
notes: Bridges the gap between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi; part of a multimedia project spanning novel, video game, comics, and toys.
blurb: With Han Solo frozen in carbonite and delivered to Jabba the Hutt, Leia Organa and Lando Calrissian scramble to track him down while the ruthless crime lord Prince Xizor maneuvers to seize control of the Empire's underworld and eliminate Luke Skywalker for good. Caught between Xizor's schemes and Vader's wrath, the Rebellion's most valuable pawns must survive a game with no clear rules. It is a story of shifting loyalties playing out entirely in the shadow of the Death Star's reconstruction.
trivia: Shadows of the Empire was a deliberate experiment in crossmedia storytelling, released simultaneously as a novel, N64/PC video game, comic miniseries, toy line, and soundtrack album, filling a story gap that exists between two films rather than adapting one.

title: Star Wars: The Bounty Hunter Wars: The Mandalorian Armor
creator: K. W. Jeter
notes: Book 1 of the Bounty Hunter Wars trilogy.
blurb: Freshly clawed out of the belly of the Sarlacc, Boba Fett is a shell of the hunter he once was, and rivals sense weakness. A cunning pretender has stolen his identity and his iconic armor to seize control of the fractured Bounty Hunters' Guild, forcing Fett into an uneasy alliance to reclaim what is his. Old grudges resurface as former partners and enemies alike circle the wounded legend, each with their own price on his head.
trivia: Author K. W. Jeter was primarily known as a cyberpunk novelist (he coined the term 'steampunk') before taking on this trilogy, giving the series a notably grittier, noir-inflected tone than most Star Wars fiction of its era.

title: Star Wars: The Bounty Hunter Wars: Slave Ship
creator: K. W. Jeter
notes: Book 2 of the Bounty Hunter Wars trilogy.
blurb: The Bounty Hunters' Guild is in open chaos, and a staggering bounty on a rogue former stormtrooper sends every hunter in the galaxy scrambling for the prize. To chase it, Boba Fett must abandon his beloved Slave I, leaving him more vulnerable than he has been in years. As betrayals mount within the Guild's ranks, Fett is forced to decide how far he will go to protect his reputation and his life.
trivia: The plot turns on Boba Fett voluntarily giving up his signature ship, Slave I, for most of the book, a rare instance of the character separated from one of his most iconic pieces of equipment.

title: Star Wars: The Bounty Hunter Wars: Hard Merchandise
creator: K. W. Jeter
notes: Book 3 of the Bounty Hunter Wars trilogy.
blurb: With the Bounty Hunters' Guild collapsing into factional warfare, Boba Fett closes in on the identity thief who has spent months impersonating him and dismantling his standing among his peers. Old allies, new enemies, and the New Republic's own agents converge as the true scope of the conspiracy against Fett comes into focus. The trilogy's final confrontation forces Fett to reassert, once and for all, exactly who he is.
trivia: Hard Merchandise closes out the Bounty Hunter Wars trilogy and was the last Star Wars novel K. W. Jeter wrote, capping a series that helped cement Boba Fett's post-Sarlacc survival and reputation as a fan favorite ahead of the character's expanded Legends-era spotlight.

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi
creator: James Kahn
notes: Novelization of Episode VI, based on the shooting script by Lawrence Kasdan and George Lucas.
blurb: To rescue Han Solo from the clutches of Jabba the Hutt, Luke Skywalker, Leia Organa, and their companions stage a daring infiltration of the crime lord's desert palace. With Han freed, the Rebel Alliance mounts its final assault on the second Death Star while Luke confronts Darth Vader and the Emperor aboard the battle station, determined to redeem his father before it is too late. The fate of the galaxy rests on a battle fought in the stars above Endor and in the heart of one family.
trivia: The novelization was drafted from an earlier version of the screenplay when the film was still titled Revenge of the Jedi, leaving small details and lines of dialogue in the book that differ from the finished movie.

title: Star Wars: Tales from Jabba's Palace
creator: ed. Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Anthology of short stories set among the motley denizens of Jabba the Hutt's palace on Tatooine.
blurb: Behind the gates of Jabba the Hutt's palace lurks a menagerie of smugglers, monsters, musicians, and assassins, each with a story worth telling. This anthology wanders through the court's darkest corners, from the dancer Oola's fate to the schemes of bounty hunters and sycophants jockeying for the crime lord's favor. Woven throughout is the tightening net of Luke Skywalker's rescue plan, seen through the eyes of the very creatures who call the palace home.
trivia: Like its companion volume Tales of the Bounty Hunters, this anthology gives voice and backstory to numerous background aliens and creatures glimpsed only fleetingly in Return of the Jedi's palace and barge sequences, including the Max Rebo Band and Salacious Crumb.

title: Star Wars: Tales from the Empire
creator: ed. Peter Schweighofer
notes: Fourth entry in Bantam's Star Wars Tales anthology series; ten short stories by nine authors set throughout the Imperial era.
blurb: Across the length and breadth of the Galactic Empire, ordinary beings are swept up in extraordinary events. From Imperial officers questioning their loyalties to smugglers dodging Star Destroyers, these ten tales illuminate the shadowed corners of Palpatine's reign. Some stories unfold in the waning days after the Clone Wars; others echo in the uneasy years following the Emperor's death. Together they reveal the Empire not as a faceless machine, but as a galaxy of individual choices, some noble, some damning.
trivia: Collects several stories originally published in West End Games' Star Wars Adventure Journal alongside new material commissioned for the anthology.
inUniverseDate: ~11 BBY-10 ABY (anthology spanning the Imperial era)

title: Star Wars: Tales from the New Republic
creator: ed. Peter Schweighofer and Craig Carey
notes: Fifth and final entry in the Star Wars Tales anthology series; eleven short stories.
blurb: As the New Republic struggles to rebuild a fractured galaxy, its citizens face triumphs and hardships far from the spotlight of galactic history. These eleven stories follow smugglers turned diplomats, war-weary soldiers, and hopeful settlers navigating a fragile peace. Spanning years from the immediate aftermath of the Empire's defeat to the height of New Republic power, the collection captures a galaxy still learning how to live without a tyrant's grip.
trivia: Closes out Bantam's Star Wars Tales anthology series, which began in 1995 with Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina.
inUniverseDate: ~1 BBY-18 ABY (anthology spanning the New Republic era)

title: Star Wars: The Truce at Bakura
creator: Kathy Tyers
notes: Direct sequel to Return of the Jedi, beginning the day after the Battle of Endor.
blurb: The cheers of Endor have barely faded when a new threat emerges: an Imperial fleet has been ambushed by an alien invasion force at the remote world of Bakura, and the beleaguered Imperial governor calls for help from an unlikely source, the Rebel Alliance. Luke, Leia, Han, and Chewbacca must decide whether old enemies can become allies against a common foe from beyond known space. As Luke wrestles with unsettling new visions of his fallen father, the fledgling Alliance faces its first true test of galactic leadership.
trivia: Was the first Star Wars novel to directly continue the story from Return of the Jedi, picking up literally the day after the film's events.
inUniverseDate: ~4 ABY (immediately after the Battle of Endor)

title: Star Wars: Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor
creator: Matthew Stover
notes: Standalone novel chronicling the Battle of Mindor.
blurb: Months after the Emperor's death, a masked warlord known as Lord Shadowspawn emerges from the ashes of the old regime, wielding dark technology and a fanatical army of shadow troopers. When he threatens to unravel the fragile New Republic from its Inner Rim strongholds, Luke Skywalker leads a ragtag strike force into the heart of enemy territory. What begins as a rescue mission becomes a descent into a nightmare where nothing, not even Luke's own perceptions, can be trusted.
trivia: Author Matthew Stover wrote it as a deliberate throwback to pulp adventure serials, a fast-paced standalone story distinct from his more literary New Jedi Order and Legacy of the Force work.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Rogue Squadron
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 1 of the X-Wing series; introduces the reformation of Rogue Squadron.
blurb: The war against the Empire didn't end at Endor. With Imperial remnants still holding key worlds, General Wedge Antilles is tasked with rebuilding the legendary Rogue Squadron from a mix of green recruits and battle-scarred veterans. Their first mission: retake the strategic world of Borleias from a ruthless Imperial commander. It's a trial by fire that will determine whether this new generation of pilots can live up to the legacy of Luke Skywalker and Biggs Darklighter.
trivia: The first Star Wars novel built around an ensemble cast outside the core saga characters, launching Stackpole's long-running X-Wing series.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 2 of the X-Wing series.
blurb: With Rogue Squadron proven in battle, Wedge Antilles sets his sights on the ultimate prize: Coruscant, the very heart of the crumbling Empire. Disguised as civilians, Wedge and his pilots infiltrate the Imperial capital to lay the groundwork for a New Republic invasion, gathering allies among the city's oppressed and disillusioned. But treachery lurks close to home, and the Rogues must decide how far they're willing to gamble everything for a galaxy watching and waiting.
trivia: Gives one of the earliest detailed looks at Coruscant's civilian population and underworld living under Imperial occupation, well before the prequel films depicted the planet.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: The Krytos Trap
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 3 of the X-Wing series.
blurb: Coruscant has fallen to the New Republic, but victory is far from secure. Imperial Intelligence chief Ysanne Isard unleashes a horrifying bioweapon, the Krytos virus, targeting non-human species across the capital to sow chaos and turn public opinion against the fragile new government. As the city descends into panic, Wedge Antilles and Rogue Squadron must root out the source of the plague while fending off political betrayal from within their own ranks.
trivia: The Krytos virus storyline was praised by fans for tackling species-targeted genocide and political fallout with more moral weight than typical Imperial-versus-Rebel conflicts in earlier EU novels.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: The Bacta War
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 4 of the X-Wing series, concluding the original four-book Rogue Squadron arc.
blurb: Framed for treason and stripped of their commissions, Wedge Antilles and Rogue Squadron become outlaws in the very government they fought to establish. Branded criminals, they forge an uneasy alliance with smugglers and mercenaries to strike back at Ysanne Isard's stranglehold on the bacta trade, a monopoly that could cripple the New Republic's ability to heal from war. It all builds to a desperate assault on Isard's fortress world of Thyferra, where the fate of the Squadron, and the galaxy's medical lifeline, hangs in the balance.
trivia: Concludes the four-book X-Wing arc Stackpole wrote consecutively across 1996-1997; he did not return to the series until Isard's Revenge in 1999.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Wraith Squadron
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 5 of the X-Wing series
blurb: When New Republic Intelligence needs a squadron capable of missions too unorthodox for regular fighter pilots, Wedge Antilles assembles a unit of rejects, screwups, and misfits pulled from across the fleet. Under his command, this ragtag group, soon dubbed Wraith Squadron, trains not just to fly but to infiltrate, deceive, and improvise their way through operations no by-the-book unit could survive. As they take on their first deep-cover mission against the forces of Imperial Warlord Zsinj, the Wraiths must learn to trust each other's flaws as much as their skills.
trivia: Wraith Squadron's roster includes a fictional Ewok pilot named 'Kettch,' a running gag invented by pilot Face Loran for psychological-warfare broadcasts, despite Wedge pointing out that an Ewok couldn't even reach an X-wing's controls.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Iron Fist
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 6 of the X-Wing series
blurb: Fresh off their first mission, the pilots of Wraith Squadron dive back into the shadow war against Imperial Warlord Zsinj, whose Super Star Destroyer Iron Fist anchors a battle fleet still capable of crippling the New Republic. Posing as turncoats and slipping into Zsinj's own ranks, the Wraiths risk exposure and execution with every deception. As personal rivalries and blossoming romances complicate the mission, Wedge Antilles's misfit unit must out-scheme an enemy commander as cunning as he is ruthless.
trivia: The book's title refers to the Super Star Destroyer Iron Fist, flagship of Imperial Warlord Zsinj, whose hunt for the Wraiths anchors the middle chapter of Aaron Allston's three-book arc that concludes in Solo Command.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Solo Command
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 7 of the X-Wing series
blurb: With Zsinj's fleet reeling but not broken, the Wraiths and a task force under General Han Solo close in for a final reckoning with the warlord who has evaded the New Republic for years. Deception, sabotage, and a desperate hunt for Zsinj's hidden base push the squadron to its limits as old wounds among its members resurface. The endgame of the Zsinj campaign forces Wedge Antilles's unconventional fighters to gamble everything on one last unorthodox plan.
trivia: Solo Command wraps up the multi-book hunt for Imperial Warlord Zsinj that spanned three consecutive Aaron Allston novels, and its audiobook, like its two predecessors, was narrated by actor Anthony Heald.

title: Star Wars: The Courtship of Princess Leia
creator: Dave Wolverton
notes: Standalone novel; ends with the wedding of Han Solo and Leia Organa
blurb: When Leia Organa agrees to a political marriage with Prince Isolder of the powerful Hapes Consortium to secure desperately needed warships for the New Republic, Han Solo refuses to accept losing her without a fight. In a move as reckless as it is romantic, Han hijacks Leia mid-negotiation and sets a course for a planet he intends to claim as a wedding gift, only for both of them to crash-land on the witch-haunted world of Dathomir. Stranded among rival clans of Force-wielding witches and prowling rancors, Han and Leia are forced to confront what they actually want, together.
trivia: Author Dave Wolverton later found fantasy-genre fame writing under the pen name David Farland; the political marriage plot he devised here introduced the Hapes Consortium and Prince Isolder, both of which recurred throughout later Expanded Universe novels.

title: Star Wars: Tatooine Ghost
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Standalone novel set shortly before Heir to the Empire, though published a decade after the Thrawn Trilogy
blurb: A recovery mission sends Han, Leia, Chewbacca, and C-3PO back to Tatooine to retrieve a stolen piece of Alderaanian art hiding a vital New Republic communications key. Amid the chaos of a black-market auction and an Imperial ambush, Leia stumbles across relics and recordings tied to a man she never knew as anything but Darth Vader, her father, Anakin Skywalker. As old ghosts surface in the desert that shaped him, Leia must reconcile her father's buried humanity with the fears it raises about her own future.
trivia: Published in 2003 during the New Jedi Order era, Tatooine Ghost is set nearly a decade earlier in-universe and includes an unnamed cameo appearance by Grand Admiral Thrawn, whose identity the heroes don't yet know.

title: Star Wars: Heir to the Empire
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Book 1 of the original Thrawn Trilogy; credited with relaunching the Star Wars Expanded Universe in 1991
blurb: Five years after the fall of the Emperor, the New Republic is stretched thin, and a surviving Imperial officer of terrifying brilliance is about to test it. Grand Admiral Thrawn, the last competent warlord left in the fractured Empire, begins a patient, calculated campaign to break the fledgling government, aided by an insane resurrected Jedi clone and a smuggler's knowledge of the New Republic's blind spots. Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Leia Organa must face an enemy who wins not through the dark side, but through strategy sharper than their own.
trivia: Released in May 1991, Heir to the Empire is widely credited with reviving Star Wars publishing after Return of the Jedi, hitting the New York Times bestseller list and proving there was still a mass audience for new Star Wars stories years before the prequel films.

title: Star Wars: Dark Force Rising
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Book 2 of the original Thrawn Trilogy
blurb: As Grand Admiral Thrawn hunts for the legendary Katana fleet, two hundred Dreadnaughts that could tip the galactic balance of power, Luke Skywalker and the smuggler Mara Jade find themselves reluctantly thrown together on a mission that tests old hatreds. Meanwhile, Leia travels to the mysterious world of Honoghr to investigate a conspiracy that threatens both her marriage and her standing with the New Republic. As Thrawn's net closes and the insane clone Jedi Joruus C'baoth's ambitions grow, the New Republic's survival hinges on secrets buried in its own past.
trivia: The novel centers on the hunt for the Katana fleet, two hundred Dreadnaught-class ships lost since the era of the Clone Wars, a plot device Timothy Zahn invented that went on to be referenced across the wider Expanded Universe.

title: Star Wars: The Last Command
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Book 3 of the original Thrawn Trilogy
blurb: With the rediscovered Katana fleet now crewed by cloned soldiers loyal to him, Grand Admiral Thrawn stands closer than ever to crushing the New Republic for good. Luke Skywalker confronts the mad clone Jedi Master Joruus C'baoth on Wayland, while Han and Leia race against time as Thrawn's endgame accelerates and their newborn twins hang in the balance. In a climax years in the making, the fate of the galaxy comes down to a single, desperate gambit aboard Thrawn's own flagship.
trivia: The Last Command ends with the death of Grand Admiral Thrawn, a character so popular with fans that Timothy Zahn brought him back decades later, first in the Legends-era Hand of Thrawn duology and eventually in an all-new canon Thrawn trilogy beginning in 2017.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Isard's Revenge
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 8 of the X-Wing series; set earlier in the in-universe timeline than its 1999 release, filling a gap between the Bacta War and the Thrawn crisis era.
blurb: With the tyrant Ysanne Isard presumed dead, Rogue Squadron is sent to help liberate the Imperial-held world of Thyferra and secure its vital bacta supply for the New Republic. But Isard has survived in the shadows, and she has one final, merciless act of vengeance planned for the pilots who broke her. As old wounds resurface and new recruits are blooded in combat, Corran Horn and his squadron mates must face an enemy who would rather scorch the galaxy than accept defeat.
trivia: Although published in 1999 as the eighth X-Wing novel, the story is set earlier in the timeline (around 9 ABY), slotting into a gap between the Bacta War and the Thrawn trilogy era rather than continuing directly from the series' prior release.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Search
creator: Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Book 1 of the Jedi Academy Trilogy.
blurb: Five years after the Battle of Endor, Luke Skywalker sets out to rebuild the Jedi Order, gathering a handful of Force-sensitive students to train at a new academy on Yavin 4.
