Meanwhile, Han Solo and Chewbacca infiltrate the spice mines of Kessel to rescue a relative of Leia's, and escape with an unexpected companion: a young prisoner named Kyp Durron, whose latent power will shape the fate of the fledgling Jedi Academy. As old dangers stir in the ruins of an ancient temple, the seeds of a dangerous new threat to the New Republic are quietly sown.
trivia: The trilogy's central villain, the Dark Lord Exar Kun, is first hinted at (unnamed) in Jedi Search before being fully introduced in the direct sequel, Dark Apprentice, released later that same year.

title: Star Wars: Dark Apprentice
creator: Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Book 2 of the Jedi Academy Trilogy.
blurb: At the fledgling Jedi Academy, Luke's students begin to manifest extraordinary power, none more so than Kyp Durron, whose raw talent draws him toward the corrupting whispers of a spirit long thought destroyed. As the ancient Dark Lord Exar Kun tightens his hold on Kyp's mind, the New Republic races to stop the awakening of the Sun Crusher, a weapon capable of annihilating entire star systems. Luke must decide how far he can go to save a student who may already be lost to the dark side.
trivia: All three Jedi Academy Trilogy novels were written and published within the same year, 1994, with the volumes released only a few months apart from one another.

title: Star Wars: Champions of the Force
creator: Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Book 3 of the Jedi Academy Trilogy.
blurb: Possessed by the spirit of Exar Kun and wielding the terrifying Sun Crusher, Kyp Durron has become the galaxy's most dangerous weapon, and only Luke Skywalker may be able to reach the young man still trapped inside him. As the New Republic reels from devastating losses and Han and Leia race to save the surviving Jedi trainees, Luke must confront Exar Kun directly in a final battle for Kyp's soul and the future of the reborn Jedi Order.
trivia: Champions of the Force closed out the Jedi Academy Trilogy in October 1994, capping a run of three novels released within the same calendar year and cementing Kevin J. Anderson as one of the era's most prolific Star Wars authors.

title: Star Wars: I, Jedi
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Standalone novel that runs concurrent with the Jedi Academy Trilogy, retold from Corran Horn's first-person point of view; also connects to Stackpole's X-Wing series.
blurb: When his wife Mirax vanishes on a covert mission, Corran Horn realizes his only hope of finding her lies in mastering the mystical arts of the Jedi. Enrolling at Luke Skywalker's academy, Corran uncovers a hidden Jedi heritage in his own family while flashes of insight into the galaxy's criminal underworld point him toward Mirax's captors. Racing against time and clashing with the Academy's traditions, Corran forges his own unconventional path to becoming a Jedi Knight.
trivia: I, Jedi was the first Star Wars novel narrated entirely in first person, and it retroactively weaves Corran Horn into the events of the 1994 Jedi Academy Trilogy, a character who did not yet exist when that trilogy was originally written.

title: Star Wars: Children of the Jedi
creator: Barbara Hambly
notes: Book 1 of the informal Callista Trilogy, followed by Darksaber and Hambly's later Planet of Twilight.
blurb: A dormant Imperial superweapon, the Eye of Palpatine, has awakened deep in unexplored space, and Leia, Han, and Chewbacca must find and stop it before it can annihilate entire worlds. Aboard the ship, Luke Skywalker forms an unexpected bond with Callista, the disembodied consciousness of a Jedi Knight from a bygone era who has been trapped for decades. As Luke falls for a woman without a body, the fate of countless lives hangs on whether the ancient battle station can be stopped in time.
trivia: The novel's title originally referred to grown spouses and children of Jedi Knights; a later reference guide published after the prequel trilogy retconned the phrase to mean Jedi younglings, reflecting how the saga's lore on Jedi attachment shifted over time.

title: Star Wars: Darksaber
creator: Kevin J. Anderson
notes: Book 2 of the informal Callista Trilogy, following Barbara Hambly's Children of the Jedi.
blurb: The Hutts have never forgiven the New Republic for crippling their criminal empire, and now the ruthless Durga the Hutt is secretly building a devastating new superweapon: a scaled-down Death Star called the Darksaber. As Han and Lando scramble to uncover the plot before it is unleashed, Luke struggles to help Callista adjust to a newly restored body, and old rivalries among the Hutt clans threaten to spiral out of control.
trivia: Despite mixed reviews criticizing its reuse of the Death Star concept, Darksaber still reached number three on the New York Times bestseller list following its October 1995 release.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Traitor
creator: Matthew Stover
notes: Book 13 of the 19-book New Jedi Order series
blurb: Jacen Solo, captured by the Yuuzhan Vong, is placed in the care of the enigmatic Vergere, who challenges everything he believes about the Force and the nature of the light and dark sides. Isolated, tortured, and pushed to the edge of endurance, he must decide whether survival is worth sacrificing his ideals. A tense psychological journey set against the darkest hour of the New Jedi Order.
trivia: Author Matthew Stover drew on his martial-arts background and interest in Zen philosophy while writing the novel, and it is widely cited by fans and critics as one of the best-written entries in the entire New Jedi Order series.

title: Star Wars: The Black Fleet Crisis: Before the Storm
creator: Michael P. Kube-McDowell
notes: Book 1 of 3 in the Black Fleet Crisis trilogy
blurb: When the reclusive Yevetha turn on the New Republic and slaughter every non-Yevethan being in the Koornacht Cluster, Leia Organa Solo is sent to negotiate a peace that may already be impossible. Meanwhile Luke Skywalker follows a decades-old mystery toward a hidden fleet of Imperial warships lost deep in unexplored space. As old wounds resurface, the New Republic edges toward a war it may not be ready to fight.
trivia: The novel introduces the Yevetha, whose xenophobic campaign of genocide against non-Yevethan sentients in the Koornacht Cluster became one of the more grim, morally unflinching threads in the early Expanded Universe.

title: Star Wars: The Black Fleet Crisis: Shield of Lies
creator: Michael P. Kube-McDowell
notes: Book 2 of 3 in the Black Fleet Crisis trilogy
blurb: With the Yevethan crisis spiraling toward open war, Han Solo sets out on a private, dangerous search for Luke Skywalker, who has vanished chasing rumors of an ancient fleet and a mysterious Force tradition. Back in the Senate, Leia struggles to hold the fracturing New Republic together as political maneuvering threatens to do the Yevethans' work for them. Secrets long buried in the galaxy's shadows begin to surface.
trivia: Shield of Lies deepens the trilogy's introduction of the Fallanassi, a secretive order of Force users who manipulate the 'White Current' rather than the traditional Force, expanding the Expanded Universe's exploration of Force traditions outside the Jedi and Sith.

title: Star Wars: The Corellian Trilogy: Showdown at Centerpoint
creator: Roger MacBride Allen
notes: Book 3 of 3 in the Corellian Trilogy
blurb: With Corellia's home system in open rebellion and the ancient superweapon Centerpoint Station primed to repeat a planet-shattering atrocity, Han Solo, Luke Skywalker, and their allies race to stop a conspirator bent on rewriting galactic history through force. Old friendships are tested and unlikely heroes step forward as the fate of five worlds comes down to a desperate final gambit. The trilogy's climax pits resourcefulness against unimaginable firepower.
trivia: Centerpoint Station, the planet-destroying superweapon at the heart of the trilogy's climax, was later tied in other Legends material to the ancient Celestials, one of the earliest and most advanced civilizations in Star Wars lore.

title: Star Wars: The Corellian Trilogy: Ambush at Corellia
creator: Roger MacBride Allen
notes: Book 1 of 3 in the Corellian Trilogy
blurb: A diplomatic visit to Han Solo's homeworld turns deadly when an assassination attempt on Chief of State Leia Organa Solo exposes a conspiracy brewing deep within the Corellian system. As mysterious interdiction fields begin stranding ships across the sector, Han and Leia uncover buried secrets and old loyalties that could make Corellia the New Republic's most dangerous enemy yet. The opening chapter of a crisis that will threaten five worlds at once.
trivia: The Corellian Trilogy was among the first Star Wars novel series to deeply develop the five interlinked worlds of the Corellian system, worldbuilding that influenced many later Legends stories set in that sector.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 11 of the 19-book New Jedi Order series; first half of the Enemy Lines duology
blurb: With Coruscant fallen to the Yuuzhan Vong, newly-promoted General Wedge Antilles leads a battered coalition of pilots, warships, and refugees in a desperate guerrilla campaign against overwhelming odds. Jaina Solo forges a harder new identity in the crucible of war while Wraith Squadron's gift for deception is pushed to its limits. The first half of the Enemy Lines duology delivers a tense, fleet-scale fight for survival deep behind enemy lines.
trivia: The novel reached number seven on the New York Times paperback bestseller list for the week of April 14, 2002, and marks Wedge Antilles's promotion to General, capping his long evolution from X-wing pilot to fleet commander across decades of Star Wars novels.

title: Star Wars: The Crystal Star
creator: Vonda N. McIntyre
notes: Standalone novel, not part of a numbered trilogy or series
blurb: When the Solo children are kidnapped from the Errant Venture, Han and Leia's desperate search takes them across the galaxy while Luke Skywalker is drawn into the schemes of a fallen Jedi seeking to reshape the Force itself. Strange worlds, ancient dangers, and a dying star complicate a rescue that becomes far more than it first appears. A standalone adventure that tests the Solo family bond against powers beyond their understanding.
trivia: The Crystal Star is frequently cited by fans as one of the more divisive entries in the classic Expanded Universe; the 2012 Essential Reader's Companion redated it to roughly 14 ABY, years later than older fan chronologies which placed it around 9-10 ABY.
inUniverseDate: ~14 ABY (per Essential Reader's Companion; older sources place it ~9-10 ABY)

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime
creator: R. A. Salvatore
notes: Launch novel of the 19-book New Jedi Order mega-series; opens the Yuuzhan Vong invasion arc that defined Star Wars Legends publishing for the next several years
blurb: When ships begin vanishing without explanation and a hidden armada surfaces from beyond the galaxy's edge, the New Republic faces an invader unlike any it has fought before, one the Force itself cannot sense coming. As the Yuuzhan Vong unleash devastation not seen since the height of the Empire, the Solo and Skywalker families are pulled into a war that will cost them more than they ever imagined. The opening novel of the New Jedi Order ignites a galaxy-spanning invasion that spans nineteen books.
trivia: Vector Prime is infamous among fans for killing off Chewbacca in its opening chapters, a shocking, controversial death that signaled the darker, higher-stakes tone of the New Jedi Order era that followed.

title: Star Wars: The Black Fleet Crisis: Tyrant's Test
creator: Michael P. Kube-McDowell
notes: Book 3 of 3 in the Black Fleet Crisis trilogy; not part of the New Jedi Order mega-series.
blurb: As the Yevethan warlord Nil Spaar tightens his grip on the Koornacht Cluster, the New Republic teeters on the edge of war. Luke Skywalker races to uncover the truth about his birth mother while Han and Chewbacca mount a desperate rescue deep in hostile territory. Leia must decide how far the Republic will go to stop a genocidal enemy before the crisis consumes them all.
trivia: The trilogy's subplot about Luke searching for the identity of his birth mother was rendered moot once the prequel films later established her as Padme Amidala, leaving this thread an interesting relic of pre-prequel Legends continuity.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Balance Point
creator: Kathy Tyers
notes: Book 6 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series.
blurb: As the Yuuzhan Vong push deeper into the galaxy, Han and Leia lead a refugee fleet while Jacen and Jaina Solo are pulled toward very different paths through the Force. When Jacen is captured, the twins' choices force the family to confront how far they are willing to go in a war with no clean answers. The novel crystallizes the moral tension over aggression, sacrifice, and what a Jedi is allowed to become in wartime.
trivia: Balance Point is where Jacen Solo formulates his guiding philosophy that aggression, even in defense of others, leads to the dark side — a principle that drives much of his arc for the rest of the series.

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 9 of the X-Wing series; the final novel of the original X-Wing series, set well before the Yuuzhan Vong invasion and not part of the New Jedi Order.
blurb: Wedge Antilles and a handful of the galaxy's best pilots are sent as diplomats to Adumar, a warrior culture obsessed with flying skill, tasked with winning the world over to the New Republic before Imperial remnants can do the same. Between duels, banquets, and political maneuvering, Wedge is pressed to choose sides in a conflict he never wanted to fight. What starts as a goodwill mission spirals into a test of loyalty, honor, and what a soldier owes his government.
trivia: It is the highest Goodreads-rated novel in the entire original X-Wing series, frequently praised by fans for its comedic tone and Wedge Antilles's political speeches.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant
creator: Sean Williams and Shane Dix
notes: Book 15 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series; first of the Force Heretic trilogy.
blurb: With the Imperial Remnant reeling from Yuuzhan Vong incursions, Han and Leia are dispatched to broker an uneasy alliance with an old enemy. Meanwhile Jaina Solo and a Jedi strike team chase a desperate lead that may turn the tide of the war, even as the fractured New Republic government struggles to hold itself together. Old rivalries and new necessities collide as the galaxy searches for any path to survival.
trivia: Force Heretic was written by the Australian writing duo Sean Williams and Shane Dix, one of the few New Jedi Order story arcs handled by non-American authors.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 3 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series; concludes the two-part Dark Tide arc.
blurb: As the Yuuzhan Vong tighten their hold on the Outer Rim, Luke Skywalker leads a desperate defense of the sacred world of Ithor, only to watch the invaders lay waste to it. The New Republic's military and political leadership fracture under the strain while Corran Horn and other Jedi grapple with the invaders' unsettling immunity to the Force. It is the moment the New Jedi Order stops treating the Yuuzhan Vong as a containable threat and starts treating them as existential.
trivia: Dark Tide II: Ruin depicts the destruction of Ithor, homeworld of the peaceful, Hutt-allied Ithorians, one of the New Jedi Order's earliest and most shocking demonstrations of Yuuzhan Vong scorched-earth tactics.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee
creator: Sean Williams and Shane Dix
notes: Book 16 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series; second of the Force Heretic trilogy.
blurb: Jaina Solo's search for a Jedi renegade who may hold the key to defeating the Yuuzhan Vong pulls her deeper into hostile territory. Meanwhile Han and Leia's diplomatic mission grows more fraught as political rivals scheme against them from within the New Republic. As refugee crises overwhelm systems that can barely support them, the fragile alliance holding the galaxy together looks more uncertain than ever.
trivia: Refugee continues Jaina Solo's development into the 'Sword of the Jedi,' a role first hinted at earlier in the New Jedi Order and expanded significantly across the Force Heretic trilogy.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Star by Star
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 9 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series; the longest novel in the series at over 600 pages.
blurb: Luke Skywalker approves a desperate strike-team mission to Myrkr to destroy the Yuuzhan Vong's voxyn cloning facility, a weapon bred to hunt and kill Jedi. Leading the team is young Anakin Solo, whose growing recklessness puts the entire mission and his fellow Jedi in jeopardy. What begins as a bold gambit becomes one of the New Jedi Order's darkest turning points, with losses that permanently reshape the Solo family and the war itself.
trivia: Star by Star is the longest book in the New Jedi Order series and is best known for the death of Anakin Solo during the Myrkr strike-team mission, one of the most controversial character deaths in Star Wars Legends history.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way
creator: Walter Jon Williams
notes: Book 14 of 19 in the New Jedi Order series.
blurb: With Coruscant lost to the Yuuzhan Vong, the New Republic's fractured fleets and government struggle to mount a unified resistance. Admiral Ackbar devises a daring trap to lure the invaders' Warmaster into a decisive engagement, while Han Solo is pulled into a mission that could finally shift the war's momentum. As old allies test new loyalties, the New Republic reaches a breaking point that forces a reckoning over how the war can actually be won.
trivia: Destiny's Way features the pivotal Battle of Ebaq, an elaborate ambush engineered by Admiral Ackbar that results in the death of Yuuzhan Vong Warmaster Tsavong Lah at the hands of Jaina Solo, marking a major turning point in the war.

title: Star Wars: Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Sunrise
creator: Kevin J. Anderson and Rebecca Moesta
notes: Omnibus collecting Lightsabers, Darkest Knight, and Jedi Under Siege (Young Jedi Knights books 4-6); published by Berkley Jam in December 2003, several months after the companion omnibus Jedi Shadow.
blurb: At the Jedi academy on Yavin 4, Jaina and Jacen Solo, Tenel Ka, Lowbacca, and Zekk face their most dangerous trials yet as a shadowy enemy plots against the fledgling Jedi order. Lightsaber training turns deadly, a trusted teacher's dark secret threatens to tear the young Jedi apart, and an all-out siege forces the students to defend the very academy that trained them. Friendship and courage are tested as the next generation of Jedi comes of age under fire.
trivia: All six Young Jedi Knights novels split across the Jedi Shadow and Jedi Sunrise omnibuses were also combined into a single hardcover volume titled The Rise of the Shadow Academy.

title: Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn: Vision of the Future
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Hand of Thrawn Book 2 of 2; sequel to Specter of the Past.
blurb: As the New Republic teeters on the edge of civil war, a rumor of Grand Admiral Thrawn's return sends shockwaves through the Empire and the fragile coalition holding the galaxy together. Luke, Leia, and Han race to unmask an elaborate Imperial deception before it can shatter the peace, while Mara Jade infiltrates a fortress of fanatics awaiting their lost commander's call. Old enemies and old friends collide as the truth about the legendary Hand of Thrawn finally comes to light.
trivia: The novel ends with Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade's engagement, a storyline resolved the following year in the Union comic book miniseries, which depicted their wedding.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey
creator: Elaine Cunningham
notes: The New Jedi Order Book 10.
blurb: Reeling from catastrophic losses behind Yuuzhan Vong lines, Jaina Solo flees into the chaos of a galaxy at war, her grief curdling into anger and doubt. Drawn toward Kyp Durron's reckless brand of justice even as an unexpected attraction pulls her elsewhere, Jaina walks the knife's edge between light and dark. In the treacherous Hapes Cluster, old grudges and royal intrigue threaten to finish what the war has started.
trivia: The novel quietly plants the earliest seeds of the Jaina Solo-Jagged Fel relationship, which becomes a major thread through the rest of the New Jedi Order and beyond.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse
creator: James Luceno
notes: The New Jedi Order Book 5; second half of the Agents of Chaos duology.
blurb: As Yuuzhan Vong victories mount and world after world falls, Leia Organa Solo throws herself into the desperate work of evacuating refugees ahead of the invasion. Luke Skywalker struggles to hold his fracturing Jedi order together while one Knight risks everything on a reckless mission behind enemy lines. With morale crumbling across the New Republic, a single act of daring may be the only thing standing between hope and collapse.
trivia: The book features Wraith Squadron running a covert psychological operation that involves helping Jaina Solo impersonate a Yuuzhan Vong deity.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory I: Conquest
creator: Greg Keyes
notes: The New Jedi Order Book 7; first half of the Edge of Victory duology.
blurb: With a Yuuzhan Vong fleet bearing down on the Jedi academy at Yavin 4, Talon Karrde mounts a rescue for the stranded students, but Anakin Solo refuses to wait for help to arrive. Racing off on his own, Anakin discovers that his friend Tahiri has been captured, and that the Yuuzhan Vong have far darker plans for her than simple imprisonment. What begins as a rescue becomes a desperate fight to save a friend's very identity.
trivia: The book develops the beginning of Anakin Solo and Tahiri Veila's romantic relationship, a bond later shattered by Tahiri's Yuuzhan Vong-induced transformation into 'Riina Kwaad.'

title: Star Wars: Scourge
creator: Jeff Grubb
notes: Standalone novel set in the post-Return of the Jedi era, roughly fifteen years before the Yuuzhan Vong invasion.
blurb: When a young Jedi is murdered while investigating a lucrative and lawless hyperspace route, his former Master, archivist Mander Zuma, sets out to learn the truth. His search plunges him into the cutthroat world of Hutt crime lords, smugglers, and killers all vying for control of the newly discovered trade lane. Zuma will have to master skills far removed from the archives if he hopes to find justice for his fallen apprentice and survive the attempt.
trivia: Scourge is adapted from the Star Wars Roleplaying Game adventure module Tempest Feud, and it remains the only Star Wars novel written by veteran game designer Jeff Grubb, co-creator of the Forgotten Realms setting.

title: Star Wars: Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Shadow
creator: Kevin J. Anderson and Rebecca Moesta
notes: Omnibus collecting Heirs of the Force, Shadow Academy, and The Lost Ones (Young Jedi Knights books 1-3); published by Berkley Jam in September 2003, ahead of the companion omnibus Jedi Sunrise.
blurb: Han and Leia's twins, Jacen and Jaina Solo, arrive at Luke Skywalker's Jedi academy on Yavin 4 to begin their training alongside new friends Tenel Ka, Lowbacca, and the troubled Zekk. But a rogue faction calling itself the Shadow Academy is recruiting Jedi hopefuls to the dark side, and its ambitions reach all the way to the young students themselves. As old rivalries and new dangers collide, the next generation of Jedi must prove they are ready for the fight ahead.
trivia: Jedi Shadow was published in September 2003, three months ahead of its companion omnibus Jedi Sunrise, making it the earlier of the two Berkley Jam reissue volumes in the Young Jedi Knights reading order.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial
creator: James Luceno
notes: The New Jedi Order Book 4; first half of the Agents of Chaos duology.
blurb: Grieving the death of Chewbacca, Han Solo withdraws from his family and stumbles into a conspiracy of smugglers and pirates secretly trading with the Yuuzhan Vong. His investigation uncovers a Vong plot to strike at the heart of the New Jedi Order using a deadly bio-weapon and an infiltrator posing as a defector. As old scores resurface and new betrayals emerge, Han must decide how far he'll go to protect the people he has left.
trivia: Early outlines for the novel had Boba Fett serving as the information broker on the Ord Mantell space station, but Luceno replaced him with the character Big Bunji to avoid overloading the story with familiar faces.

title: Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn: Specter of the Past
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Book 1 of 2 in the Hand of Thrawn duology; followed by Vision of the Future.
blurb: Ten years after his death at the Battle of Bilbringi, Grand Admiral Thrawn is reported to be alive, and the remnants of the Empire are rallying behind him once more. As panic spreads and old wounds reopen, Han and Leia race to keep the fragile New Republic from collapsing into civil war, while Luke and Mara Jade pursue a mystery involving a warship crewed entirely by clones. Behind it all, a disgraced Moff's desperate gambit threatens to tear the galaxy apart before the truth can be uncovered.
trivia: The duology reveals that the mysterious clone-crewed pirate ship was seeded by the antagonist, Moff Disra, as part of an elaborate hoax meant to convince the galaxy that Thrawn had returned from the dead.

title: Star Wars: Planet of Twilight
creator: Barbara Hambly
notes: Third and final book of the informal 'Callista trilogy,' following Children of the Jedi and Darksaber; no series branding appears on the cover.
blurb: When Leia Organa Solo is captured by a ruthless warlord on the desolate, crystal-scarred world of Nam Chorios, she must survive a hostile planet crawling with fanatics, monstrous drochs, and secrets buried for centuries. Meanwhile Luke Skywalker searches for the missing Callista, the woman he loves, whose Force-bond with him is unraveling in ways neither can explain. As ancient dangers stir beneath the planet's surface, old loyalties and new betrayals collide in a fight for the future of the New Republic.
trivia: Barbara Hambly wrote this novel to close out the loose 'Callista trilogy' she began with Children of the Jedi, effectively writing the character Callista out of Luke Skywalker's story after fan reaction to her proved divisive.

title: Star Wars: The New Rebellion
creator: Kristine Kathryn Rusch
notes: Standalone novel, not part of a numbered sub-series; antagonist is the fallen Jedi Kueller.
blurb: When a shattering disturbance in the Force claims the lives of over a million beings, Luke Skywalker senses that a new and terrible enemy has emerged from the shadows of the Empire's fall. As bombs rip through the Senate Hall on Coruscant and suspicion falls on Han Solo himself, Chief of State Leia Organa Solo must root out a hidden mastermind before he can seize control of the galaxy. Behind the chaos stands a vengeful fallen Jedi, and only the Skywalker twins can stop him before he brings the New Republic to its knees.
trivia: The novel's continuity clashed noticeably with Michael P. Kube-McDowell's preceding Black Fleet Crisis trilogy, leading many fans to conclude Rusch's story was originally drafted for an earlier point in the timeline.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 12 of the 19-book New Jedi Order series; second half of the Enemy Lines duology.
blurb: With Coruscant lost to the Yuuzhan Vong, Han and Leia lead a scattered band of resistance fighters in a desperate campaign to buy time for fleeing refugees. Above the ashes of the galactic capital, Wedge Antilles and a ragtag strike force stage one last, near-suicidal assault to strike a blow against the invaders. Meanwhile, held captive deep within enemy territory, Jacen Solo endures an ordeal that will forever change who he is, and what he becomes.
trivia: This novel, together with its companion Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream, depicts the fall of Coruscant to the Yuuzhan Vong, one of the most significant turning points in the entire New Jedi Order series.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Survivor's Quest
creator: Timothy Zahn
notes: Published a year after the main New Jedi Order series concluded, but set chronologically much earlier, bridging Zahn's own Hand of Thrawn duology and the start of the Yuuzhan Vong invasion.
blurb: Fifty years after Grand Admiral Thrawn destroyed the doomed Outbound Flight expedition, the Chiss have found its wreckage deep in the Unknown Regions, and they invite Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker to witness its recovery firsthand. But the newlywed Jedi soon discover that not everything among their hosts is as it seems, and the peaceful expedition conceals a decades-old vendetta with deadly stakes. As alliances are tested across the icy reaches of Chiss space, the Skywalkers must uncover the truth before old grudges reignite into open war.
trivia: This is the first novel to depict Luke and Mara Jade as a married couple, and it quietly bridges the decade-plus gap between Zahn's Hand of Thrawn duology and the outbreak of the Yuuzhan Vong war.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught
creator: Michael A. Stackpole
notes: Book 2 of the New Jedi Order series; first half of the Dark Tide duology.
blurb: The Yuuzhan Vong invasion has begun, and the New Republic's warnings are met with disbelief and political infighting even as entire worlds fall silent. Luke Skywalker dispatches Jedi across the frontier to gather proof of the threat, sending Jacen to the ravaged world of Belkadan and Anakin and Mara Jade into danger on Dantooine. As the invaders' living technology and merciless warriors overrun everything in their path, the Jedi confront an enemy unlike any they have faced before, one the Force itself cannot fully perceive.
trivia: Michael A. Stackpole, best known for his X-wing novels, was tapped to escalate the Yuuzhan Vong threat from the first-contact events of Vector Prime into a full-scale, galaxy-wide invasion.

title: Star Wars: The Corellian Trilogy: Assault at Selonia
creator: Roger MacBride Allen
notes: Book 2 of 3 in the Corellian Trilogy, following Ambush at Corellia and preceding Showdown at Centerpoint.
blurb: Imprisoned by his own treacherous cousin on a Corellia teetering toward civil war, Han Solo must escape captivity and reach Selonia before Thracken Sal-Solo's plot to seize the system succeeds. There, Leia, Luke, and Lando race to unravel the secrets of the ancient Centerpoint Station and the mysterious Starbuster conspiracy threatening to plunge the Five Brothers into chaos. With old loyalties fracturing and a planet-killing weapon possibly at stake, the fate of the entire Corellian sector hangs on a desperate gamble.
trivia: The Corellian Trilogy introduced Centerpoint Station and fleshed out the five inhabited worlds of the Corellian system (the 'Five Brothers'), worldbuilding that later Legends authors continued to draw on for years afterward.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth
creator: Greg Keyes
notes: Book 8 of the New Jedi Order series; second half of the Edge of Victory duology, following Edge of Victory I: Conquest.
blurb: In the aftermath of the Yuuzhan Vong's brutal conquest of Yavin 4, a shattered band of Jedi younglings and their wounded leader, Anakin Solo, fight to survive behind enemy lines. Haunted by failure and forced into impossible choices, Anakin must find the resolve to lead if any of them are to escape the jungle moon alive. Amid captured warriors, uneasy alliances, and the invaders' merciless code of honor, a new kind of hero begins to emerge from the wreckage of defeat.
trivia: This novel completes Anakin Solo's arc from the preceding Conquest, marking his transformation from an impulsive teenager into a battle-hardened leader, a shift that shaped his prominent role for the rest of the New Jedi Order series.

title: Star Wars: Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 2 of the Dark Nest trilogy
blurb: The insectoid Killiks of the Unknown Regions are spreading across the galaxy, absorbing new members into their hive mind, among them Jacen and Jaina Solo. As Chief of State Cal Omas weighs war with the Chiss Ascendancy, a hidden Dark Jedi known only as the Unseen Queen manipulates both the Killik nests and the Jedi from the shadows. Luke Skywalker and Han Solo race to uncover her identity before the fragile peace collapses into full-scale war.
trivia: Lomi Plo, a minor Dark Jedi from the Yuuzhan Vong War era, is revealed in this book as the mysterious 'Unseen Queen' secretly controlling the Gorog Killik nest.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 2 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series
blurb: Two years after the war with the Yuuzhan Vong, the Galactic Alliance is fraying, and Jacen Solo is given command of a ruthless new security force meant to root out corruption. As Jacen's methods grow harder and darker, a mysterious bounty hunter targets his family with a vendetta rooted in Han Solo's past. Boba Fett re-enters the Solos' lives with a revelation that ties their bloodlines together forever.
trivia: Bloodlines is the novel that reveals Boba Fett as Jacen Solo's maternal grandfather, tying the bounty hunter permanently into the Solo family's history.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force
creator: James Luceno
notes: Final book (#19) of the 19-book New Jedi Order mega-series; concludes the Yuuzhan Vong War
blurb: The Yuuzhan Vong War reaches its climax as the fleets of the Galactic Alliance converge on Coruscant for a final reckoning with the invaders. Jacen Solo and Luke Skywalker search for a way to end the war without annihilating the Vong outright, even as political intrigue threatens to unravel the alliance from within. The fate of the galaxy, and the true nature of the Force itself, hangs on the outcome.
trivia: As the capstone to the 19-book New Jedi Order series, the original hardcover shipped with a bonus CD-ROM containing a full digital copy of the series-opening novel Vector Prime plus a roundtable interview with the NJO creative team.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion
creator: Sean Williams and Shane Dix
notes: Book 3 of the Force Heretic trilogy; book 17 of the New Jedi Order overall
blurb: Luke Skywalker, Jacen Solo, and the crew of the Jade Shadow finally reach the living planet Zonama Sekot, only to find it unwilling to join the fight against the Yuuzhan Vong. As the war builds toward a decisive confrontation at Esfandia, old allies and enemies collide in a battle that will help determine whether the galaxy can survive the invasion. Reunion closes out the Force Heretic trilogy on the eve of the war's final chapter.
trivia: The climactic Battle of Esfandia depicted in this novel takes place roughly two months before the events of The Unifying Force, according to the New Jedi Order's internal timeline.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Outcast
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 1 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series
blurb: In the wake of Jacen Solo's fall, the Jedi Order looks to Luke Skywalker's son Ben as a symbol of hope, until troubling visions of an ancient evil drive Luke into exile with Ben at his side. Meanwhile on Coruscant, a violent psychosis begins spreading among Jedi Knights, forcing the Order to confront a threat unlike anything it has faced before. The search for answers will take Luke and Ben to the strangest, most dangerous reaches of the galaxy.
trivia: Outcast opens with Luke Skywalker being formally exiled from Coruscant and the Jedi Order by the Jedi Council, a direct consequence of the events of Legacy of the Force.

title: Star Wars: Riptide
creator: Paul S. Kemp
notes: Standalone sequel to Crosscurrent; follows Jedi Knight Jaden Korr
blurb: Jedi Knight Jaden Korr thought his ordeal aboard the ancient derelict Fidelity was over, but the ship's dangerous cargo has followed him home. A cabal of criminals and Sith sympathizers wants what Jaden recovered, and they are willing to tear apart a peaceful world to get it. With allies scattered and time running out, Jaden must master a discovery from the deep past before an ancient evil resurfaces.
trivia: Riptide picks up immediately where Crosscurrent left off and gives Jaden Korr, a protagonist originally created as a player character in the video game Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy, one of his few starring roles in full-length novel form.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Conviction
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 7 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series
blurb: Luke and Ben Skywalker close in on Abeloth, the ancient entity whose corruption has shaken the Jedi Order to its foundations, cornering their quarry on the desolate world of Nam Chorios. At the same time, Tahiri Veila stands trial for the murder of Galactic Alliance officer Gilad Pellaeon, a case that could reshape the Jedi's standing in the galaxy. As old enemies forge unexpected alliances, the fight against Abeloth grows more desperate than ever.
trivia: Conviction debuted on the New York Times bestseller list, reaching number three during its second week of release in June 2011.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 5 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series
blurb: Jacen Solo's transformation into a Sith Lord demands one final, terrible price. As Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker close in on the truth behind the shadowy Lumiya, they uncover a betrayal far more personal and devastating than either expected. Sacrifice marks the point of no return in the war tearing the Solo-Skywalker family apart.
trivia: This is the novel in which Jacen Solo kills his aunt Mara Jade Skywalker, the act that completes his fall and confirms his identity as the Sith Lord Darth Caedus.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Tempest
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 3 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: As the Corellian insurgency spreads, a botched assassination attempt on Hapes's Queen Mother Tenel Ka is pinned on Han and Leia Solo, forcing them to flee the very Galactic Alliance they once served. Their son Jacen, now commanding his own Star Destroyer and enforcing order through the shadowy GAG, issues a warrant for his own parents' arrest. As old loyalties fracture across the Alliance, a hidden Sith presence quietly maneuvers Jacen ever closer to the dark side.
trivia: Tempest marks the operational debut of the Galactic Alliance Guard's flagship, the Star Destroyer Anakin Solo, named for Jacen and Jaina's late brother.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Exile
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 4 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: Branded a fugitive alongside her parents, Jaina Solo comes to a grim realization: she may be the only one who can stop her twin brother Jacen before his grip on the Galactic Alliance becomes absolute. Lacking his dark training, she travels to Mandalore to learn ruthless, unconventional combat from the family's old adversary, Boba Fett. Meanwhile the Corellian rebellion hardens into open war, and the Solo family's fractures deepen beyond repair.
trivia: In Exile, Jaina Solo apprentices under bounty hunter Boba Fett on Mandalore, one of the rare instances in the Expanded Universe of a Jedi training seriously under a non-Force-sensitive combat master to prepare for a duel with another Force user.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Omen
creator: Christie Golden
notes: Book 2 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series.
blurb: In the uneasy peace following the Second Galactic Civil War, Jedi Knights across the galaxy begin succumbing to a strange madness, hearing whispers that push them toward violence and self-destruction. Luke and his son Ben set off on a quest to understand what corrupted Jacen Solo, while back on Coruscant, Jaina, Han, and Leia confront the escalating crisis among their own ranks. Something ancient and unseen appears to be manipulating the Force itself.
trivia: Omen debuted at #4 on the New York Times bestseller list and quietly introduces the influence of Abeloth, the entity who would come to dominate the rest of the Fate of the Jedi series, years before she is named on the page.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Fury
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 7 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: Reeling from Mara Jade's murder, Luke Skywalker hunts for her killer while grief and suspicion tear at what remains of his family. Aboard the Anakin Solo, Darth Caedus turns a captured Yuuzhan Vong torture device on young Ben Skywalker, determined to break him and remake him as an ally. As the Corellian war grinds on, Jaina, Jag, and Zekk race to uncover the truth before Caedus claims another victim.
trivia: Fury shows Jacen Solo, now the Sith Lord Darth Caedus, using a captured Yuuzhan Vong coercion device to torture his own nephew Ben in a bid to turn him toward the dark side.

title: Star Wars: The New Jedi Order: The Final Prophecy
creator: Greg Keyes
notes: Book 18 (of 19) in The New Jedi Order series, near the climax of the Yuuzhan Vong War.
blurb: On the living planet Zonama Sekot, Luke Skywalker and Jacen Solo negotiate a desperate alliance as the world's biot ships offer the galaxy's best hope against the Yuuzhan Vong. When one of Sekot's living vessels is seized by the invaders, its secrets threaten to unravel the Vong's own hidden history. Meanwhile General Wedge Antilles finds his fleet stranded deep in enemy territory during a critical push to retake Bilbringi.
trivia: Greg Keyes wrote three New York Times bestselling entries in the New Jedi Order series; The Final Prophecy was also released as a limited Science Fiction Book Club exclusive hardcover in 2003.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Ascension
creator: Christie Golden
notes: Book 8 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series.
blurb: On the Sith world of Kesh, Vestara Khai is forced to choose between her family and the Skywalkers she has come to trust, a choice that turns deadly when her own father moves against her. As the entity Abeloth forges a dangerous alliance with the Lost Tribe of Sith, a brutal power struggle erupts that leaves the Sith order fractured. Luke and Ben press their hunt for Abeloth before she can turn her new allies loose on the galaxy.
trivia: Ascension features Vestara Khai killing her own father, Gavar Khai, after he executes her pet uvak as punishment for her sympathies toward Ben Skywalker and the Jedi.

title: Star Wars: Crucible
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Standalone novel; marketed as the final adventure of the classic trio (Luke, Han, and Leia); effectively the last Legends-continuity novel published chronologically before the Legends line was wound down following Disney's 2012 acquisition of Lucasfilm.
blurb: Decades after the fall of the Empire, Han and Leia arrive at old friend Lando Calrissian's Outer Rim mining venture just as a hostile takeover turns violent. What looks like corporate sabotage quickly reveals a far darker agenda, drawing in Luke Skywalker and pitting the trio against a pair of brilliant, ruthless adversaries with a decades-old vendetta against Han. It becomes one last galaxy-spanning adventure for three friends who have weathered nearly everything together.
trivia: Crucible is, chronologically, the last Star Wars Legends novel ever released, arriving in July 2013 after Disney's acquisition of Lucasfilm had already set in motion the rebranding of the old Expanded Universe as 'Legends.'

title: Star Wars: X-Wing: Mercy Kill
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 10, a later standalone revival of the 1990s X-Wing series, released in 2012 and set decades after the original nine volumes. It was the last Star Wars novel Aaron Allston completed before his death in February 2014.
blurb: Decades after the fall of the Empire, the legendary Wraith Squadron is quietly reassembled to expose a decorated Galactic Alliance general suspected of treason. Reuniting old comrades and untested recruits alike, Face Loran and Voort saBinring stage an elaborate campaign of deception, sabotage, and outright theft to draw their target into the open. Peeling back the general's carefully rebuilt identity proves as dangerous as any dogfight, forcing the Wraiths to rely on wit and improvisation rather than firepower. It's one last mission for a squadron built on outsmarting impossible odds.
trivia: It was the last Star Wars novel Aaron Allston completed before his death in February 2014, and serves as a one-off tenth entry to the X-Wing series, reuniting the cast decades after the original nine books.
inUniverseDate: ~44 ABY (main storyline; flashback sequences set in 13 ABY, 19 ABY, and 29 ABY)

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Backlash
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 4 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series.
blurb: With the Jedi Order fracturing under Chief of State Natasi Daala's crackdown, Luke and Ben Skywalker press deeper into the mystery of the Force psychosis spreading among young Jedi. Their search brings them into direct contact with a long-hidden faction of the Sith, whose ambitious apprentice, Vestara Khai, becomes an unlikely and dangerous companion. Meanwhile on Coruscant, Han and Leia risk everything to shield accused Jedi from Daala's growing purge. Old loyalties bend as Jedi and Sith are pushed toward an uneasy reckoning.
trivia: Backlash introduces the recurring Sith apprentice Vestara Khai, who becomes one of the pivotal supporting characters for the remainder of the Fate of the Jedi series.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Abyss
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 3 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series.
blurb: As a strange madness spreads through the ranks of the young Jedi, Luke Skywalker's search for its source leads him toward a mysterious, ancient evil buried in the galaxy's most treacherous region, the Maw. While Han and Leia work to protect their granddaughter Allana from political enemies circling Coruscant, Luke and Ben chase visions that blur the line between prophecy and trap. What they find in the Maw threatens to unravel everything the Jedi believe about the Force. The deeper they go, the harder it becomes to tell rescue from ambush.
trivia: Abyss marks the first full appearance of Abeloth, an ancient, shape-shifting Force entity who goes on to become the primary antagonist driving the remainder of the Fate of the Jedi series.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Invincible
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 9, the final book, of the Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: The Second Galactic Civil War reaches its brutal conclusion as Jacen Solo, now the Sith Lord Darth Caedus, tightens his grip on the Galactic Alliance by any means necessary. His own family stands against him: Han, Leia, Luke, and Jaina Solo must decide how far they are willing to go to end the threat he has become. As fleets clash and old bonds are tested past breaking, the fate of the galaxy rests on a confrontation between twins that no one will walk away from unchanged.
trivia: Invincible depicts the death of Jacen Solo, alias the Sith Lord Darth Caedus, at the hands of his twin sister Jaina, resolving the Skywalker-Solo family civil war storyline that had run through the entire nine-book series.

title: Star Wars: Millennium Falcon
creator: James Luceno
notes: Standalone novel centered on the history of the Millennium Falcon; bridges the Legacy of the Force/Crosscurrent-Riptide era and the start of the Fate of the Jedi series (its framing story falls immediately before Fate of the Jedi: Outcast).
blurb: Grieving the loss of their son Jacen, Han and Leia Solo find unexpected comfort in caring for his young daughter, Allana, until she discovers a strange, long-hidden device tucked inside the Falcon's battered hull. The find sends the family, along with C-3PO, chasing the ship's tangled history across decades and owners, from smugglers and pirates to war heroes and warlords. Each stop uncovers another secret the Falcon has carried in silence for years, drawing the attention of dangerous people who want that history to stay buried. What begins as a personal search for meaning becomes a galaxy-spanning chase with the ship itself as the prize.
trivia: The novel retroactively gives the Falcon a detailed ownership history predating Han Solo, including an earlier name, the Stellar Envoy, given to it by a Republic-era smuggling crew during the final year of the Clone Wars.
inUniverseDate: ~43 ABY (framing story; flashback sequences span 60 BBY to 5 BBY)

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Allies
creator: Christie Golden
notes: Book 5 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series (Outcast, Omen, Abyss, Backlash, Allies, Vortex, Conviction, Ascension, Apocalypse). Note: this is the fifth entry, not the sixth.
blurb: An uneasy truce forms between Luke Skywalker and the Sith fleet pursuing him, as both sides face a threat neither can defeat alone: the ancient, shapeshifting entity known as Abeloth. Luke and Ben journey deep into the deadly gravity well of the Maw to confront her, trusting allies they have every reason to doubt. On Coruscant, Han and Leia fight a different battle, defending the Jedi Order from Chief of State Daala's escalating crackdown as Tahiri Veila's trial threatens to seal the Order's fate. Trust and betrayal blur together as old enemies become uneasy partners.
trivia: Allies picks up immediately where Backlash leaves off and forges a temporary, deeply uneasy alliance between Luke Skywalker's Jedi and the Sith fleet pursuing him, a rare instance of open Jedi-Sith cooperation in the Legends continuity.

title: Star Wars: Crosscurrent
creator: Paul S. Kemp
notes: Standalone novel; directly precedes Riptide, which picks up immediately after Crosscurrent ends. Set after Legacy of the Force: Invincible and before Fate of the Jedi.
blurb: As the last embers of the Second Galactic Civil War fade, Jedi Knight Jaden Korr follows a powerful Force vision into deep space, expecting a routine rescue. Instead he finds a five-thousand-year-old Sith dreadnought, flung forward in time from the ancient Great Hyperspace War, carrying an army of Sith and a cargo capable of making the dark side nearly unstoppable. Racing against the ship's sole surviving ancient Jedi, who is determined to destroy it by any means, Jaden must decide how far to go to keep its power out of the wrong hands. What he uncovers threatens far more than his own crew; it endangers everything the Jedi Order has fought to rebuild.
trivia: Crosscurrent ties directly into the Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice e-novella and features a Sith dreadnought from the 5,000-year-old Great Hyperspace War era flung forward in time into the post-Legacy of the Force galaxy.
inUniverseDate: ~41 ABY (with a flashback sequence set during the Great Hyperspace War, ~5000 BBY)

title: Star Wars: Dark Nest I: The Joiner King
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 1 of the Dark Nest trilogy. Unlike most Star Wars EU series, all three Dark Nest novels were written solely by Troy Denning.
blurb: Years after the Yuuzhan Vong War, an insectoid hive-mind called the Killiks begins expanding across the Unknown Regions, drawing disaffected Jedi into its eerie telepathic collective. When Luke Skywalker sends a team to investigate the threat the Colony poses to an uneasy truce with the Chiss, he discovers that some of his own Jedi -- including a restless Jacen Solo -- are being seduced by the hive's promise of belonging over individuality. Old feelings resurface between Jaina Solo and Zekk even as the galaxy edges toward a new war.
trivia: Troy Denning wrote all three Dark Nest novels himself, a rarity for a Star Wars multi-book series, which were typically split among rotating authors.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Inferno
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 6 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: With Mara Jade Skywalker dead at an assassin's hand and the Galactic Alliance sliding into civil war, a grief-stricken Luke Skywalker hunts for his wife's killer. His nephew Jacen Solo, meanwhile, moves quickly to consolidate power as the secret architect of a new authoritarian order. As evidence mounts pointing toward Jacen himself, young Ben Skywalker's quiet investigation threatens to expose the truth before the war claims anyone else the family loves.
trivia: Inferno picks up directly from Mara Jade Skywalker's assassination at the close of the previous novel, Sacrifice -- a killing later revealed to have been carried out by her own nephew, Jacen Solo.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 9, the final novel, of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series. Concludes the arc begun with Jacen Solo's fall in Legacy of the Force.
blurb: The Skywalker family's long war against the ancient, shape-shifting entity Abeloth reaches its climax as Luke, Ben, and Jaina lead a fractious alliance of Jedi, Sith, and Galactic Alliance forces against her on Coruscant. Vestara Khai must finally choose between the Sith order that raised her and the boy she has come to love, while the spirits of the dead -- including Jacen and Mara -- offer guidance from beyond the grave. The fate of Jacen's daughter Allana, and the galaxy's uneasy peace, hangs on the outcome.
trivia: In the novel's climax, the Force ghost of Jacen Solo reconciles with his sister Jaina -- who killed him at the end of Legacy of the Force -- revealing that his fall to the dark side was ultimately an attempt to prevent a future in which his own daughter, Allana, became a Sith.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Revelation
creator: Karen Traviss
notes: Book 8 of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series.
blurb: As the Galactic Alliance's war against Corellia grinds on, Jacen Solo -- now the masked warlord Darth Caedus -- tightens his grip on power through fear and surveillance, alienating even his closest allies. Luke and Ben Skywalker piece together the full extent of Jacen's fall, while Jaina Solo trains under a secretive mentor to become the one Jedi capable of stopping her own brother. Trust within the Skywalker-Solo family fractures beyond repair as the war edges toward its bloodiest turn.
trivia: Revelation was Karen Traviss's last major mainline Star Wars novel; she departed the franchise not long after, citing creative differences with the direction of The Clone Wars continuity.

title: Star Wars: Dark Nest III: The Swarm War
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 3, the concluding novel, of the Dark Nest trilogy.
blurb: The simmering conflict between the expansionist Killik hive and the Chiss Ascendancy erupts into open warfare, dragging Luke Skywalker's Jedi into a fight none of them wanted. Jacen Solo's dangerous gambit to manipulate both sides toward peace puts everyone he loves at risk, forcing Han and Leia to confront how far their son is willing to bend the truth for what he believes is the greater good. As the fighting ends, a secret that will shape the next generation of the Solo family finally comes to light.
trivia: The Swarm War reveals that Jacen Solo and Tenel Ka secretly had a daughter, Allana, whose growth Tenel Ka slowed using the Force to conceal the child's paternity -- a plot thread that would echo through the rest of the Legends continuity.

title: Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi: Vortex
creator: Troy Denning
notes: Book 6 of the 9-book Fate of the Jedi series.
blurb: On the run with the rogue Sith apprentice Vestara Khai, Luke and Ben Skywalker find themselves caught between a Sith armada hunting them and the shape-shifting horror Abeloth, who has infiltrated their inner circle with unnerving ease. Trapped on the isolated moon Pydyr, the fragile, uneasy alliance between Jedi and Sith factions is tested as old loyalties clash with the need to simply survive. Vestara must decide how far she is willing to go to protect Ben, even as her Sith masters demand his death.
trivia: A key twist in Vortex reveals that the ancient entity Abeloth faked her own death and secretly took the place of a companion aboard the Skywalkers' ship, the Jade Shadow, undetected for a stretch of the novel.

title: Star Wars: Legacy of the Force: Betrayal
creator: Aaron Allston
notes: Book 1, the opening novel, of the 9-book Legacy of the Force series, launching shortly after the New Jedi Order era.
blurb: Years after the devastating war with the Yuuzhan Vong, the fragile peace of the Galactic Alliance begins to crack as Corellia chafes under centralized rule. Jacen Solo and young Ben Skywalker undertake a covert mission to Adumar that draws Jacen deeper into a web of visions and dark temptation spun by the mysterious Lumiya. As Luke wrestles with premonitions of a shadow rising within his own family, the first cracks appear in a hero who will soon become something else entirely.
trivia: Ahead of writing Betrayal, author Aaron Allston prepared a lengthy internal document -- the so-called 'Vergere Compendium' -- outlining the dark-side mentor Vergere's earlier appearances to keep Jacen Solo's fall consistent with prior New Jedi Order continuity.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Tales of the Jedi Volume 1
creator: Tom Veitch, Kevin J. Anderson (writers); Chris Gossett, Dario Carrasco Jr., David Roach (artists)
notes: Collects Dark Horse Comics (1992) #7-9, Dark Horse Insider #15-20, Tales of the Jedi: The Golden Age of the Sith #0-5, The Fall of the Sith Empire #1-5, and Knights of the Old Republic #1-5. Approx. 440 pages. Published October 31, 2007.
blurb: Millennia before Luke Skywalker ever held a lightsaber, the galaxy burned in the first great war between Jedi and Sith. This volume traces the fall of the ancient Sith Empire under exiled dark siders Naga Sadow and Ludo Kressh, then follows Ulic Qel-Droma and Nomi Sunrider as a new generation of Jedi confronts the rising Krath cult on Onderon. It is the deep-history foundation of the entire Tales of the Jedi saga.
trivia: The Golden Age of the Sith arc reintroduced the ancient Sith Empire and warlord Naga Sadow to Star Wars continuity, ancient-history material that BioWare later drew on heavily when building the Knights of the Old Republic video games.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Tales of the Jedi Volume 2
creator: Tom Veitch, Kevin J. Anderson (writers); Chris Gossett, Christopher Moeller, Andrew Pepoy (artists)
notes: Collects The Freedon Nadd Uprising #1-2, Dark Lords of the Sith #1-6, The Sith War #1-6, and Redemption #1-5. Approx. 464 pages. Published April 2008.
blurb: The Tales of the Jedi saga reaches its climax as the spirit of the long-dead Sith Lord Freedon Nadd stirs a rebellion, drawing the Jedi Order into the catastrophic Great Sith War. Exar Kun's fall and Ulic Qel-Droma's seduction to the dark side shatter the Jedi ranks, and only years later, in quiet exile, does Ulic find a final chance at redemption through a mysterious young woman named Vima. This volume closes out one of the foundational eras of Star Wars Legends history.
trivia: Tales of the Jedi: Redemption, the closing miniseries collected here, is set roughly ten years after the Sith War and gives disgraced Sith apprentice Ulic Qel-Droma his only real shot at atonement in the entire Expanded Universe.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Clone Wars Volume 1—The Republic Goes to War
creator: John Ostrander, Haden Blackman, Scott Allie, Randy Stradley (writers); Jan Duursema, Brian Ching, Tomas Giorello, Brandon Badeaux, Stephen Thompson (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: Republic #49-54, 61, 63, and 67, plus the one-shots Jedi: Mace Windu, Jedi: Shaak Ti, Jedi: Aayla Secura, and Jedi: Count Dooku. 408 pages. Published August 22, 2012.
blurb: The Clone Wars erupt across the galaxy in the stories published immediately after Attack of the Clones. Obi-Wan Kenobi leads clone troopers into the storm-lashed defense of Kamino, Anakin Skywalker and Mace Windu are thrust into command, and Quinlan Vos walks a dangerous line as a spy inside Count Dooku's ranks. This volume captures the Jedi Order's uneasy transformation from peacekeepers into generals.
trivia: A Free Comic Book Day 2006 story, "Routine Valor," was originally solicited for inclusion in this omnibus but was pulled before the final printing.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: The Other Sons of Tatooine
creator: Jeremy Barlow, Mike W. Barr, Paul Chadwick, Michael A. Stackpole, Randy Stradley, Rob Williams (writers); Tomas Giorello, Doug Wheatley, Brandon Badeaux, Gary Erskine, Davide Fabbri (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron #1/2, Star Wars: Empire #8-9, 12, 15-18, 23, and 36-40, and Star Wars: Rebellion #1-5. 440 pages. Published March 21, 2012.
blurb: Luke Skywalker was not the only farm kid from Tatooine who found himself swept into the galaxy's war. This collection follows Biggs Darklighter's path into the Rebel Alliance and Janek "Tank" Sunber's very different choice to serve the Empire, alongside a side story starring the cantina-dwelling smuggler BoShek. Three very different sons of the same desert world, three very different roads through the Galactic Civil War.
trivia: BoShek, whose backstory anchors part of this omnibus, appears on-screen in A New Hope for only a few seconds in the Mos Eisley cantina before being fleshed out decades later in these comics.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: At War with the Empire Volume 1
creator: Scott Allie, Randy Stradley, Paul Chadwick, Jeremy Barlow, Ron Marz (writers); Davide Fabbri, Adriana Melo, Patrick Blaine, Brian Ching, Ryan Benjamin (artists)
notes: Collects seventeen issues of Star Wars: Empire (2002-2006): #1-6, part of #9, #10-11, #13-14, #19-22, #24-25, and #31. 412 pages. Published March 9, 2011.
blurb: In the chaotic days after the Death Star's destruction, the fledgling Rebel Alliance and the wounded Empire both scramble to find their footing. Rogue Imperial officers plot to assassinate Darth Vader and the Emperor, Princess Leia faces the grim costs of open war, and Vader himself must survive a deadly test of will against savage beasts on a forgotten world. This volume opens the long-running Empire series' chronicle of the early Galactic Civil War.
trivia: Star Wars: Empire, launched in 2002, was Dark Horse's first ongoing monthly series to focus specifically on the years immediately surrounding the original Star Wars film rather than earlier or later eras.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Droids
creator: Dan Thorsland, Ryder Windham (writers); Bill Hughes, Andy Mushynsky (artists)
notes: Collects every Dark Horse Droids story: The Kalarba Adventures, Rebellion, the previously uncollected Seasons of Revolt, and the Droids Special: The Protocol Offensive. 440 pages. Published June 18, 2008.
blurb: Long before they wandered into Luke Skywalker's life, R2-D2 and C-3PO served a long line of owners across the galaxy's rougher corners. This omnibus follows the droids through run-ins with pirates, bounty hunters, and the criminal Olag Greck during their years working for young mechanic Thall Joben and pilot Kea Moll. It is the complete, standalone chronicle of the droids' misadventures before A New Hope.
trivia: The included story "The Protocol Offensive" was plotted by Anthony Daniels, the actor who has played C-3PO on screen since 1977.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Quinlan Vos—Jedi in Darkness
creator: John Ostrander (writer); Jan Duursema, Davide Fabbri, Ramon F. Bachs, Ray Kryssing (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars (1998) #19-26 and #32-45. Over 500 pages, including roughly 132 pages that had been out of print for more than a decade prior to this collection. Published December 2, 2010.
blurb: Before he was a mind-wiped amnesiac spy or a battle-hardened general of the Clone Wars, Quinlan Vos was a gifted but reckless Jedi Knight drawn again and again toward the dark side. This omnibus traces his descent into slavery on Dathomir, his tangled loyalties as an undercover operative, and his growing bond with fellow Jedi Aayla Secura in the years leading up to the galaxy's collapse into war. It is the definitive collection of one of the Jedi Order's most conflicted knights.
trivia: This omnibus marks the first extended comic appearance of Aayla Secura, who was created for these Star Wars: Republic stories years before actress Amy Allen brought her to the screen in Attack of the Clones.
inUniverseDate: ~32-22 BBY (with a flashback arc to the Stark Hyperspace War, c. 44 BBY)

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Dark Times Volume 1
creator: Randy Stradley (writer); Douglas Wheatley, Dave Ross, Lui Antonio (art)
notes: Collects Star Wars: Republic #79-80, and Dark Times #0-12 (story arcs 'The Path to Nowhere,' 'Parallels,' and 'Vector'). 344 pages.
blurb: In the terrifying weeks after Order 66, two Jedi choose survival over surrender. Dass Jennir, stripped of his lightsaber's certainty, drifts through the criminal underworld aboard the smuggling ship Uhumele, while Master K'Kruhk shepherds a handful of orphaned younglings across a galaxy that now hunts them. As the newly crowned Emperor tightens his grip and Darth Vader tests the limits of his new power, old ideals collide with a very dark new order.
trivia: Writer Randy Stradley scripted the series under two pseudonyms, 'Welles Hartley' for story credits and 'Mick Harrison' for scripting, a bit of misdirection meant to keep the character-focused, morally gray tone of Dark Times distinct from his other Star Wars work.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Dark Times Volume 2
creator: Randy Stradley (writer); Douglas Wheatley, Gabriel Guzman (art)
notes: Collects Dark Times #13-32 (story arcs 'Blue Harvest,' 'Out of the Wilderness,' 'Fire Carrier,' and 'A Spark Remains'). 456 pages.
blurb: Dass Jennir trades his Jedi robes for a mercenary's blaster, but a job gone wrong draws the attention of Darth Vader himself. Meanwhile K'Kruhk's fugitive Padawans find an uneasy refuge on a war-scarred world, even as Vader closes in on any surviving spark of the Jedi Order. The Dark Times saga races toward a desperate, unresolved confrontation between hunted and hunter.
trivia: 'A Spark Remains,' the arc that closes this volume and the ongoing Dark Times series, shipped its final issue in December 2013 without fully resolving its cliffhangers, as Dark Horse's Star Wars comics license wound down ahead of the license transferring to Marvel Comics in 2015.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: A Long Time Ago.... Volume One
creator: Roy Thomas, Don Glut, Archie Goodwin, Mary Jo Duffy (writers); Howard Chaykin, Tom Palmer, Terry Austin, Walt Simonson (art)
notes: Collects Marvel's Star Wars (1977) #1-27, including the six-issue adaptation of A New Hope. 480 pages.
blurb: Long before Dark Horse ever touched a lightsaber, Marvel Comics carried Star Wars into the newsstand age. This first volume opens with the comics adaptation of A New Hope and follows Luke, Leia, Han, and the droids into a run of freewheeling, occasionally strange adventures dreamed up between films. It's the galaxy far, far away as 1977 imagined it: brash, colorful, and unmistakably of its era.
trivia: Marvel's Star Wars #1 (April 1977), reprinted in this volume, sold so well that it went back for multiple additional print runs and is widely credited with helping keep Marvel Comics financially solvent during a rocky stretch in the late 1970s.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: A Long Time Ago.... Volume Two
creator: Archie Goodwin, Chris Claremont (writers); Michael Golden, Terry Austin, Al Williamson, Walter Simonson (art)
notes: Collects Marvel's Star Wars (1977) #28-49 and Star Wars Annual #1, including the six-issue adaptation of The Empire Strikes Back. 480 pages.
blurb: The Rebellion regroups, and Marvel's original creative team keeps the adventures coming between films. This volume carries the story through the comics adaptation of The Empire Strikes Back, plus a run of standalone tales filling the gap before and after Han's fate is sealed in carbonite. Michael Golden's artwork and Archie Goodwin's scripts anchor some of the run's most fondly remembered issues.
trivia: Marvel's Empire Strikes Back adaptation (serialized here across issues #39-44) hit newsstands in the same month as the film's June 1980 release, meaning some readers learned Darth Vader was Luke's father from the comic rather than the theater.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: A Long Time Ago.... Volume 3
creator: Chris Claremont, Michael Fleisher, Archie Goodwin, David Michelinie (writers); Walter Simonson, Al Williamson, Tom Palmer (art)
notes: Collects Marvel's Star Wars (1977) #50-67 and Star Wars Annual #2. 480 pages.
blurb: Fresh from the trauma of Hoth and Bespin, Luke, Leia, and the crew of the Millennium Falcon scatter across the galaxy while Darth Vader hunts his son in earnest. This volume gathers a run of standalone adventures produced in the year after The Empire Strikes Back, including the debut of a mysterious new adversary who will loom over the saga for years to come. Walter Simonson's dynamic artwork headlines a stretch widely regarded as a high point of the Marvel run.
trivia: Star Wars #56 (February 1982), collected in this volume, marks the first appearance of Imperial pilot Shira Brie, the character who would later be revealed as the Dark Lady of the Sith, Lumiya.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: A Long Time Ago.... Volume 4
creator: Jo Duffy, Archie Goodwin, David Michelinie (writers); Ron Frenz, Gene Day, Kerry Gammill, Klaus Janson, Carmine Infantino, Al Williamson, Tom Palmer (art)
notes: Collects Marvel's Star Wars (1977) #68-85, Star Wars Annual #3, and the original four-issue Return of the Jedi adaptation. 576 pages.
blurb: As the Rebellion prepares its final assault on the second Death Star, this volume collects the original four-issue Marvel adaptation of Return of the Jedi alongside the surrounding issues of the ongoing series. Luke completes his training, Vader wrestles with his loyalties, and the fall of the Empire plays out through the same comic that reached newsstands the year the film premiered. It's classic-era Star Wars comics at their most consequential.
trivia: The four-issue Return of the Jedi adaptation collected here was drawn by Al Williamson working from an early cut of the film and production stills, which is why a few small character and staging details differ slightly from the movie's final theatrical version.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: A Long Time Ago.... Volume 5
creator: Jo Duffy (writer); Ron Frenz, Cynthia Martin (art)
notes: Collects Marvel's Star Wars (1977) #86-107, the final US-published issues of the original series. 568 pages.
blurb: With the Empire in ruins and the galaxy still finding its footing, Marvel's Star Wars series spins increasingly personal stories for its final stretch. This fifth and final volume collects the remaining twenty-two issues published in North America, introducing new threats to the fledgling New Republic before the series wrapped in 1986. It's the last word on Marvel's pioneering original run, five years before Dark Horse would pick up the license.
trivia: Star Wars #107 (September 1986), 'All Together Now,' closed out Marvel's original run without much fanfare; the license would sit dormant for five years until Dark Horse Comics acquired Star Wars comics rights in 1991.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Boba Fett
creator: John Wagner, Mike Kennedy, Ron Marz, Thomas Andrews (writers); Ian Gibson, Cam Kennedy, Carlos Meglia, Adriana Melo, Francisco Ruiz Velasco (artists)
notes: Collects Boba Fett: Enemy of the Empire; Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika; Empire #7 "Sacrifice" and #28 "Wreckage"; Boba Fett: Overkill; Boba Fett: Salvage; Boba Fett: Twin Engines of Destruction; Boba Fett: Death, Lies, and Treachery; and Boba Fett: Agent of Doom. 494 pages.
blurb: The galaxy's most feared bounty hunter gets the full-career treatment in this collection of nine stand-alone stories, from a tense standoff with Darth Vader himself to a chaotic three-way scramble for a legendary relic alongside Han Solo, Lando, and Chewbacca. Later tales find Fett years removed from his fall into the Sarlacc, still hunting and still guarding a reputation that refuses to die. Nine different creative teams give Fett nine very different faces, but the cold professionalism stays constant throughout.
trivia: The "Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika" story crams an unusual number of classic-trilogy scoundrels into one job, with Han Solo, Chewbacca, Lando Calrissian, Greedo, and Boba Fett all separately hired by rival Hutt lords to retrieve the same artifact.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Knights of the Old Republic Volume 1
creator: John Jackson Miller (writer); Brian Ching, Travel Foreman, Dustin Weaver, Harvey Tolibao (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #0-18. 424 pages.
blurb: Padawan Zayne Carrick flees across the galaxy as a hunted man, framed for a massacre his own Jedi Masters actually committed. Teaming up with a band of misfit companions, he stays one step ahead of assassins and old allies alike while trying to uncover why his teachers wanted him dead. Set centuries before the rise of the Empire, it lays the groundwork for the era later explored in the Knights of the Old Republic video games.
trivia: Issue #0 of the series was distributed as a Free Comic Book Day giveaway in 2006, serving as many readers' introduction to Zayne Carrick before the ongoing series launched.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Knights of the Old Republic Volume 2
creator: John Jackson Miller (writer); Brian Ching, Bong Dazo, Scott Hepburn, Alan Robinson, Dustin Weaver (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #19-37, including the "Vector" crossover arc. 440 pages.
blurb: Still a fugitive, Zayne Carrick is dragged deeper into galaxy-spanning intrigue as ancient Sith artifacts, a mad industrialist's doomsday scheme, and the shadowy Jedi Covenant all converge on him and his crew. Old wounds with his former Master come to a head as the true architect behind the frame-up is finally revealed. The volume also folds in the multi-series "Vector" crossover, linking this ancient-era story to Dark Horse's Dark Times and Legacy titles set thousands of years later.
trivia: The "Vector" arc collected here is a rare four-part crossover event that threads a single storyline through Knights of the Old Republic, Dark Times, and Legacy, connecting comics set thousands of years apart in the Star Wars timeline.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Knights of the Old Republic Volume 3
creator: John Jackson Miller (writer); Ron Chan, Brian Ching, Bong Dazo, Andrea Mutti, Dean Zachary (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #38-50 and the 5-issue Knights of the Old Republic: War miniseries. 416 pages.
blurb: Zayne Carrick's long fight to clear his name reaches its climax as old enemies close in and the true scale of his former Masters' betrayal finally comes to light. The volume closes out the ongoing series before shifting into the War tie-in miniseries, which pulls the cast into the opening moves of the Mandalorian Wars. It's the final chapter of the story that set the stage for the Knights of the Old Republic games.
trivia: The Knights of the Old Republic: War miniseries collected here was published in 2012 to tie in with the launch of the Star Wars: The Old Republic MMO, bridging the ongoing comic's cast directly into the game's backstory.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 1
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Michael A. Stackpole, Mike Baron, Darko Macan (writers); John Nadeau and others (artists)
notes: Collects X-Wing: Rogue Leader #1-3, X-Wing Rogue Squadron #1-8, and Star Wars Handbook #1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron. 296 pages.
blurb: Fresh off the destruction of the second Death Star, Wedge Antilles rebuilds Rogue Squadron into the New Republic's premier strike force. This first volume introduces a new roster of pilots and chases down Imperial holdouts who refuse to accept the war is over, mixing dogfighting action with the growing pains of a fledgling Republic. A character handbook at the back rounds out the roster of Rogues old and new.
trivia: The mid-1990s issues collected here were written by Michael A. Stackpole, Mike Baron, and Darko Macan, adapting the same era of the Rogue Squadron novels into comic form.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 2
creator: Michael A. Stackpole (writer), with Jan Strnad and Ryder Windham; John Nadeau, Gary Erskine, Jordi Ensign (artists)
notes: Collects the X-Wing Rogue Squadron Special plus X-Wing Rogue Squadron #9-20, comprising "Battleground: Tatooine," "The Warrior Princess," and "Requiem for a Rogue." 288 pages.
blurb: Rogue Squadron keeps hunting down Imperial remnants across three linked missions: a chaotic hunt for a weapons cache on Tatooine that stirs up an old enemy, a diplomatic crisis on Eiattu that exposes a hidden royal past, and a rescue mission that drags the squadron into an ancient, dark presence. Along the way the team loses members and gains new ones, cementing Rogue Squadron's reputation as the New Republic's go-to unit for the missions nobody else wants.
trivia: "The Warrior Princess" arc collected here reveals that Rogue Squadron pilot Plourr Ilo is secretly Eiattan royalty, a twist that sends her away from the squadron to reclaim her homeworld's throne.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3
creator: Michael A. Stackpole (writer); John Nadeau, Steve Crespo, Jim Hall (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron #21-35: 'In the Empire's Service,' 'The Making of Baron Fel,' 'Family Ties,' 'Masquerade,' and 'Mandatory Retirement.' 360 pages, full color.
blurb: With the Empire fractured and its Interim-Emperor on the run, Wedge Antilles and Rogue Squadron are handed the mission of a lifetime: seizing Coruscant itself for the New Republic. Standing in their way is Ysanne Isard, the ruthless director of Imperial Intelligence, and Baron Soontir Fel, the finest TIE pilot the Empire has ever produced. As old loyalties are tested and new pilots earn their wings, the Rogues discover that reclaiming the galactic capital may cost them more than they bargained for.
trivia: This is the final volume of Dark Horse's original ongoing X-Wing Rogue Squadron series, and the story reveals that Darth Vader had Baron Soontir Fel's TIE interceptor specially modified after Fel kept out-flying him in Imperial simulations.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Shadows of the Empire
creator: John Wagner, Steve Perry, Timothy Zahn (writers); Kilian Plunkett, Carlos Ezquerra, John Nadeau, Ron Randall (artists)
notes: Collects the 6-issue Shadows of the Empire comic miniseries (1996) plus Star Wars: Mara Jade - By the Emperor's Hand #0-6 and Shadows of the Empire: Evolution #1-5. 408 pages, full color.
blurb: Han Solo lies frozen in carbonite, bound for Jabba the Hutt's palace, while Luke Skywalker and Leia Organa race to intercept Boba Fett before the bounty hunter completes his delivery. Watching from the shadows is Prince Xizor, the cunning crime lord of Black Sun, who schemes to destroy Skywalker and topple Darth Vader in the Emperor's favor. This volume also follows a droid assassin's search for redemption in Evolution, and the final, fatal mission of the Emperor's own Hand, Mara Jade.
