trivia: The original Shadows of the Empire comic was part of a unique 1996 multimedia project released with no accompanying film, filling the story gap between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi across a novel, video game, soundtrack, and toy line simultaneously.
inUniverseDate: ~3-3.5 ABY (main story); backup material spans ~4-11 ABY

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Rise of the Sith
series: Prequel Era One-Shots and Miniseries (Star Wars: Republic)
creator: Mike Kennedy, Ron Marz, Ryder Windham, Randy Stradley, Jan Strnad, Dean Motter (writers); Ramon Bachs, Jan Duursema, Davide Fabbri, Lucas Marangon, John Nadeau, and others (artists)
notes: Collects The Aurorient Express, Last Stand on Ord Mantell, Aurra's Song, Jedi Council: Acts of War, Prelude to Rebellion (Star Wars: Republic #0-5), and the Darth Maul miniseries (#1-4). 448 pages, full color.
blurb: Long before the Clone Wars, the Jedi Order quietly kept the peace across a galaxy that had all but forgotten the Sith. Follow a young Obi-Wan Kenobi and his master Qui-Gon Jinn on early missions of intrigue and survival, walk the halls of the Jedi Council with Mace Windu and Ki-Adi-Mundi as new threats emerge, and trace the grim origins of the bounty hunter Aurra Sing. Finally, ride alongside Darth Maul himself as the Sith apprentice erases every trace of his Master's plans before they can be discovered.
trivia: The Prelude to Rebellion arc collected here was the launch storyline of Dark Horse's ongoing prequel-era series and is one of the earliest comics to explore Ki-Adi-Mundi and Mace Windu as protagonists in their own right.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Emissaries and Assassins
creator: Ryder Windham and others (writers); various artists including Davide Fabbri and Ramon F. Bachs
notes: Collects the four Episode I Adventures one-shots (Anakin Skywalker, Queen Amidala, Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi), Star Wars: Republic #7-18 ('Outlander' and 'Emissaries to Malastare'), and Star Wars: Jango Fett - Open Seasons #1-4. 464 pages, full color.
blurb: In the uneasy calm following the Battle of Naboo, the Jedi Order finds itself drawn deeper into a galaxy sliding toward war. Anakin Skywalker, Padme Amidala, Qui-Gon Jinn, and Obi-Wan Kenobi each face trials that echo the events of The Phantom Menace, while members of the Jedi Council are dispatched to the volatile world of Malastare and beyond. At the same time, a young Jango Fett rises from a shattered Mandalorian past to become the galaxy's deadliest gun for hire, and the eventual template for a clone army still to come.
trivia: This omnibus marks the first time the four Episode I Adventures one-shots were reassembled in the story order originally intended by their creators, after having previously only circulated as scattered single issues.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Menace Revealed
creator: Timothy Truman, Haden Blackman, Ryder Windham, Jason Hall (writers); Davide Fabbri, Ramon Bachs, Timothy Truman, Christian Dalla Vecchia, and others (artists)
notes: Collects Star Wars #27 'Starcrash,' Star Wars: The Hunt for Aurra Sing, Star Wars: Jedi Quest #1-4, Star Wars: Starfighter - Crossbones #1-3, Star Wars Episode II Hasbro Minicomics #1-4, and Dark Horse Extra material ('Heart of Fire' and 'Poison Moon'). 384 pages, full color.
blurb: Between the fall of the Trade Federation on Naboo and the gathering storm of the Clone Wars, the galaxy grows more dangerous by the day. A young Anakin Skywalker learns hard lessons about fear and duty on his first assignments as a Padawan, while pirates, slavers, and hired killers carve out fortunes in the chaos the Jedi are stretched thin to contain. This omnibus gathers Dark Horse's rarest and most obscure tales from the years between Episode I and Episode II in one volume for the first time.
trivia: Dark Horse billed this as its largest single omnibus of never-before-collected and out-of-print Star Wars material at the time, and it remains one of the few volumes in the classic Star Wars Omnibus line that Marvel Comics never reprinted after regaining the Star Wars comics license in 2015.

title: Star Wars Omnibus: Early Victories
series: Post-A New Hope One-Shots and Miniseries
creator: Darko Macan (Vader's Quest); Louise Simonson (River of Chaos); Terry Austin and Chris Sprouse (Splinter of the Mind's Eye adaptation); Bruce Jones and others (Shadow Stalker, Tales from Mos Eisley); various artists
notes: Collects Vader's Quest #1-4, River of Chaos #1-4, Splinter of the Mind's Eye #1-4, Shadow Stalker, and Tales from Mos Eisley. 336 pages, full color. Collects post-A New Hope Rebellion-era stories, not the Clone Wars-era Republic series.
blurb: Fresh off the destruction of the first Death Star, Luke Skywalker and the fledgling Rebel Alliance quickly learn that one victory does not end a war. Darth Vader hunts for the pilot who humiliated him at Yavin, uncovering a secret that will haunt him for years, while Luke and Leia face smugglers, cultists, and Imperial agents across the Outer Rim in Splinter of the Mind's Eye and beyond. This collection gathers some of the earliest post-Yavin Star Wars comics, many long out of print before this omnibus brought them together.
trivia: Splinter of the Mind's Eye adapts Alan Dean Foster's 1978 novel of the same name, which George Lucas originally commissioned as a low-budget sequel to A New Hope in case the film's box-office success wasn't enough to greenlight The Empire Strikes Back.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars — Ultimate Library Box Set (20 Books)
creator: DK Publishing (Catherine Saunders, Simon Beecroft, Clare Hibbert, Laura Buller, Lindsay Kent, Ryder Windham, Shari Last, Benjamin Harper, Tori Kosara, et al.)
notes: DK boxed slipcase set bundling 20 previously-separate DK Readers titles (Beware the Dark Side, Battle for Naboo, Darth Maul: Sith Apprentice, Death Star Battles, Jedi Heroes, etc.), marketed as "Star Wars Readers Ultimate Library Collection: 20 Books Box Gift Set." Cover art and several included titles draw on Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008 animated series) content, which Lucasfilm designates in-universe Canon, hence the Canon tag, though the box set itself is a real-world nonfiction reader product.
blurb: A DK boxed set collecting 20 individual Star Wars reader volumes spanning DK Readers Levels 1 through 3, packaged in a slipcase and topped with a "CONTAINS 20 GREAT BOOKS!" sticker. The cover art draws on Clone Wars-era imagery of Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano, and the included titles range from Darth Maul to Death Star battles, aimed at young readers building up their skills.
rating: No reliable rating found for this specific box-set edition
trivia: Every book in the set was originally sold as a standalone DK Readers volume before being repackaged into this slipcased collection; titles like "Darth Maul: Sith Apprentice" and "Battle for Naboo" tie the set to the prequel/Clone Wars era rather than just the original trilogy.

title: Star Wars: Essential Library Box Set (15 Books)
creator: DK Publishing (Simon Beecroft, Laura Buller, Kate Simkins, Shari Last, Lindsay Kent, et al.)
notes: DK boxed slipcase set of 15 DK Readers titles, cover featuring Yoda and a "CONTAINS 15 GREAT BOOKS!" sticker. Included titles span both the original trilogy (The Story of Darth Vader, Death Star Battles) and prequel content (Ready, Set, Podrace!), so it is not tied specifically to one era.
blurb: A companion DK boxed set to the larger 20-book Ultimate Library, this "Essential Library" collection bundles 15 shorter DK Reader volumes across three reading levels in a slipcase with a Yoda-featured cover. Titles range from Obi-Wan Kenobi and Darth Vader profiles to a podracing adventure, aimed at building young readers' skills through Star Wars stories.
rating: Goodreads 4.00/5 based on only 1 rating (sample too small to be meaningful)
trivia: At full retail, the 15 individual books each cost £4.99, meaning this boxed set (RRP £74.85) was priced as a straight bundle of the standalone titles rather than a discounted collector's edition.

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (UK paperback novelization)
creator: James Kahn (based on the screenplay by Lawrence Kasdan and George Lucas)
notes: Vintage UK paperback printing of the Return of the Jedi novelization, published by Futura Publications (Orbit imprint) with an 8-page color photo insert from the film, matching the "WITH 8 PAGES OF FABULOUS COLOUR" cover text. Distinct from the standard US Del Rey movie-poster-cover edition (already catalogued separately) — a different physical printing, not a duplicate.
blurb: The 1983 UK paperback printing of James Kahn's novelization of Return of the Jedi, published to tie in with the film's release and featuring an 8-page color photo insert, flagged on the cover as "WITH 8 PAGES OF FABULOUS COLOUR." It adapts Lawrence Kasdan and George Lucas's screenplay for the trilogy's closing chapter, including some scene and dialogue details that differ slightly from the finished film.
rating: Goodreads 4.07/5 (~11,200 ratings, aggregated across all editions/printings of the work)
trivia: James Kahn wrote the novelization from an earlier draft of the shooting script before the film's final cut was locked, which is why the book contains minor differences from the released movie.

title: Star Wars: From the Adventures of Luke Skywalker (Special Young Readers' Edition)
creator: George Lucas (ghostwritten by Alan Dean Foster)
notes: Abridged adaptation, for younger readers, of the original November 1976 Ballantine Books novelization of the first Star Wars film (later retitled A New Hope). Credited solely to George Lucas but actually ghostwritten by Alan Dean Foster from Lucas's screenplay.
blurb: An abridged, "Special Young Readers' Edition" of the original Star Wars novelization, credited to George Lucas though actually ghostwritten by Alan Dean Foster. Trimmed and simplified for a younger audience, it retells Luke Skywalker's journey from moisture farmer to Rebel hero in A New Hope, preserving added backstory not present in the film, such as the Journal of the Whills prologue.
rating: Goodreads 3.91/5 (~1,721 ratings, reflects the general work across editions)
trivia: The full-length original novelization sold out its first 500,000-copy print run by February 1977, three months before the film even opened in theaters, helping build anticipation ahead of the movie's release.

title: The Jedi Master's Quizbook
creator: Rusty Miller (compiler)
notes: Published by Del Rey, October 1982. Contains 425 trivia questions covering Star Wars (A New Hope) and The Empire Strikes Back, trimmed from an original 631-question manuscript.
blurb: A trivia book compiled by then-preteen fan Rusty Miller, testing readers on minutiae from the first two Star Wars films. Begun as a personal project when Miller was eleven years old and eventually whittled down from over 600 questions to 425, it stands as a snapshot of how much (and how little) was publicly known about the saga before the prequels or expanded universe existed.
trivia: Rusty Miller began compiling the questions in summer 1981 at age eleven; his mother helped him submit the manuscript to Del Rey, which requested a full manuscript after seeing his growing list of trivia questions.

title: Once Upon a Galaxy: A Journal of the Making of The Empire Strikes Back
creator: Alan Arnold
notes: Published by Ballantine/Del Rey, 1980. A 277-page day-by-day production diary including 32 pages of black-and-white behind-the-scenes photos, covering location shoots in Norway (Hoth sequences) and England along with California studio work.
blurb: Alan Arnold's behind-the-scenes production diary chronicling the making of The Empire Strikes Back, written from his vantage point as the film's on-set unit publicist. Covering the Norway and England shoots along with studio work in California, it mixes day-by-day observations with candid interviews from Mark Hamill, Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher, and George Lucas.
trivia: Arnold was Lucasfilm's on-set unit publicist during the Empire Strikes Back shoot, giving him direct access to cast and crew for the firsthand interviews and observations that fill the diary.

title: Star Wars: TIE Fighter — A Pocket Manual
creator: David West Reynolds
notes: Published by Running Press (October 7, 1998) as part of its Miniature Editions line, a companion volume to X-Wing: A Pocket Manual (also by Reynolds, same year/imprint). Framed as an in-universe Imperial training manual; includes three pop-up tactical diagrams and a 3-D fold-out TIE fighter plus photographic stills from the Special Edition trilogy.
blurb: A pop-up "technical manual" styled as an in-universe Imperial training booklet for TIE fighter pilots, complete with three-dimensional pop-up tactical diagrams and a fold-out TIE fighter in flight. Written by archaeologist-turned-Star-Wars-author David West Reynolds, it leans into propagandistic Imperial bluster for comedic and immersive effect, paired with photographic stills from the Special Edition trilogy.
rating: No reliable rating found specifically for this title
trivia: Reynolds is credited on the title page as "Captain David West Reynolds" to sustain the book's in-universe conceit, and he deliberately modeled its propagandistic tone on WWII-era training material to sell the Imperial perspective.

title: Star Wars: The Mandalorian — The Tiny Book of Grogu
creator: Insight Editions
notes: Published by Insight Editions, November 9, 2021, 192 pages, measuring 1.34" x 1.73". Part of Insight Editions' novelty "Tiny Books" line alongside The Tiny Book of Jedi and The Tiny Book of Sith. Classified as 'Other' format rather than Hardcover/Paperback since it is a miniature novelty item, not a standard-format reading book.
blurb: A pocket-sized novelty book from Insight Editions' "Tiny Books" line, packed with quotes and imagery celebrating Grogu's adventures across the first two seasons of The Mandalorian. Measuring under two inches tall, it's designed as a cute collectible or stocking-stuffer rather than a conventional reading book.
trivia: At 1.34" x 1.73", the book is physically smaller than most Grogu action figures, and reviewers note some interior images are dark and hard to see given the tiny page size.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic
creator: Henry Gilroy (writer); Scott Hepburn, Ramon Perez, Lucas Marangon (art); Dan Parsons (inks); Michael E. Wiggam (colors)
notes: Collects issues #1-6 (the 'Mystery of Kiros' arc) of the Dark Horse ongoing series Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008-2010), which ran alongside the animated show's early seasons. TPB released December 2, 2009. Loosely adapted years later into the Season 4 TV episodes 'Kidnapped,' 'Slaves of the Republic,' and 'Escape from Kadavo.'
blurb: When the Separatists 'evacuate' the Togruta colonists of Kiros for their own safety, Anakin Skywalker and Padawan Ahsoka Tano investigate and discover the missing colonists have been sold into slavery on Zygerria. Anakin poses as consort to the ruthless Slave Queen to rescue Ahsoka and free the captives, uncovering the horrors of the Zygerrian slave trade along the way. It's a darker, more mature story than most all-ages Clone Wars comics of its era.
trivia: Written by Henry Gilroy, the head writer for the first season of the animated Clone Wars series, making this comic arc an early example of a TV writer directly shaping tie-in comics before the material was eventually adapted back into the show itself.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Strange Allies
creator: Ryder Windham (writer); Ben Dewey (art); Mae Hao (colors); Stéphane Roux (cover)
notes: Standalone digest-sized graphic novella in Dark Horse's Clone Wars line (not a collected issue run). Released October 19, 2011. Ties into Ryder Windham's prose series Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Secret Missions, bringing the novel-exclusive 'Breakout Squad' characters into comic form.
blurb: With Jedi Generals stretched thin across the galaxy, masterless Padawan Nuru Kungurama, his clone squad, and a hulking swoop-biker ally named Gizz are assigned a routine protection detail that spirals into a mystery massacre, a hijacked freighter, and the kidnapping of a group of orphaned younglings. Nuru must rely on unconventional help to see the mission through.
trivia: The story spotlights characters originating in Ryder Windham's Clone Wars: Secret Missions novels rather than the animated show's core cast, making it a rare comic crossover from a prose sub-series.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Deadly Hands of Shon-Ju
creator: Jeremy Barlow (writer); Brian Koschak (art); Ronda Pattison (colors)
notes: Standalone original graphic novel in Dark Horse's digest-sized Clone Wars line, not a collection of separate single issues. Published December 1, 2010 (80 pages).
blurb: Behind enemy lines, Jedi Knight Aayla Secura's covert mission to capture a Separatist warlord is complicated by Shon-Ju, a fallen former Padawan turned cult leader who is hunting the same target for his own vengeful reasons. Aayla must decide whether to trust a dangerous former Jedi to complete her mission.
trivia: Wookieepedia dates the story to 21 BBY, placing it between the comic stories 'Duchess of Mandalore' and 'Corruption' in the Clone Wars Legends timeline.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Wind Raiders of Taloraan
creator: John Ostrander (writer); Wayne Lo (art)
notes: Standalone digest-sized graphic novella in Dark Horse's Clone Wars line. Published May 27, 2009 (96 pages), aimed at younger readers per the publisher's own description.
blurb: Jedi Knights Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, with Padawan Ahsoka Tano in tow, travel to the wind-swept world of Taloraan hoping to win the Republic new allies. Neither of the planet's ruling factions is eager to cooperate, and when Ahsoka uncovers a Separatist plot, she must win over the fierce, beast-riding Wind Raiders to save her companions.
trivia: Written by veteran Star Wars comics writer John Ostrander (Star Wars: Republic, Star Wars: Legacy), who brought his signature political intrigue to this younger-reader-focused entry.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: In Service of the Republic
creator: Henry Gilroy, Steven Melching (writers); Scott Hepburn, Ramon Perez (art); Dan Parsons (inks); Michael E. Wiggam (colors)
notes: Collects issues #7-9 of the Dark Horse ongoing Star Wars: The Clone Wars series (2008-2010). TPB released June 16, 2010.
blurb: On the storm-wracked world of Khorm, the Republic's air superiority is grounded, forcing Jedi Masters Kit Fisto and Plo Koon to plan a daring ground assault on a Separatist mountain fortress alongside a squad of elite Republic commandos. Complicating matters is a glory-hungry young officer and the sudden arrival of the assassin Asajj Ventress, who ambushes Plo Koon and leaves him badly wounded.
trivia: This arc introduces Captain Kendal Ozzel in his younger years as a Republic officer, decades before the vain, overconfident admiral would famously fail Darth Vader aboard the Executor in The Empire Strikes Back.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Volume 1
creator: W. Haden Blackman (writer); Ben Caldwell, Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach (art)
notes: Digest-sized all-ages collection tying into the 2003-2005 Genndy Tartakovsky Star Wars: Clone Wars micro-series on Cartoon Network. Collects three done-in-one stories: 'Blind Force,' 'Heavy Metal Jedi,' and 'Fierce Currents.' Published July 2004 (96 pages).
blurb: Three bite-sized adventures in the style of the Cartoon Network micro-series: Obi-Wan and Anakin battle the dreaded Shadowmen in total darkness on the night-world of Nivek; Mace Windu and Saesee Tiin clash over tactics while grinding through waves of battle droids; and Kit Fisto leads his surviving clone troopers into a new threat on the flooded surface of Mon Calamari.
trivia: This was the first volume of Dark Horse's long-running Clone Wars Adventures digest line, which would ultimately stretch to ten volumes between 2004 and 2007, each anthologizing quick, single-issue stories in the visual style of the animated micro-series.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Volume 2
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Welles Hartley (writers); Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach (art)
notes: Digest-sized all-ages collection tying into the 2003-2005 Clone Wars micro-series. Collects three stories: 'Skywalkers,' 'Hide in Plain Sight,' and 'Run Mace Run.' Published November 2004 (96 pages).
blurb: Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker play a deadly game of cat-and-mouse against Separatist fighters in a treacherous asteroid ring; Luminara Unduli and her Padawan Barriss Offee race to evacuate farming villagers before General Grievous's droid army overruns them; and Mace Windu finds himself in a tight scrape of his own on the front lines.
trivia: This volume is one of the higher-rated entries in the Clone Wars Adventures digest line on Goodreads, helped by the introduction of the fan-favorite Luminara/Barriss teacher-student dynamic before it was more fully explored in the animated series.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Volume 3
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Ryan Kaufman (writers); Thomas Andrews, Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach (art)
notes: Digest-sized all-ages collection tying into the 2003-2005 Clone Wars micro-series. Collects four stories: 'Rogue's Gallery,' 'The Package,' 'A Stranger in Town,' and 'One Battle.' Published March 2005 (96 pages).
blurb: This volume widens its lens beyond the marquee Jedi to spotlight the everyday grunts of the war: put-upon clone troopers on the front lines, a tense escort mission, and the scheming of Count Dooku and General Grievous as they probe the Republic for weaknesses. A quick, kid-friendly snapshot of the Clone Wars from multiple points of view.
trivia: Volume 3 was among the first Clone Wars Adventures issues to give substantial page time to ordinary clone troopers rather than focusing almost exclusively on named Jedi characters.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 4
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Ryan Kaufman, Justin Lambros, Fillbach Brothers (writers); Rick Lacy, Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach (artists)
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four original stories: 'Another Fine Mess' (R2-D2 and C-3PO foil a plot against Padme), 'The Brink' (Anakin Skywalker rescues Jedi Serra Keto aboard an infested space station), 'Orders' (a clone commando squad and an orphaned boy, ending at Order 66), and 'Descent' (Chewbacca and the Wookiees defend Kashyyyk). 96 pages, 5 1/4" x 7 1/2". Published Oct. 26, 2005. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-402-9.
blurb: Four bite-sized tales set as the Clone Wars rage toward their end. R2-D2 and C-3PO stumble into a plot against Senator Padme Amidala, Anakin Skywalker rescues a fellow Jedi from a nightmare aboard a derelict space station, a clone commando squad gives an orphaned boy a harsh lesson in duty, and Chewbacca leads the Wookiees in a desperate defense of Kashyyyk. Told in the stripped-down, high-energy visual style of the Cartoon Network micro-series.
trivia: One of the first post-Revenge of the Sith Clone Wars Adventures issues to explore Order 66 from the clone troopers' point of view, years before Karen Traviss's Republic Commando novels made that perspective a franchise staple.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 5
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Ryan Kaufman, Justin Lambros, Fillbach Brothers (writers); Rick Lacy, Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach (artists)
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four stories: Jedi Aayla Secura saves an Ewok village from a monstrous threat, a clone commander sees firsthand what the Separatists will sacrifice for their cause, Senator Bail Organa infiltrates enemy territory to rescue a friend, and Padawan Joc Sah is caught in the crossfire of Order 66. 96 pages. Published April 26, 2006. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-483-8.
blurb: Jedi Aayla Secura ventures into a dark forest to save a besieged Ewok village, a clone commander witnesses the lengths the Separatists will go to for their cause, Senator Bail Organa mounts a covert rescue mission, and young Padawan Joc Sah finds himself caught in the chaos of Order 66. Another quartet of fast-paced, all-ages Clone Wars stories drawn in the show's iconic angular style.
trivia: Gives Bail Organa a rare starring role in the all-ages Clone Wars Adventures line, going undercover on a rescue mission years before his better-known appearances in Revenge of the Sith and Star Wars Rebels.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 6
creator: W. Haden Blackman, Mike Kennedy, Fillbach Brothers, and others (writers); Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, Stewart McKenny, and others (artists)
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four stories: Saesee Tiin steals a secret Separatist starfighter, Ki-Adi-Mundi and Rivi-Anu rescue a stranded army of clone troopers, a squad of clone commandos battles through the clouds of a gas giant, and Plo Koon and Kit Fisto are trapped in an underwater prison. 96 pages. Published Aug. 16, 2006. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-567-5. Dark Horse noted over 100,000 copies of the series in print by this point.
blurb: Jedi Master Saesee Tiin steals a Separatist starfighter, Ki-Adi-Mundi and Rivi-Anu race to rescue a stranded army of clone troopers, a squad of clone commandos battles through the clouds of a gas giant, and Plo Koon and Kit Fisto must escape an underwater prison. Four more adrenaline-charged, all-ages adventures set during the twilight of the Jedi Order.
trivia: The cover depicts Saesee Tiin wielding a green lightsaber, but inside the included story 'It Takes a Thief' his blade is actually blue -- a continuity slip Wookieepedia calls out explicitly.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 7
creator: Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, Chris Avellone, Ethen Beavers, and others
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four stories: Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker are attacked by giant monsters, Padme Amidala becomes a spy, Jedi Bultar Swan storms an impenetrable fortress, and three friends rob a bank guarded by an army of clones. 80 pages. Published Jan. 31, 2007. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-678-8.
blurb: Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker are ambushed by monstrous creatures, Padme Amidala goes undercover as a spy, Jedi Knight Bultar Swan storms a fortified stronghold, and a trio of unlikely friends attempt to rob a bank guarded by an army of clones. A fast, action-first collection capturing the Republic-versus-Confederacy conflict at its most explosive.
trivia: One of the few Clone Wars Adventures issues to put Padme Amidala in an active espionage role rather than a purely political or damsel-in-distress part.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 8
creator: Matt Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, and various writers/artists
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four stories: a malfunctioning battle droid tries to escape its fate on the battlefield, bounty hunter Aurra Sing comes face-to-face with her deadly past, and Obi-Wan Kenobi becomes entangled in a nefarious espionage plot, among other Republic-vs-Separatist tales. 80 pages. Published June 20, 2007. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-680-1.
blurb: A malfunctioning battle droid tries to outrun its fate on the battlefield, bounty hunter Aurra Sing comes face to face with a ghost from her past, and Obi-Wan Kenobi gets tangled up in a dangerous espionage plot. Four more scrappy, all-ages tales of Republic-versus-Separatist warfare.
trivia: Features one of bounty hunter Aurra Sing's rare all-ages comic appearances, fleshing out her Legends backstory outside the more mature Republic and Boba Fett comic lines.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 9
creator: Matthew Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, and various writers/artists
notes: Dark Horse all-ages digest TPB collecting four stories: Dexter Jettster braves the wilds of Dractu, a clone trooper becomes a scavenger's cargo, Quinlan Vos battles through the sewers of Coruscant, and Mace Windu discovers a lost city. 80 pages. Published Oct. 31, 2007. ISBN-13 978-1-59307-832-4.
blurb: Dexter Jettster braves the wilds of a remote world, a lone clone trooper becomes a scavenger's unwilling cargo, bounty-hunter-turned-Jedi Quinlan Vos fights through the sewers beneath Coruscant, and Mace Windu stumbles onto a lost city. Four more pulse-pounding, all-ages Clone Wars vignettes.
trivia: Gives Quinlan Vos -- later a central figure in the 2015 novel Dark Disciple -- one of his only appearances in the kid-friendly Clone Wars Adventures format.

title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures, Vol. 10
creator: Matthew Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, Chris Avellone, Jason Hall (writers); Matthew Fillbach, Shawn Fillbach, Stewart McKenny, Ethan Beavers (artists)
notes: Final volume of the 10-volume Dark Horse digest series. Collects four stories: Separatists ambush the farms of Dantooine, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker race a junked speeder through a canyon of bounty hunters, Aayla Secura and Ki-Adi-Mundi assign a young Jedi a top-secret mission, and a lone clone trooper battles an army of droids. 80 pages. Published Dec. 19, 2007.
blurb: In the final volume of the series, Separatist forces ambush the peaceful farms of Dantooine, Obi-Wan and Anakin race a beat-up speeder through a canyon crawling with bounty hunters, Aayla Secura and Ki-Adi-Mundi send a young Jedi on a secret mission, and a single clone trooper makes a last stand against an army of droids. A fitting send-off for Dark Horse's all-ages Clone Wars Adventures line.
trivia: Series editor Jeremy Barlow said at the time this would be 'the last one for a while,' since Dark Horse was still deciding how to handle comics tie-ins for the upcoming CGI Clone Wars series that launched in 2008; the digest line never resumed in this format.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest: Path to Truth
creator: Jude Watson
notes: VERIFIED CONTENTS: 'Path to Truth' is the unnumbered introductory novel of the 11-book Jedi Quest series -- it is NOT a 3-in-1 omnibus of 'The Way of the Apprentice,' 'The Trail of the Jedi,' and 'The Dangerous Games' as initially suspected from the cover. Those are separate, individually numbered paperbacks (Books 1-3) released in 2002. This hardcover, with dust jacket reading 'Anakin's Story Between Episode I and Episode II,' is a stand-alone single-story volume: Anakin builds his first lightsaber on Ilum and joins Obi-Wan on a mission tied to his slave past on Tatooine. US hardcover, Scholastic, Sept. 2001. ISBN-13 978-0-439-24204-2.
blurb: Almost thirteen years old, Anakin Skywalker journeys to the ice caves of Ilum to build his first lightsaber, confronting old fears in the process. He and Master Obi-Wan Kenobi are then sent on a mission that reopens deep wounds from Anakin's slave days on Tatooine, after learning that the crime lord Krayn -- who once kidnapped and killed slaves for profit -- has resurfaced and grown more dangerous than ever. Obi-Wan must keep Anakin's simmering anger from tipping into vengeance as their hunt for Krayn threatens galactic peace.
trivia: Despite reading as a complete, self-contained story, Path to Truth is technically the unnumbered prologue volume of the Jedi Quest series; the formally numbered entries begin with Book 1, The Way of the Apprentice, released the following year.
inUniverseDate: ~28 BBY (between The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #1: The Rising Force
creator: Dave Wolverton
notes: Cataloging correction: this specific volume was written by Dave Wolverton (later known as David Farland), NOT Jude Watson — it is the only book in the 20-volume Jedi Apprentice series not written by Watson, who took over starting with book #2. Published by Scholastic, May 1999. Series overseer/creator credit for the franchise is often loosely attributed to Watson given she wrote the vast majority of entries.
blurb: Thirteen-year-old Obi-Wan Kenobi is on the verge of being sent to the Agricultural Corps, having grown too old to be chosen as a Padawan, when Qui-Gon Jinn reluctantly takes him on a final mission to the mining world of Bandomeer. Clashing personalities and a conspiracy among the planet's miners force the two to learn to trust one another. It's the story that sets the entire Qui-Gon/Obi-Wan partnership in motion.
trivia: Dave Wolverton wrote this launch title before handing the series to Jude Watson for all subsequent entries; Wolverton later found greater fame writing fantasy under the pen name David Farland.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #2: The Dark Rival
creator: Jude Watson
notes: First Jedi Apprentice book written by Jude Watson, who authored the remainder of the series. Published by Scholastic, 1999.
blurb: Qui-Gon and his new Padawan remain on Bandomeer to mediate a dispute between rival mining companies, but the mission is a trap set by Xanatos, Qui-Gon's former apprentice who fell to the dark side. As old wounds resurface, Obi-Wan must prove himself trustworthy while the bond between master and student begins to grow.
trivia: This book properly introduces Xanatos, Qui-Gon's fallen first apprentice, who becomes the series' recurring antagonist for its first several volumes.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #3: The Hidden Past
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Published by Scholastic, 1999. Begins a two-book arc on the planet Gala that concludes in book #4.
blurb: Sent by Master Yoda on what seems like a dull assignment to observe elections on the planet Gala, Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan are hijacked en route to Phindar, ruled by the sinister Syndicat, which erases the memories of its enemies and sells them into slavery. The two Jedi throw in with local freedom fighters and uncover a conspiracy reaching back to Gala's own royal family.
trivia: The Phindan Syndicat's mind-wiping slavery operation is one of the darker premises in the early, otherwise fairly light-hearted run of the series.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #4: The Mark of the Crown
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Published by Scholastic, October 1999. Concludes the Gala arc begun in The Hidden Past.
blurb: Arriving on Gala as neutral observers for the planet's first elections, Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan find themselves entangled in a succession crisis: the dying queen's ambitious son will do anything to hold power, even as rumors swirl of another heir bearing the fabled Mark of the Crown. The two Jedi must keep the peace as a hidden power struggle turns deadly.
trivia: The book directly follows on from The Hidden Past's cliffhanger involving Gala's royal succession and the Syndicat conspiracy.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #5: The Defenders of the Dead
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Published by Scholastic Press, December 1999. Introduces Jedi Knight Tahl and begins the pivotal Melida/Daan arc that concludes in book #6.
blurb: Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan travel to war-ravaged Melida/Daan to rescue Jedi Knight Tahl, who was attempting to broker peace in a decades-long civil war. Obi-Wan is drawn to Cerasi and Nield, teenage leaders of a rebel faction called the Young who are fighting to end the fighting for good, and finds his loyalty to the Jedi Code tested like never before.
trivia: This is the emotional turning point of the early series: it ends with Obi-Wan handing Qui-Gon his lightsaber and choosing to stay behind and fight alongside the Young, effectively leaving the Jedi Order.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #6: The Uncertain Path
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Published by Scholastic, February 2000. Direct continuation of The Defenders of the Dead, resolving the Melida/Daan arc.
blurb: Having left the Jedi Order, Obi-Wan discovers that winning peace on Melida/Daan is far harder than winning the war, as the Young struggle to govern amid renewed factional tension. Meanwhile Qui-Gon, back at the Temple and stung by his apprentice's departure, is drawn into investigating a string of mysterious thefts alongside Tahl, all while wondering whether taking on Obi-Wan was ever the right choice.
trivia: The story picks up mere weeks after The Defenders of the Dead and resolves whether Obi-Wan returns to the Jedi Order, closing out the series' first major character arc.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #1: The Way of the Apprentice
creator: Jude Watson
notes: First numbered volume of the Jedi Quest series (preceded by the unnumbered Path to Truth, 2001). Published by Scholastic; reached #9 on the New York Times Children's Paperback Books bestseller list in June 2002.
blurb: Three years into his apprenticeship, fourteen-year-old Anakin Skywalker joins Obi-Wan and three other Master-Padawan teams on a mission to the plague-stricken world of Radnor. When the group is split apart, Anakin must overcome his rivalry with fellow Padawan Ferus Olin and set aside his pride to keep everyone alive and uncover a deeper conspiracy behind the outbreak.
trivia: This book introduces the recurring Jedi Quest supporting cast — Ferus Olin, Siri Tachi, Tru Veld, and Darra Thel-Tanis — who reappear throughout the eleven-book series.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #2: The Trail of the Jedi
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Published by Scholastic, 2002, as a 128-page paperback.
blurb: Obi-Wan sets up a survival and tracking exercise for Anakin on the icy world of Ragoon 6, but the training mission turns deadly when a squad of bounty hunters hired by the mysterious Granta Omega ambushes them. Master and apprentice must survive the wilderness and each other's doubts while uncovering who wants them dead.
trivia: This story introduces Granta Omega, who becomes the primary antagonist of the entire Jedi Quest series and is later revealed to be the son of the fallen Jedi Xanatos.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #3: The Dangerous Games
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 3 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series. Cover/interior art credited to Alicia Buelow and David Mattingly. Also released as an audiobook (Listening Library, narrated by Jonathan Davis).
blurb: Sent to the Galactic Games as Jedi peacekeepers, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker uncover an illegal underground Podracing circuit hidden beneath the sanctioned events. For Anakin, the races are an uncomfortable echo of his slave days on Tatooine, testing his self-control and pulling at old temptations. As Master and apprentice dig deeper, they find corruption that could turn the games deadly for everyone involved.
trivia: The story deliberately echoes Anakin's Podracing scenes from The Phantom Menace, giving young readers a direct throughline between the film and the novel continuity.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #4: The Master of Disguise
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 4 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, first published November 2002. Audiobook edition narrated by Jonathan Davis for Listening Library.
blurb: Obi-Wan and Anakin find themselves stranded on a hostile world while hunting Granta Omega, a wealthy, ruthless enemy of the Republic who proves as elusive as he is dangerous. Omega's resources and cunning let him slip through every trap the Jedi set, and his schemes threaten to push vulnerable systems toward the dark side. Master and apprentice must outthink a foe who always seems to be one step ahead of them.
trivia: This entry deepens Granta Omega's role as the Jedi Quest series' central recurring antagonist, a vendetta against Obi-Wan and Anakin that carries through several later books.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #5: The School of Fear
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 5 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, released February 1, 2003.
blurb: When a senator's son vanishes, Obi-Wan sends Anakin undercover into an elite, high-pressure leadership academy to investigate. There Anakin is forced to work alongside his rival Ferus Olin, and the two uncover a secret society of renegade students operating beneath the school's rigid surface. Anakin must master his own fears and temper if he hopes to crack the mystery.
trivia: The School of Fear formally establishes Ferus Olin as Anakin's rival Padawan, a rivalry that becomes a throughline for the remainder of the Jedi Quest series.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #6: The Shadow Trap
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 6 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, released May 2003. Illustrated by Alicia Buelow and David Mattingly.
blurb: Sent to broker peace on the war-ravaged planet Mawan, Obi-Wan and Anakin discover the mission is a trap laid by Granta Omega using a biological weapon against the Jedi and the planet's desperate population. In the chaos, a senior member of the Jedi Council sacrifices herself to save Anakin, leaving him wracked with guilt. It stands as one of the most consequential losses in the series.
trivia: This novel provides the Legends-continuity explanation for Jedi Master Yaddle's disappearance between The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones, killing her off in the line of duty.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #7: The Moment of Truth
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 7 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, released November 2003.
blurb: Still shaken by the tragedy on Mawan, Anakin and Obi-Wan struggle to reconnect as guilt and doubt strain their bond. When a rescue mission to the last free planet in the Uziel system goes wrong, the two are separated, and their unresolved tension threatens the mission's success. Both Master and apprentice are forced to confront what kind of team they want to be.
trivia: Fans frequently point to The Moment of Truth as the emotional low point of the Obi-Wan/Anakin partnership in the Jedi Quest series, foreshadowing tensions explored later in the Clone Wars era.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #8: The Changing of the Guard
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 8 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, released March 1, 2004.
blurb: Obi-Wan, Anakin, Siri Tachi, and Ferus Olin go undercover as criminals to infiltrate Romin, a lawless refuge for the galaxy's worst, in pursuit of the ruthless scientist Jenna Zan Arbor. Posing as thieves forces Anakin to walk an uncomfortably thin line between duty and deception. The mission raises hard questions about how far the Jedi can bend their own principles to catch a criminal mastermind.
trivia: The book pairs two Master/Padawan teams on the same undercover assignment, letting the series directly contrast Anakin's and Ferus Olin's very different approaches to bending the rules.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #9: The False Peace
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 9 of 10 in the original Jedi Quest series, released July 1, 2004.
blurb: Granta Omega and Jenna Zan Arbor join forces in a plot to destroy the Republic Senate itself, forcing Obi-Wan to confront an old enemy while Anakin, Siri, and Ferus race to stop the attack. Under pressure, Anakin bends the rules he has sworn to follow, straining his standing with the Jedi Order. The uneasy alliance of villains raises the stakes higher than any previous mission in the series.
trivia: The False Peace brings together the series' two major recurring antagonists, Granta Omega and Jenna Zan Arbor, for a single combined threat against the Senate.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Quest #10: The Final Showdown
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Scholastic Paperbacks young-reader novel; book 10 of 10, closing out the original Jedi Quest series in 2004.
blurb: The hunt for Granta Omega and Jenna Zan Arbor leads Obi-Wan, Anakin, and Ferus to the ancient Sith world of Korriban, where visions of the dark side linger among the ruins. A bitter rivalry between Anakin and Ferus, newly fast-tracked toward Knighthood, spirals into tragedy with lasting consequences for both Padawans. Obi-Wan is left to face Omega alone amid the ruins of a Sith temple.
trivia: The Final Showdown closes the original 10-book Jedi Quest run by having Ferus Olin leave the Jedi Order, a plot thread Jude Watson later revisited in her Coruscant Nights and Last of the Jedi series.

title: Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith (Junior Novelization)
creator: Patricia C. Wrede
notes: Young-reader adaptation (ages ~9-12) of the film, based on the screenplay by George Lucas; published by Scholastic in May 2005, ahead of the movie's theatrical release. Distinct from Matthew Stover's adult novelization of the same film. Softens some of the darkest beats (e.g. Mace Windu's death, the execution of Order 66) for younger readers. One of three junior novelizations Wrede wrote covering the entire prequel trilogy.
blurb: As the Clone Wars rage across the galaxy, Anakin Skywalker is torn between his duty to the Jedi Order and a growing fear of losing the people he loves. When Chancellor Palpatine offers a path to power the Jedi refuse to teach, Anakin faces the choice that will define the rest of his life. This young-reader retelling follows the fall of the Jedi and the birth of Darth Vader through the eyes of the film's key characters.
trivia: Because it was published before the film opened in theaters, some young readers learned Anakin's fate and the details of Order 66 from this book before ever seeing Revenge of the Sith on screen.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Escape
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Prelude novella to the series' six-book main sequence; originally released in the UK (Egmont, Feb 25 2016) as a low-cost World Book Day title before being folded into the series as its formal opening entry. US eBook edition followed via Disney-Lucasfilm Press in Dec 2016. Noticeably shorter than the full-length books that follow.
blurb: While mapping the unknown reaches of Wild Space with their parents, siblings Milo and Lina Graf watch their lives upend when Imperial agents led by Captain Korda abduct their mother and father. With only their cantankerous droid CR-8R for help, the children must escape capture themselves and begin the desperate search that drives the rest of the series.
trivia: As a UK World Book Day tie-in, The Escape was originally sold as a short, inexpensive introduction to the series rather than a standard full-length novel.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Snare
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: First full-length entry in the six-book main sequence, following prelude novella The Escape. UK edition by Egmont (2016); US edition published by Disney-Lucasfilm Press Jan 3, 2017.
blurb: Having narrowly escaped Imperial custody, Milo and Lina Graf set out across Wild Space to rescue their kidnapped parents, following the trail left by their captor, Captain Korda. Fast-paced chases and narrow escapes test the siblings' courage as they learn to rely on each other, their droid CR-8R, and their own wits against the Empire.
trivia: The Snare established the series' brisk, twelve-chapter structure, packing a spaceship crash, a tense standoff, and a speeder/boat chase into one short book.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Nest
creator: Tom Huddleston
notes: Second full-length entry in the main sequence. UK edition by Egmont (2016); US edition published by Disney-Lucasfilm Press Jan 3, 2017.
blurb: Milo and Lina Graf trace a new clue to a remote jungle world, where a terrifying beast lurks amid the ruins. As the children close in on their parents' trail, they also intercept a mysterious transmission calling for revolt against the Empire, an early spark of the rebellion to come.
trivia: The intercepted rebel broadcast in The Nest is one of several subtle nods in the series toward the wider anti-Imperial resistance later depicted in Star Wars Rebels.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Rescue
creator: Tom Huddleston
notes: Sixth and final full-length entry (seventh overall counting the prelude, The Escape), closing the Graf family's story arc. UK Egmont edition May 4, 2017; US Disney-Lucasfilm Press edition April 10, 2018.
blurb: Milo and Lina Graf have finally tracked their parents to a secret Imperial base hidden deep in Wild Space. With a full legion of stormtroopers standing between them and freedom, the siblings must use everything they've learned on their journey for one last, desperate rescue attempt.
trivia: As the finale of the series, The Rescue arrived more than a year after The Escape kicked off the story in early 2016, closing out one of the longer-running Star Wars young-reader series of its era.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Dark
creator: Tom Huddleston
notes: Fourth full-length entry, ~160 pages. UK Egmont edition (titled The Dark) released June 30, 2016; the US Disney-Lucasfilm Press edition was retitled The Darkness (Aug 15, 2017). This physical copy uses the original UK title, The Dark.
blurb: Adrift aboard a damaged starship spiraling toward disaster, Milo and Lina Graf find themselves trapped with a dangerous criminal while an Imperial patrol closes in. Something even more sinister waits in the ship's shadows, forcing the siblings to confront real fear on their search for their parents.
rating: No reliable aggregate rating found for the UK 'The Dark' edition specifically
trivia: Fans and reviewers frequently single out The Dark as a series highlight for leaning into genuine horror-style tension rather than the lighter adventure tone of earlier entries.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Steal
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Third full-length entry, ~160 pages. UK Egmont edition (titled The Steal) released June 30, 2016; the US Disney-Lucasfilm Press edition was retitled The Heist (April 11, 2017). This physical copy uses the original UK title, The Steal.
blurb: Still hunting for their kidnapped parents, Milo and Lina Graf travel to Lothal seeking an ally who can help them. When something precious is stolen from the siblings, they're forced into their most dangerous mission yet just to keep their search alive.
trivia: The Steal's Lothal setting ties the series to the same planet later made famous by Star Wars Rebels, reinforcing where Adventures in Wild Space sits on the wider timeline.

title: Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space: The Cold
creator: Cavan Scott
notes: Fifth full-length entry, ~160 pages. UK Egmont edition released March 9, 2017; US Disney-Lucasfilm Press edition released October 24, 2017.
blurb: Milo and Lina Graf have finally picked up their parents' trail, until an ambush strands them on a desolate ice planet deep in Wild Space. With an old enemy returning for revenge, the siblings must survive the frozen wilderness before they can continue their search.
trivia: The Cold brings back a returning antagonist from earlier in the series, sharpening Milo and Lina's personal stakes as the story heads toward its final book.

title: Star Wars Rebels: The Rebellion Begins
creator: Michael Kogge
notes: Junior novel (middle-grade chapter book) adapting the Star Wars Rebels pilot movie 'Spark of Rebellion' and the show's earliest episodes. Includes an 8-page color photo insert from the animated series. Part of the Star Wars Rebels chapter-book line distinct from the Servants of the Empire series.
blurb: On the Outer Rim world of Lothal, teenage thief Ezra Bridger scrapes by under the Empire's shadow until he crosses paths with a small band of rebels aboard the starship Ghost. Drawn into their orbit by Kanan Jarrus and Hera Syndulla, Ezra gets swept up in a daring mission to free enslaved Wookiees from an Imperial transport. Along the way he begins to discover there is more to himself, and to the fight against tyranny, than he ever expected.
trivia: Author Michael Kogge is a frequent Lucasfilm collaborator who also wrote several other Star Wars Rebels tie-in books; this novelization was released alongside the show's October 2014 television premiere.

title: Star Wars: Servants of the Empire, Book 1: Edge of the Galaxy
creator: Jason Fry
notes: First entry in the four-book Servants of the Empire young-readers series, written concurrently with and tying into Star Wars Rebels Season 1. Developed with input from Lucasfilm Story Group and Rebels executive producer Greg Weisman.
blurb: On Lothal, Zare Leonis watches his sister Dhara achieve her dream of entering the Imperial Academy, even as Zare himself grows increasingly uneasy about the Empire's true intentions for their homeworld. When strange happenings at the Academy raise his suspicions, Zare begins quietly digging for answers. His search puts him on a collision course with the Empire he's been raised to serve.
trivia: The series was plotted to run parallel to Zare Leonis's appearances on Star Wars Rebels, letting Jason Fry invent the character's backstory before his on-screen debut.

title: Star Wars: Servants of the Empire, Book 2: Rebel in the Ranks
creator: Jason Fry
notes: Second entry in the Servants of the Empire series; continues directly from Edge of the Galaxy as Zare enrolls at the Lothal Imperial Academy as a cadet.
blurb: Determined to learn the truth behind his sister Dhara's disappearance, Zare Leonis enlists as a cadet at the Imperial Academy on Lothal, playing the part of a loyal recruit while secretly searching for answers. Outside the Academy walls, his girlfriend Merei Spanjaf uses her hacking skills to dig through Imperial data systems. Together they begin to uncover the edges of a hidden Imperial program connected to Dhara's fate.
trivia: The book was released on March 3, 2015, and marked Zare's shift from bystander to active double agent within the Imperial military.

title: Star Wars: Servants of the Empire, Book 3: Imperial Justice
creator: Jason Fry
notes: Third entry in the Servants of the Empire series, set in the aftermath of a rebel strike on the Lothal Imperial Academy depicted in Star Wars Rebels.
blurb: Following a rebel attack on the Imperial Academy, Zare Leonis pushes deeper into his cadet training while the conspiracy surrounding Project Harvester grows harder to ignore. As Zare's investigation widens, he begins to see the Empire's reach and ruthlessness extend far beyond Lothal. Every step closer to the truth puts his cover, and his life, at greater risk.
trivia: Released July 7, 2015, this installment expands the scope of the Project Harvester conspiracy first hinted at in Rebel in the Ranks.

title: Star Wars: Servants of the Empire, Book 4: The Secret Academy
creator: Jason Fry
notes: Fourth and final entry in the Servants of the Empire series, bringing Zare Leonis's arc to a close and folding him into the crew of the Ghost.
blurb: With the help of an ally and the rebel crew known as the Spectres, Zare Leonis mounts a final push to rescue his sister Dhara from the secretive Imperial installation known as Area Null. What he finds there reveals the true, dangerous nature of the program that took her, and forces Zare to choose a side once and for all.
trivia: Released October 6, 2015, this finale reveals Dhara Leonis to be Force-sensitive, tying the series into the broader mysteries explored on Star Wars Rebels.

title: Star Wars: A New Hope (Junior Novelization)
creator: Ryder Windham
notes: This is the young-reader junior novelization by Ryder Windham, not the standard adult novelization. This printing is the 2017 40th-anniversary edition with the minimalist black cover, lightsaber/starburst art, and 'Star Wars 40' anniversary branding, released as part of a matching junior-novelization set for the original trilogy. Research across multiple retailer and library listings (Egmont/Disney-Lucasfilm Press editions) consistently describes this printing as a paperback (roughly 200-210 pages), not a hardcover as initially assumed for cataloging -- physical binding should be double-checked against the actual copy in hand in case a hardcover variant exists.
blurb: On the desert world of Tatooine, farm boy Luke Skywalker's life changes forever when two droids carrying a secret message fall into his hands. Guided by the reclusive Ben Kenobi, Luke is pulled into a galaxy-spanning rebellion against the Empire, alongside smuggler Han Solo, Chewbacca, and the captured Princess Leia. As the Rebel Alliance races against the Empire's ultimate weapon, Luke discovers a power in himself he never knew existed.
trivia: This junior novelization was first published in 2004 and later revised to align with Disney's post-2014 canon; the 2017 printing reissued it in a matching black cover design across the trilogy to mark the 40th anniversary of A New Hope's theatrical release.

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Junior Novelization)
creator: Ryder Windham
notes: Young-reader junior novelization by Ryder Windham (not the standard adult novelization), matching the black-cover 40th-anniversary junior-novelization set. Verified across multiple listings (e.g., 9781405285438, 224 pages) as a paperback edition rather than a hardcover -- worth confirming physical binding against the actual shelf copy.
blurb: After the Empire tracks the Rebel Alliance to its icy hideout on Hoth, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, Princess Leia, and their companions scatter across the galaxy to survive. While Luke travels to the swamp world of Dagobah to begin Jedi training under the diminutive Master Yoda, Han and Leia are pursued by bounty hunters into the clouds of Bespin. A shocking confrontation with Darth Vader will change Luke's understanding of himself, and of the war he's fighting, forever.
trivia: Like its A New Hope counterpart, this junior novelization dates back to a 2004 original release and was revised for Disney's new canon before being reissued in the matching 2017 anniversary paperback set.

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (Junior Novelization)
creator: Ryder Windham
notes: Young-reader junior novelization by Ryder Windham (not the standard adult novelization), matching the black-cover 40th-anniversary junior-novelization set for the original trilogy. Verified across multiple listings (e.g., 9781405285445, ~188-224 pages) as a paperback edition rather than a hardcover -- worth confirming physical binding against the actual shelf copy.
blurb: With Han Solo frozen and in the clutches of Jabba the Hutt, Luke Skywalker and his allies mount a daring rescue before turning their attention to a far greater threat: the Empire's second Death Star. As the Rebel fleet prepares for a final assault and Luke completes his Jedi training, he must confront Darth Vader and the Emperor themselves, gambling everything on the hope that good still remains in his fallen father.
trivia: This is the third volume of Windham's matching 40th-anniversary junior novelization set; like the other two, its text was originally published in 2004 and updated for current Disney canon before this 2017 reissue.

title: Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel
creator: Matt Forbeck
notes: Junior novelization of the 2016 film Rogue One: A Star Wars Story. Originally released as an eBook by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on December 16, 2016; the US hardcover edition followed on March 28, 2017 (ISBN 9781484705094) and includes eight bonus pages of color photos from the film. A separate UK Egmont paperback also exists. Not to be confused with the all-ages novelization of the same film written by Alexander Freed.
blurb: Jyn Erso, a reluctant recruit with a rebellious streak, is pulled into a desperate Rebel mission to steal the plans for the Empire's ultimate weapon, the Death Star. Teaming with intelligence officer Cassian Andor, the reprogrammed Imperial droid K-2SO, and a small band of unlikely allies, she must infiltrate a heavily fortified Imperial data vault on Scarif. Their success or failure sets the stage for the opening moments of the original 1977 Star Wars film.
trivia: The junior novelization's eBook edition actually reached readers before the film itself premiered in December 2016, giving young fans an early preview of the story.

title: Star Wars: The Weapon of a Jedi: A Luke Skywalker Adventure
series: Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: Jason Fry
notes: Part of the 'Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens' publishing initiative timed to the 2015 film's release. Originally published in US hardcover by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on September 4, 2015 (ISBN 9781484724965); UK Egmont paperback edition (ISBN 9781405277860) released the same year. Illustrated by Phil Noto.
blurb: Stranded on the remote planet Devaron while awaiting rendezvous with the Rebel fleet, Luke Skywalker uses the downtime to begin teaching himself the ways of the Force, guided only by Obi-Wan Kenobi's old journal. His quiet self-training is interrupted when he's drawn into a local conflict and squares off against a mysterious, Force-sensitive rival. It's an early, tentative step on Luke's path toward becoming a Jedi Knight.
trivia: This was one of three character-focused 'Journey to The Force Awakens' novels released simultaneously on September 4, 2015 alongside Smuggler's Run and Moving Target, all illustrated by artist Phil Noto in a shared visual style.

title: Star Wars: Smuggler's Run: A Han Solo & Chewbacca Adventure
series: Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: Greg Rucka
notes: Part of the 'Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens' publishing initiative. Originally published in US hardcover by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on September 4, 2015; UK Egmont paperback edition released the same year (192 pages). Illustrated by Phil Noto; audiobook narrated by Marc Thompson.
blurb: Fresh off their reward for the destruction of the first Death Star, Han Solo and Chewbacca are recruited by Princess Leia for a secret mission: extract a hunted Rebel operative from the crime-ridden planet Cyrkon aboard the Millennium Falcon. Evading ruthless bounty hunters and a relentless Imperial agent, the pair find that collecting on old debts is a lot more complicated than they'd hoped. Set immediately after A New Hope, the story hints at threads that would echo years later in The Force Awakens.
trivia: A promotional animated comic adaptation of the story was produced for a Nestle cereal marketing tie-in, accessible via digital codes printed on cereal boxes.

title: Star Wars: Moving Target: A Princess Leia Adventure
series: Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens
creator: Cecil Castellucci and Jason Fry
notes: Part of the 'Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens' publishing initiative. Originally published in US hardcover by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on September 4, 2015 (240 pages); UK Egmont paperback edition (ISBN 9781405277877) released the same year. Illustrated by Phil Noto. Framed as a story Leia recounts shortly before the events of The Force Awakens; Star Wars: Timelines dates the core mission to 4 ABY.
blurb: Set between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, Princess Leia leads a small, ragtag crew on a decoy mission across several worlds to distract the Empire from the massing Rebel fleet before the Battle of Endor. Framed as a story Leia recounts to General Organa's aide years later, the tale explores the personal cost of leadership and the sacrifices made to keep the Rebellion's most wanted target one step ahead of the Empire.
trivia: The novel bookends its main story with framing scenes set shortly before The Force Awakens, tying an Original Trilogy-era adventure directly into the then-upcoming sequel film.

title: Star Wars: Before the Awakening
creator: Greg Rucka
notes: A companion anthology to the 'Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens' character novels, though not formally numbered within that line. Published by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on December 18, 2015 (US hardcover, 216 pages); UK Egmont paperback edition released the same day (224 pages). Illustrated by Phil Noto. New York Times bestseller. Contains three linked short stories, one each for Finn, Rey, and Poe Dameron.
blurb: Three stories set in the months before The Force Awakens reveal the paths that brought Finn, Rey, and Poe Dameron to the fateful events on Jakku. Finn undergoes brutal First Order stormtrooper training and begins to question his orders; Rey discovers a derelict starship in the Jakku desert that could change her fortunes; and Poe Dameron leaves the New Republic military to join Leia Organa's fledgling Resistance. Each tale deepens the backstory of a hero audiences had just met on the big screen.
trivia: Poe's story is dated roughly three years before The Force Awakens (around 31 ABY), while Finn's and Rey's stories take place immediately before the film in 34 ABY, meaning the book's three sections don't all take place at the same time.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Book of the Film
creator: Lucasfilm Press (adaptation; no individual author credited)
notes: UK Egmont Books illustrated retelling of the 2015 film for young readers (ISBN 9781405283939, ~192-198 pages), published January 2016. Distinct from both Alan Dean Foster's full adult novelization (Del Rey) and Michael Kogge's 'A Junior Novel' adaptation (Disney-Lucasfilm Press) -- this photo/illustration-heavy volume condenses the film's story for younger readers. No individual credited author was found in available records; listings attribute it simply to Lucasfilm.
blurb: A scavenger named Rey, a defecting stormtrooper called Finn, and ace Resistance pilot Poe Dameron are thrown together when a map holding the key to finding the missing Luke Skywalker falls into their hands. Pursued across the galaxy by the sinister First Order and the masked Kylo Ren, they find unexpected help from smuggler Han Solo and Chewbacca aboard the legendary Millennium Falcon. This illustrated retelling recaps the film's story for younger readers with photos and artwork from the movie.
trivia: This is one of several parallel Force Awakens book adaptations released for different reading levels in 2015-2016, ranging from Alan Dean Foster's full novelization down to picture-book retellings -- 'Book of the Film' sits in the middle as an illustrated young-reader edition.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi: A Junior Novel
creator: Michael Kogge
notes: Junior novelization of the 2017 film, published by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on March 6, 2018 (ISBN 9781368012287). Includes an eight-page full-color photo insert and several deleted/extended and exclusive scenes not in the theatrical cut. A UK Egmont edition also exists (ISBN 9781405289221). Audiobook narrated by Jessica Almasy.
blurb: With the Resistance on the run from the First Order's relentless fleet, Rey seeks out the self-exiled Luke Skywalker on a remote ocean planet, hoping he'll help turn the tide of the war. Meanwhile Finn and new mechanic Rose Tico attempt a risky mission to disable the First Order's tracking device, while General Leia Organa and Poe Dameron clash over how to save the dwindling Resistance fleet. This young-reader adaptation retells the film's events with a handful of extra character moments.
trivia: Michael Kogge also wrote the junior novelizations for both The Force Awakens and The Rise of Skywalker, making him the author behind all three sequel-trilogy junior novels.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Cobalt Squadron
creator: Elizabeth Wein
notes: Part of the 'Journey to Star Wars: The Last Jedi' publishing line, released alongside the companion novel The Last Jedi: Bomber Command by Jason Fry on the same day. Published by Disney-Lucasfilm Press on December 15, 2017 (hardcover, 251 pages) with a simultaneous Egmont paperback (256 pages). Illustrated by Phil Noto; audiobook narrated by Kelly Marie Tran, who plays Rose Tico onscreen.
blurb: Sisters Rose and Paige Tico fled their home system after the First Order devastated their world, and now serve the Resistance together -- Paige as a bomber gunner in Cobalt Squadron, Rose as the mechanic who keeps their ships flying. When Cobalt Squadron is sent on a dangerous mission to save civilians from a First Order attack, the sisters' bond and courage are put to the test. The story leads directly into the evacuation of the Resistance base on D'Qar seen in The Last Jedi.
trivia: The audiobook is narrated by actress Kelly Marie Tran, who portrays Rose Tico in the film itself, giving listeners a performance straight from the character's onscreen voice.

title: Star Wars: Spark of the Resistance
series: Journey to Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
creator: Justina Ireland
notes: Junior/middle-grade novel, illustrated by Phil Noto; part of the four-title 'Journey to Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker' publishing initiative released ahead of Episode IX.
blurb: Rey, Poe Dameron, Rose Tico, and BB-8 divert from a Resistance supply run to answer a distress call on the planet Minfar, home to the peaceful Zixon people. Though badly outnumbered, the group vows to defend the Zixon from an encroaching First Order battalion. Along the way they must survive terrifying flying creatures and a mysterious superweapon that could tip the balance of the war.
trivia: Published October 4, 2019, it was one of four 'Journey to The Rise of Skywalker' tie-in novels released alongside a middle-grade line meant to bridge The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy of Fear, Book 1: Eaten Alive (Limited Collector's Edition)
creator: John Whitman
notes: This copy is the promotional 'Limited Collector's Edition' printing featuring a lenticular/holographic cover: tilted one way it shows a friendly alien face with an open hand, tilted the other it reveals the same creature baring rows of razor teeth and a long tongue. Bantam Skylark, first book of the 12-volume series.
blurb: Orphaned siblings Tash and Zak Arranda, survivors of Alderaan's destruction, travel the galaxy with their shape-shifting Shi'ido uncle Hoole aboard the starship Lightrunner. On the resource-rich world of D'vouran they cross paths with Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Princess Leia, but soon discover townsfolk are mysteriously vanishing without a trace. As the disappearances mount, the Arrandas uncover a horror lurking beneath the planet's welcoming surface.
trivia: Galaxy of Fear was explicitly modeled on R.L. Stine's Goosebumps, and this early Bantam Skylark printing used a lenticular hologram cover gimmick as a one-time collector's promotion, making it a sought-after variant among Legends-era collectors today.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy of Fear, Book 2: City of the Dead (Limited Collector's Edition)
creator: John Whitman
notes: This copy is the promotional 'Limited Collector's Edition' printing with a holographic/lenticular cover, matching the variant produced for Book 1. Bantam Skylark, second book of the 12-volume series.
blurb: After the loss of their ship the Lightrunner, Tash, Zak, and their uncle Hoole stop on the planet Necropolis to find new transport. Zak sneaks into the planet's eerie cemetery at midnight to prove himself to new friends, only to stumble onto the secret underground lab of the deranged Dr. Evazan, who is using stolen corpses to build an army of the reanimated dead. The Arrandas must stop the plot before Necropolis is overrun.
trivia: Like Book 1, this Limited Collector's Edition printing used a lenticular hologram cover as a short-lived promotional gimmick, and copies in good condition are now prized by Galaxy of Fear collectors.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy of Fear, Book 5: Ghost of the Jedi
creator: John Whitman
notes: Fifth entry in the 12-book Galaxy of Fear series (John Whitman), published by Bantam Skylark.
blurb: Fleeing the sinister Imperial scientist Borborygmus Gog, Tash, Zak, and Hoole take refuge on Nespis 8, an abandoned space station rumored to house a cursed, haunted Jedi library. Guided by a mysterious HoloNet contact called 'Forceflow,' Tash begins to uncover her own Force sensitivity with help from the ghost of a long-dead Jedi, Aidan Bok. She soon learns Forceflow is actually Gog himself, luring her into a device designed to drain her life essence.
trivia: This installment is the first to reveal Tash Arranda's latent Force sensitivity, a plot thread that becomes central to the remainder of the series.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy of Fear, Book 6: Army of Terror
creator: John Whitman
notes: Sixth entry in the 12-book Galaxy of Fear series (John Whitman), published by Bantam Skylark.
blurb: Determined to confirm that Borborygmus Gog's twisted bioweapon program, Project Starscream, has truly been destroyed, Tash, Zak, and Hoole travel to the barren Outer Rim world of Kiva. There they find Gog's laboratory abandoned but discover a spectral army born from his experiments, and rescue an infant, Eppon, caught up in the horror. Han Solo, Leia, Chewbacca, Luke Skywalker, and C-3PO all lend a hand against the shape-shifting, fear-feeding creatures.
trivia: The Army of Terror creatures were designed to be immune to the Force, one of the few Legends-era antagonist forces explicitly written to sidestep Jedi abilities entirely.

title: Star Wars Joke Book
creator: Lucasfilm Press
notes: Illustrated humor/activity book compiling Star Wars-themed jokes, riddles, and puns, framed as being 'hosted' by Salacious B. Crumb in Jabba's Palace. UK edition published by Egmont Publishing under license from Lucasfilm; US editions credited to Disney-Lucasfilm Press. Exact printing/edition of this copy not independently confirmed.
blurb: A kid-friendly gag book packed with puns, one-liners, and riddles spanning the Star Wars saga, narrated in-universe by Jabba the Hutt's cackling court jester Salacious B. Crumb. Pages are illustrated with cartoon-style art of familiar characters delivering the jokes.
trivia: The book uses Salacious B. Crumb, Jabba the Hutt's cackling monkey-lizard jester from Return of the Jedi, as its in-universe joke-book host.

title: Star Wars Crochet
creator: Lucy Collin
notes: Originally released as part of a boxed 'Crochet Kits' set (Running Press) that included yarn, a hook, needle, stuffing, and safety eyes alongside the pattern book; this catalog entry covers the instructional paperback itself.
blurb: A step-by-step amigurumi crochet pattern guide for twelve classic Star Wars characters from the original trilogy, including Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, Princess Leia, Yoda, R2-D2, and Jabba the Hutt. Each project includes full-color photos and beginner-friendly instructions for building your own yarn versions of the galaxy's most iconic figures.
trivia: Author Lucy Collin went on to write two follow-up volumes, Star Wars Even More Crochet and Star Wars: The Mandalorian Crochet, extending the pattern library to prequel- and Mandalorian-era characters.

title: Star Wars Mad Libs: World's Greatest Word Game
creator: Roger Price and Leonard Stern
notes: Fill-in-the-blank word game book applying the classic Mad Libs format to Star Wars saga scenes and characters; published by Mad Libs/Price Stern Sloan.
blurb: A fill-in-the-blank party word game featuring stories built around Star Wars characters, planets, and moments from the saga. Players supply nouns, verbs, and adjectives without seeing the story, then read the often-absurd results aloud.
trivia: Mad Libs was invented by Roger Price and Leonard Stern in 1958; this Star Wars edition, first published September 1, 2008, is one of many licensed tie-in volumes the long-running format has spawned.

title: Star Wars Expert Guide
creator: DK Publishing
notes: UK Tesco-exclusive release; compiles content previously published across earlier DK guides (Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary, Beware the Sith, Battles for the Galaxy, Mysteries of the Jedi). Credited Lucasfilm Story Group adviser Leland Chee later said he had not vetted the book, so its contents are generally treated as Legends.
blurb: A fact-packed DK reference guide covering Jedi and Sith, Rebels and Imperials, clones and stormtroopers, lightsabers, vehicles and droids, aimed at giving young fans a broad overview of the Star Wars galaxy with new material added for The Force Awakens.
trivia: Although marketed as an official guide, the book's own listed Story Group consultant Leland Chee said he had never seen it prior to release, raising questions among fans about how much of its content should be treated as authoritative.

title: Star Wars: How Not to Get Eaten by Ewoks and Other Galactic Survival Skills
creator: Christian Blauvelt (DK Publishing)
notes: 128 pages. Written as an in-universe survival manual for the Star Wars galaxy, with flowcharts, creature size comparisons, and tongue-in-cheek advice drawn from the films and animated shows.
blurb: A tongue-in-cheek, in-universe survival guide to staying alive in the Star Wars galaxy, covering hostile environments, dangerous creatures and megafauna, social and cultural pitfalls, and what to do if you've already been eaten by something enormous.
trivia: Author Christian Blauvelt wrote this book alongside the similarly styled Be More Leia, and several reviewers have noted the two share the same dry, in-universe comic voice.

title: Star Wars: Be More Leia: Find Your Rebel Voice and Fight the System
creator: Christian Blauvelt (DK Publishing)
notes: 64 pages. Part of DK's illustrated inspirational/lifestyle tie-in line, pairing film stills and quotes from Leia, Rey, Padme, Yoda, Obi-Wan, Jyn and others with real-world advice on leadership and rebellion.
blurb: A humorous mini self-help book that repackages Princess Leia's most defiant moments -- along with wisdom from Rey, Padme, Yoda, and other heroes -- into witty, real-world advice about confidence, leadership, and fighting the system.
trivia: Published in 2019, the same year Leia made her final on-screen appearance in The Rise of Skywalker, several reviewers read the book as an affectionate tribute to actress Carrie Fisher.

title: Star Wars: 99 Stormtroopers Join the Empire
creator: Greg Stones (Chronicle Books)
notes: 96 pages, published as part of the 'Star Wars x Chronicle Books' line. A darkly comic illustrated countdown book, not an official in-universe or continuity-specific reference.
blurb: Ninety-nine stormtroopers join the Empire, and then, one by one, meet increasingly absurd and unfortunate ends -- underestimating a princess, interrupting Vader's meditation, mouthing off to Jabba -- in this colorfully illustrated dark-comedy countdown for grown-up fans.
trivia: Illustrator Greg Stones is best known for his 'Cute Will Save the World' art series, and reviewers frequently compared this book to Edward Gorey's morbid alphabet book The Gashlycrumb Tinies.

title: LEGO Star Wars Phonics Boxed Set: Pack 1
creator: Quinlan B. Lee (Scholastic, in partnership with LEGO/Lucasfilm)
notes: Boxed set of 10 leveled phonics readers plus 2 workbooks, packaged in a sturdy carrying box with plastic handle (ISBN 9780545908825). Focuses on short and long vowel sounds using LEGO Star Wars minifigure characters; the first LEGO Star Wars phonics box set Scholastic produced.
blurb: An early-reader phonics program starring LEGO versions of Han Solo, Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, Yoda and other Star Wars characters, using ten short storybooks and two companion workbooks to teach beginning readers core vowel sounds.
trivia: This was the first entry in Scholastic's LEGO Star Wars phonics line, which was later followed by additional boxed packs aimed at the same beginning-reader age group.

title: The Star Wars Craft Book
creator: Bonnie Burton (Del Rey / Random House)
notes: 176 pages. Contains over 40 DIY projects across five chapters: Playtime, Home Decor, Holiday Crafts, Nature and Science Crafts, and Star Wars Style. Goodreads shelves the title under its 'Star Wars - Legends' continuity marker.
blurb: A fully illustrated, step-by-step craft guide packed with more than forty original Star Wars-themed DIY projects, from Chewbacca sock puppets and an AT-AT herb garden to Ewok fleece hats and a crocheted R2-D2 beanie.
