trivia: Author Bonnie Burton hosted hands-on crafting demonstrations at Star Wars conventions and later applied the same DIY approach to other franchises with her book Crafting with Feminism.

title: The Ultimate Star Wars Quiz Book: Over 1,000 Questions to Test Your Star Wars Knowledge!
creator: Paddy Kempshall (Studio Press / Walt Disney)
notes: Organized into 24 categories split across three difficulty levels, spanning the prequel, original, and sequel trilogies plus The Clone Wars, The Bad Batch, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Andor, The Mandalorian, The Book of Boba Fett and more. Exact print format inferred from typical Studio Press quiz-book releases.
blurb: A bumper trivia collection with over 1,000 questions split into 24 themed categories and three difficulty tiers, testing everything from classic-trilogy lore to the latest Disney+ Star Wars series.
trivia: Author Paddy Kempshall is a Star Wars Celebration stage host and podcaster, and structured the book's questions into beginner, intermediate, and expert tiers so fans of any experience level could take part.

title: Star Wars: Smuggler's Starship Activity Book and Model: Make Your Own Millennium Falcon
creator: Craig Jelley / Insight Editions
notes: 36 pages. Includes mazes, codewords and puzzles alongside press-out pieces to build a mini paper Millennium Falcon model. Originally published in the UK by Egmont in 2016 as part of the Star Wars Construction Books line; this US edition was released by Insight Editions in 2020. Multiple retitled editions exist across territories.
blurb: A hybrid activity book and papercraft kit that pairs Star Wars-themed mazes, puzzles, and codeword games with press-out pieces for building your own miniature Millennium Falcon model.
trivia: The title has been reprinted under at least three different names and editions across different publishers and years, including a UK Egmont edition and a US Studio Fun International edition called Star Wars Build Your Own: Millennium Falcon.

title: Star Wars: The Original Topps Trading Card Series, Volume One
series: The Original Topps Trading Card Series
creator: Abrams ComicArts / The Topps Company (text by Gary Gerani, afterword by Robert V. Conte)
notes: Deluxe reprint of the complete original 1977-1978 Topps Star Wars trading card series (5 sets: blue, red, yellow, orange, green). Reproduces fronts and backs of all 330 cards and 55 stickers, plus the rare Wonder Bread cards, with 4 exclusive bonus cards tipped into the back. Dust jacket mimics the waxy wrapper of the original card packs; cover art depicts the gum stick with C-3PO featured prominently on front cover art. First in the Abrams Topps trilogy (Vol. 1 ANH, Vol. 2 ESB, Vol. 3 ROTJ).
blurb: This deluxe hardcover reprints, in full color and full size, every card and sticker from Topps' legendary 1977-78 Star Wars trading card series - the very images that let a generation relive the movie before home video existed. Original Topps editor Gary Gerani supplies commentary on the production quirks and infamous mistakes (including the notorious green-series C-3PO error card), while collector Robert V. Conte contributes an afterword on the ultra-rare Wonder Bread cards. Four newly created bonus cards round out this nostalgia-soaked collector's volume.
trivia: The book's dust jacket is manufactured from the same waxy paper stock used for the original 1977 card wax packs, and the hardcover boards underneath depict the included stick of bubblegum - whole on the front, shattered on the back - just as kids found it in real packs.

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back: The Original Topps Trading Card Series, Volume Two
series: The Original Topps Trading Card Series
creator: Abrams ComicArts / The Topps Company (text by Gary Gerani)
notes: Deluxe reprint of Topps' 1980 Empire Strikes Back trading card series (3 sets). Reproduces fronts and backs of all 352 cards and 88 stickers, plus the Giant Photo Card series, rare promotional images, and 4 bonus cards. Cover art prominently features Darth Vader. Second volume in the Abrams Topps trilogy.
blurb: The second entry in Abrams' Topps reprint trilogy collects every card and sticker Topps issued for The Empire Strikes Back in 1980, reproduced front and back at high fidelity. Gary Gerani, the original Topps editor, returns with commentary on the production process, plus rare promotional photo cards not widely seen since their original release. A must for anyone who chased these bubblegum-scented cards as a kid in 1980.
trivia: Because Empire's card production ran more smoothly than the original film's rushed 1977 licensing scramble, Gerani's commentary notes there are markedly fewer behind-the-scenes anecdotes and errors to point out than in Volume One.

title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi: The Original Topps Trading Card Series, Volume Three
series: The Original Topps Trading Card Series
creator: Abrams ComicArts / The Topps Company (text by Gary Gerani)
notes: Deluxe reprint of Topps' 1983 Return of the Jedi trading card series (2 sets). Reproduces fronts and backs of all 220 cards and 55 stickers, plus 4 bonus cards and rare promotional images. Cover art features an Ewok. Final volume in the Abrams Topps trilogy, published by Abrams ComicArts.
blurb: Closing out the Abrams/Topps trilogy, this volume reprints every card and sticker from the two 1983 Return of the Jedi trading card series in full, front and back, alongside Gary Gerani's commentary as the line's original editor. Character profiles, puzzle-back cards, and movie trivia from the trilogy's finale are all preserved here, plus four newly minted bonus cards for collectors.
trivia: Return of the Jedi's Topps line was the smallest of the original trilogy at just two series (220 cards and 55 stickers total), reflecting a smaller card program compared to the five-series blitz for the original 1977 film.

title: Star Wars: The Lightsaber Collection
creator: Insight Editions (Daniel Wallace, with illustrators Ryan Valle and Lukasz Liszko)
notes: Research could not confirm a physical box set of lightsaber replica pens/props under this title; the verified, currently-sold Insight Editions product with this exact name is a 156-page illustrated hardcover reference guide ($34.99, ISBN 9781683839781) covering movie, animated-series, comics, and game lightsaber hilts. Format adjusted from 'Other' to 'Hardcover' to match verified product; flag for owner to confirm against the physical item on the shelf in case it is a different/unlisted pen gift set.
blurb: A lavishly illustrated coffee-table guide surveying dozens of lightsaber hilts from across the Star Wars saga, The Clone Wars, Rebels, comics, and games. Each spread offers a detailed painted illustration of a single hilt alongside in-universe construction notes and behind-the-scenes anecdotes from the films' prop designers. A visually striking must-have for fans fascinated by the franchise's signature weapon.
trivia: Author Daniel Wallace also wrote the influential in-universe reference book The Jedi Path, and here treats each lightsaber hilt almost like an artifact catalog entry, complete with technical construction details.

title: Star Wars: The High Republic: The Lightsaber Collection
creator: Insight Editions (Daniel Wallace, with illustrators Lukasz Liszko and Ryan Valle)
notes: Research could not confirm a physical box set of lightsaber replica pens/props under this title; the verified, currently-sold Insight Editions product is a 156-page illustrated hardcover reference guide ($34.99, ISBN 9798886630848) covering 50+ High Republic-era lightsaber hilts. Format adjusted from 'Other' to 'Hardcover' to match verified product; flag for owner to confirm against the physical item on the shelf in case it is a different/unlisted pen gift set. Follow-up volume to the 2020 Lightsaber Collection.
blurb: A companion volume to the original Lightsaber Collection, this guide dives into the Jedi's golden age, showcasing more than 50 lightsabers from the High Republic era - including Vernestra Rwoh's lightwhip, Stellan Gios' ornate crossguard hilt, and Burryaga's broadsword-like weapon. Many designs appear here in fully painted, photo-real illustration for the first time, drawn from the High Republic's novels, comics, and other media.
trivia: Several hilts depicted in this book, sourced from High Republic novels and comics, had never before been given official visual designs - the artists had to invent their look from textual descriptions alone.

title: Star Wars: 11 Iconic Scenes from a Galaxy Far, Far Away... (A Scanimation Book)
creator: Workman Publishing (Rufus Butler Seder)
notes: Novelty picture book using Seder's patented Scanimation illusion process (striped lenticular-style overlay on scrambled art) to animate movie moments when the page is moved. Covers scenes from the original trilogy and prequel trilogy. New York Times bestseller list appearance per publisher/retailer copy. ISBN 9780761158462.
blurb: A picture book that brings 11 classic Star Wars moments to life using Scanimation, Rufus Butler Seder's patented optical-illusion technique: move the page up and down and the Millennium Falcon zooms, Yoda's lightsaber twirls, and Luke and Vader duel in looping animation. Equal parts toy and keepsake, it distills the saga's most iconic imagery - from Tauntaun rides to Death Star escapes - into a hands-on format for fans of all ages.
trivia: Inventor Rufus Butler Seder originally developed the underlying Scanimation/Lifetiles technology for large-scale glass-tile murals that appear to move as a viewer walks past them, before adapting the process into a line of bestselling novelty books.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #9: The Fight for Truth
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #9 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: When a family on the isolated world of Kegan reports a possible Force-sensitive child, Qui-Gon Jinn and Adi Gallia travel there with their Padawans, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Siri Tachi. The planet's leaders resist outside contact, and Obi-Wan and Siri are taken and placed in an indoctrination school where independent thought is forbidden. Qui-Gon and Adi must uncover the truth behind Kegan's isolationist "General Good" philosophy before it costs the Jedi everything.
trivia: The Kegan storyline, with its stark isolationist "General Good" ideology and thought-control school, pushes into more mature, philosophical territory than earlier entries — several reviewers note it reads older than the rest of the series.
inUniverseDate: ~44 BBY, several months after the Jedi Temple attack (Obi-Wan Kenobi is 13)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #7: The Captive Temple
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #7 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: Freshly reinstated as Qui-Gon Jinn's Padawan, Obi-Wan Kenobi finds the Jedi Temple itself under siege after an assassination attempt on Master Yoda. As unrest and suspicion spread through the Temple halls, Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan race to unmask the saboteur before the Temple's very foundations are destroyed. Old enemies and new betrayals collide in a mystery that strikes at the heart of the Jedi Order.
trivia: Wookieepedia highlights the book as a goldmine of Jedi Temple worldbuilding, detailing its ductwork and underwater tunnel systems that fans still cite when mapping the Temple's interior layout.
inUniverseDate: ~44 BBY, within the continuous ~4-month arc spanning Books 1-8

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #12: The Evil Experiment
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #12 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess. Note: Wikipedia lists this title's original publication year as 2001, one year later than several of the earlier books in this batch.
blurb: With Qui-Gon Jinn held captive by the ruthless scientist Jenna Zan Arbor, a masterless Obi-Wan Kenobi must rely on everything Qui-Gon has taught him to track his mentor down. Alongside his friend Astri, Obi-Wan races against time both to find Qui-Gon and to secure a rare cure for Astri's ailing father. Meanwhile, Qui-Gon endures Zan Arbor's chilling experiments, his Jedi calm tested to its limit.
trivia: This book directly continues the cliffhanger ending of The Deadly Hunter, forming the middle chapter of a three-book Jenna Zan Arbor arc that concludes in The Dangerous Rescue.
inUniverseDate: ~43 BBY, immediately following The Deadly Hunter (Obi-Wan Kenobi is 14)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #10: The Shattered Peace
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #10 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: A centuries-old peace treaty between the planet Rutan and its moon Senali is unraveling after the exchanged heir, Prince Leed, refuses to return home. Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are sent to mediate before Leed's furious father drags both worlds into war. As kidnappings and political maneuvering escalate, the two Jedi must uncover who truly wants this fragile peace destroyed.
trivia: The paperback cover art reuses a digitally altered photo of Loje Nella, a Jabba's Palace alien from Return of the Jedi, standing in for a Rutanian/Senali character despite not matching either species' described appearance.

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #13: The Dangerous Rescue
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #13 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: Qui-Gon Jinn has been rescued from Jenna Zan Arbor's clutches, but the scientist has escaped with another Jedi prisoner clinging to life. Obi-Wan Kenobi, Siri Tachi, and Adi Gallia pursue leads across multiple worlds, clashing with the vengeful bounty hunter Ona Nobis and uncovering a deadly bioweapon plot on the planet Belasco. It's a race against time to stop Zan Arbor before her schemes claim more victims.
trivia: This closes out the three-book Zan Arbor arc (Books 11-13); fan reviews frequently single it out as a satisfying finale with an unusually large ensemble of Jedi working together on one mission.
inUniverseDate: ~43 BBY, immediately following The Evil Experiment (Obi-Wan Kenobi is 14)

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #8: The Day of Reckoning
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #8 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi track the fugitive Xanatos to his home planet of Telos, only to be framed for a capital crime and hunted as fugitives themselves. With help from a con man tied to an outlawed environmental movement, the two Jedi uncover Xanatos's corrupt mining scheme before facing him in one final, decisive confrontation. This book brings Xanatos's arc, and the opening chapter of the series, to its climax.
trivia: Per Wookieepedia, this book closes out a continuous eight-book storyline (Books 1-8) that Watson wrote to unfold across roughly four in-universe months, before the series shifted to more standalone-style adventures.
inUniverseDate: ~44 BBY, at the close of the continuous ~4-month arc spanning Books 1-8

title: Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice #11: The Deadly Hunter
creator: Jude Watson
notes: Book number #11 confirmed via Wookieepedia and Wikipedia's official Jedi Apprentice bibliography, matching your original guess.
blurb: Around the time of Obi-Wan Kenobi's fourteenth birthday, Qui-Gon Jinn's old friend Didi Oddo becomes the target of a mysterious, shapeshifting bounty hunter. As Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan dig into the case, they uncover ties to the renowned and sinister scientist Jenna Zan Arbor.
